title: Status line reports when the ccreport checkout is behind origin
description:
The status line should print a line under the cost-window line when the local ccreport checkout is behind GitHub's master.

Target render, under `24H $14/$417 · 7D $154/$1963 · 30D $154/$10259 · AT $154/$12587`:

    ↑ 12 commits behind · git pull

Decisions taken with the user (2026-08-12):

- No tags, no GitHub releases, no PyPI. master is the release; `version` in pyproject.toml stays a placeholder nobody reads. The unit of 'update available' is a commit.
- The remote state comes from the GitHub REST API, not from git. No fetch, nothing written into the user's .git, and it works when the checkout has no usable remote credentials.
- The check runs twice a day (12 h TTL), from a detached process on the slow render path, never inline. A network call on the render path is the one thing the status line's whole design avoids.

The endpoint is the compare API, which answers ancestry and count in one request:

    GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{local_sha}...master

It returns `status` (behind | ahead | identical | diverged) and `ahead_by`. `status == 'ahead'` means master is ahead of the local commit by `ahead_by` commits, which is the number to render. Unauthenticated the API allows 60 requests per hour per IP; this spends 2 per day.

Children carry the work. Nothing here is implemented yet.
closed_reason: Shipped: check, spawn, render and docs

title: update_check.py: ask GitHub how far master is ahead of the local commit
description:
New module `src/ccreport/update_check.py`, run as a detached subprocess (`python3 -m ccreport.update_check`), never imported by a render.

What it does, in order:

1. Find the checkout root from its own location: `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`. If there is no `.git` directory there, exit 0 and write nothing — the user installed with `uv tool install .` and has no checkout to update.
2. Read the local HEAD SHA. Prefer parsing `.git/HEAD` plus the ref file (and `.git/packed-refs` as fallback) over forking git, so the same helper can serve the render path.
3. Derive owner/repo from `git remote get-url origin` — do not hardcode oroddlokken/ccreport, a fork has its own. Accept both `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` and `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`.
4. GET `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{local_sha}...master` with urllib, `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`, timeout 10 s. Follow the pattern already in `src/ccreport/exchange.py:131`.
5. Write to the `meta` table (`src/ccreport/cache_db.py:55`, helpers `_get_meta` at :3067 and `_set_meta` at :3091): the local SHA it compared, the commits-ahead count, and the epoch stamp of the check.

Failure is silence. A 404 (the local commit is not on GitHub — an unpushed commit, which is the normal state for whoever develops this), a network error, a rate-limit 403, a body that does not parse: write the stamp so the 12 h TTL still advances, write no count, exit 0. Nothing this module does may ever surface as an error on a render.

Storing the local SHA alongside the count is what keeps the render honest: if the user pulls, the render sees its own SHA no longer matches the compared one and suppresses the line until the next check, rather than claiming a stale 'behind'.

Acceptance: tests under `tests/` covering the SSH and HTTPS remote-URL forms, the loose-ref and packed-refs HEAD reads, a mocked 'ahead' response writing the count, and each failure mode writing the stamp but no count.
closed_reason: update_check.py added; 38 tests pass

title: Spawn the update check from the slow render path on a 12 h TTL
description:
Wire `ccreport.update_check` into `src/ccreport/statusline.py` so it runs twice a day and costs a render nothing.

Follow `_spawn_usage_refresh` at `src/ccreport/statusline.py:659`: `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)` with stdout and stderr to DEVNULL, so it outlives the render that started it.

Gate:

- Slow renders only. The fast path (`FAST_TTL_S`, 15 s, `_Fetched`) must not spawn it, and must not re-read the meta row — the rendered segment belongs in the fast cache next to the other rendered segments.
- Spawn only when `now - update_checked_at >= 43200` (12 h). Put the constant beside the other TTLs, not inline.
- The stamp is written by the child even on failure, so a repo with no network spawns one process per 12 h, not one per render.

Acceptance: a test asserting no spawn when the stamp is fresh, one spawn when it is 12 h old, and none at all on a fast-path render.
closed_reason: Detached spawn on a 12 h stamp, slow path only

title: Render the commits-behind line under the cost windows
description:
A new status line segment, on its own line directly under the cost-window line.

Placement: in the line assembly at `src/ccreport/statusline.py:1977-2003`, after `usage_cost` is appended and before the last line (`account`, battery, elapsed). It goes in both the wide and narrow branches — a two-word line does not need the width test the session segment gets.

Content: the count from `meta`, plus what to do about it. Render only when all three hold — the stored count is above zero, the stored local SHA equals the SHA read from `.git` right now, and the stamp is not older than about a day and a half (a check that has been failing for days should go quiet rather than repeat a number nobody can trust).

Toggle: `CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_UPDATE`, read through `_on` like every other segment, default on. Document it in the module docstring's env-var table, which is the list the README points at.

Reading the local SHA happens on the render path, so it is a file read of `.git/HEAD` and the ref file — no subprocess, no import that is not already loaded. Share the helper with `update_check.py` only if that costs the render nothing; a duplicated ten-line reader beats pulling a module onto the render path.

Acceptance: tests covering the line rendering at a count above zero, staying absent at zero, absent when the local SHA has moved on from the compared one, absent when the stamp is stale, and absent when the toggle is 0.
closed_reason: Line renders under the cost windows in both layouts

title: Document the update check in README and AGENTS.md
description:
Two places, both written for someone who has not read the code.

README: a short section saying master is the release — there are no tagged versions — and that the status line tells you when your checkout is behind, checked twice a day against GitHub's API, with `CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_UPDATE=0` to turn it off. Say plainly that it makes an unauthenticated request to api.github.com every 12 h and touches nothing in the user's .git, since a tool that phones home should say so where it is installed.

AGENTS.md: one bullet under 'Pipeline rules' covering what the next agent would otherwise get wrong — the check is a detached spawn on the slow path only, the count is trusted only while the stored SHA still matches HEAD, and the child writes its stamp even on failure so a broken network cannot turn into a spawn per render.

Acceptance: both files updated, and no line in either describing a tag, a release or a version number, since none exist.
closed_reason: README Updates section, AGENTS.md bullet, reference 5.7

title: Statusline: show the scoped model quota when a subagent used that model
description:
Today the per-model weekly quota segment (S/W/Fa in the rate-limit group) is gated on the *selected* model only. In statusline.py _render_rate_limits:

    sc_wanted = sc_mode == 'always' or (
        sc_mode == 'current' and sc_model.lower() in _ustr(usage, '_current_model').lower()
    )

_current_model is inp.model, the display name Claude Code sends on stdin. So a session running Opus that dispatched Fable subagents burns the Fable weekly quota while the Fable segment stays hidden until SCOPED_MODE=always.

Subagent traffic is logged in the session's own JSONL (verified: ~/.claude/projects/.../09a9e5e9-*.jsonl carries 89 claude-fable-5 and 112 claude-opus-5 assistant records), and pricing._find_session_files already includes the <session_id>/ subdirectory, so the models a session actually used are available from the same scan that computes the session cost.

Plan:
- pricing.py: _scan_session_file already gets the model from _line_cost; accumulate pricing.model_family(model) per scan. Carry the set on _SessionCostState, persist it in the state blob (_encode/_decode_session_state, bump _SESSION_STATE_VERSION so old blobs reparse once), merge it in _resume_session_cost, and derive it in _purged_session_cost from the cached records' model field. Expose it next to the cost without a second parse.
- statusline.py: carry the families on _Fetched (bump _FAST_CACHE_SCHEMA) and widen the SCOPED_MODE=current gate to model_family(sc_model) in those families.
- docs/calculation-reference.md section on the scoped segment (~line 790) and the CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_SCOPED_MODE help text in statusline.py describe 'current model' — update both.
acceptance: SCOPED_MODE=current shows the scoped segment when the session's JSONL contains any record whose model family matches scoped_model, even though the selected model is a different family; still hidden when no record of that family exists and the selected model differs; SCOPED_MODE=always and =off unchanged; the family set survives the incremental resume path (append to the log, next render keeps the earlier families); pytest tests cover the pricing accumulation, the resume path and the statusline gate; just lint-all and just test pass.
closed_reason: Scoped segment now matches the session's logged model families; verified live as Fa under Opus 5

title: Statusline: a fresh usage row starves the per-project cost summary
acceptance: A fresh usage row plus an expired cost summary spawns exactly one --costs-only refresh; a fresh summary spawns nothing; a live costs lock suppresses the spawn; an active API error backoff does not; HISTORIC_COST=0 spawns nothing. pytest covers each branch; just lint-all and just test pass.
closed_reason: Fresh-row path spawns --costs-only on an expired per-project summary; Fa cost renders again

title: ccreport update: report how far behind master the checkout is, --pull to fast-forward
description:
The status line already renders '↑ N commits behind · git pull' from update_check.py, but there is no way to ask for that answer from the CLI. Add a 'ccreport update' subcommand.

Behaviour:
- Runs the check live (update_check.checkout_root/local_head_sha/remote_slug/commits_behind) rather than reading cache_db.read_update_check(), because a CLI invocation is not a render and the user asked now. Store the fresh result via cache_db.write_update_check() so the status line's stamp and count are refreshed too.
- Prints one of: not a git checkout (installed as a package), up to date, N commit(s) behind plus the 'git pull' hint, or 'could not check' when the API/remote did not answer.
- With --pull, and only when behind > 0, runs 'git pull --ff-only' in the checkout and prints its outcome. Never a merge, never a rebase.
- Runs before the record-loading path in main(), like migrate/overrides/limits/adopt do: it needs no corpus and has no report to print.

Files: src/ccreport/ccreport.py (cmd_update + subparser + early dispatch), tests/test_ccreport.py or a new tests/test_update_command.py, docs/calculation-reference.md and AGENTS.md if the update-check paragraph needs it.
acceptance:
- 'ccreport update' prints the live behind-count and exits 0 in every outcome including a failed check.
- 'ccreport update --pull' fast-forwards only when behind > 0 and reports what git did.
- A checkout with no .git (installed package) prints that and does not call the API.
- pytest covers: up-to-date, behind, no-checkout, unanswered check, --pull when up to date, --pull when behind.
- just lint-all and just test pass.
notes:
Implemented: cmd_update + _pull_ff_only in src/ccreport/ccreport.py:1866-1936, subparser and early dispatch in main(), tests/test_update_command.py (17 tests), docs/calculation-reference.md §5.7 and AGENTS.md update-check bullet.

Verified: 'uv run ccreport update' printed 'Up to date with origin/master.' exit=0. just lint-all: ruff 'All checks passed!', pyright '0 errors, 0 warnings'. just test: 1084 passed.
closed_reason: Implemented and verified: ccreport update reports the live behind-count, --pull fast-forwards. 17 tests, lint-all and test suite pass.

title: Statusline update hint names 'git pull', which pulls the wrong repo
description:
statusline._render_update (src/ccreport/statusline.py:983) renders:

  ↑ 12 commits behind · git pull

The status line renders in whatever project the session is in, not in the ccreport checkout. Running 'git pull' where the hint appears pulls that project's repo, which is never what the line means. The command that works from any cwd is 'ccreport update --pull' (added in ccreport-19fl).

Replace the segment text with the user's wording:

  ↑ A newer version of ccreport is available, run 'ccreport update --pull' to update

The segment has its own line (statusline.py:2099), so the extra width costs no other segment. The count drops out of the rendered string; the three render gates (behind > 0, stamp under UPDATE_MAX_AGE_S, update_local_sha == HEAD) are unchanged.

Also carrying the old string: README.md:145, docs/calculation-reference.md (§5.7 area and the segment list near line 897), and whatever asserts it in tests/test_statusline.py.
acceptance:
- The rendered segment is the sentence above, still yellow, still its own line.
- The three render gates are unchanged: no number is implied when the check could not answer.
- README.md, docs/calculation-reference.md and tests/test_statusline.py carry the new string, none the old.
- just lint-all and just test pass.
notes: Done: statusline.py:983 renders "↑ A newer version of ccreport is available, run 'ccreport update --pull' to update" (yellow, command subdued), verified by rendering it. Count still gates the line; the three render gates unchanged. tests/test_statusline.py: count assertions replaced, one test pins that bare 'git pull' is absent, layout tests use a UPDATE-SEGMENT stand-in. README.md Updates section and docs/calculation-reference.md §5.7 + segment list updated. just lint-all: ruff 'All checks passed!', pyright '0 errors'. just test: 1085 passed.
closed_reason: Segment now names 'ccreport update --pull', which works from any cwd. Docs, README and tests updated; lint-all and test suite pass.

title: ccreport limits: mark window instances whose sampling started late
description:
The week window ending 2026-08-11 18:00 opened at 2026-08-04 18:00 but the first stored snapshot is 2026-08-08 13:27 at 77% (src/ccreport/ccreport.py, rate_limit_snapshots). Capture starts when a render happens, so 4 days and 77 points went unobserved.

The report prints 'seen from 77%', but the table's Peak, Spend and $/pp read as whole-window numbers when they cover the sampled span only: that instance shows $458 and $29/pp while the real week spend was ~$2400.

Wanted: in `ccreport limits`, detect an instance whose first sample lands materially after the window start (start = resets_at - window span, from pricing.ROLLING_WINDOWS) and mark it in the table, so a partial instance is not read as a complete one. No snapshot rows are added or deleted; percentages are never synthesized.
acceptance: A window instance whose first sample is well after its start renders a visible partial marker; a fully observed instance renders unchanged; pytest covers both cases.
closed_reason: Partial-window marker shipped: Peak star, caption line, JSON fields, tests, docs

title: ccreport server: merge records from many machines and accounts
description:
Goal: an HTTP server in this repo that receives the full record stream from every machine and merges it, so one report covers machine 1 on account A, machine 2 on account B, and one person running Claude Code on several machines.

Decisions taken with the user, not to be relitigated:
- Payload: full ccreport_records rows, not rollups. A request carries whole files only, never part of one, so every ingest transaction covers a complete file.
- Read surfaces: a server-side CLI (ccreport --server URL renders tables the server computed) and the web dashboard, which lives in the web interface epic ccreport-2s6g. Remote records are NOT mirrored into the local cache.db.
- Auth: one token per machine, minted in the web UI, stored hashed, shown once. Ingest takes the machine_id from the token row, so a machine can only write its own rows and a revoked laptop stops writing on its next push. There is no shared token.
- Web app: this epic owns the shell, the IP allowlist and the machines and tokens pages (ccreport-4e9p), because they exist to hand machines their tokens. Everything the dashboard shows is ccreport-2s6g. Ingest is not behind the allowlist, since machines push from anywhere.
- Setup: ccreport server connect <url> --token <minted> [--opt-in-repos ...] [--only-on-network ...] writes ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml at mode 0600. That file holds the server, the token and the policy; there are no environment variables for any of it.
- Pricing: the server re-prices on ingest. Clients send token counts and the model id; the server computes cost with its own pricing.py, passing through only a cost the session log itself carried. One pricing source, so a machine that has not pulled cannot write wrong money into the merged history.
- Currency: the server converts, owning exchange.py and its own exchange_rates table, each record at its own Oslo-date rate.
- Grouping: the client resolves the project name through its own ccreport merge rules before pushing, and the server treats the pushed name as final.
- Duplicates: every machine copy is stored. Reports collapse records by dedup key and attribute each to the machine that first reported it, so a synced home directory neither double-counts nor silently erases one machine contribution.
- Stack: FastAPI plus Granian, in this repo, following ~/git/kantine (src/km2/web/factory.py app factory, src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py Granian entry point, src/km2/web/middleware.py dependency-style access control).
- Push trigger: both. A detached spawn from the statusline slow path at a base 30 minutes, plus a manual ccreport push. The child writes an attempt stamp on every outcome and widens the interval on consecutive failures, so an unreachable server costs one process per interval rather than one per render.
- Restricted machines: opt-in per project. A project not opted in still pushes its token counts and cost, with project, cwd, repo and session id stripped (ccreport-55s6), and the machine pushes at all only from an allowed CIDR (ccreport-1ley).

Constraints the existing code imposes:
- ccreport_records (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) carries neither account nor machine. Account comes from the account_events change log at read time (AGENTS.md, docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), so the push client stamps the account onto each record before sending; the machine comes from the token.
- statusline.py imports nothing outside the stdlib and must keep doing so. The pusher is a separate detached process, like usage_api.py and update_check.py, and it opens cache.db read-only, taking a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged.

Children: server package and schema, ingest and token auth, web app shell with machines and minting, connect command, push client, aggregation refactor, read-side CLI, restricted-machine redaction, network gate.
closed_reason: Every child closed: server, ingest, UI, push, read side, connect, redaction, network gate

title: Server package: FastAPI factory, Granian entry, merged SQLite schema
description:
Create src/ccreport/server/ holding the FastAPI app and its own SQLite database, separate from ~/.cache/ccreport/cache.db. The client cache stays a per-machine artifact; the server database is the merged one.

Follow ~/git/kantine: an app factory create_app() (src/km2/web/factory.py), a Granian entry point taking host/port/workers (src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py), and a justfile recipe. Add fastapi and granian with uv add, so uv.lock records them. Keep them out of the status line import path: statusline.py must still import stdlib only.

Schema, in a new module mirroring cache_db.py style (one column tuple driving SELECT, INSERT and row mapping, as _CCR_FIELD_COLS does at src/ccreport/cache_db.py:1938):
- machines(machine_id PK, label, first_seen, last_seen). The label is what the web UI shows; machine_id is what rows key on.
- machine_tokens(token_hash PK, machine_id, created_at, last_used_at, revoked_at). Every machine authenticates with its own minted token and the ingest endpoint takes the machine_id from the token row, so a machine can only write its own rows. There is no shared token and no client fingerprint.
- server_records: the ccreport_records columns plus machine_id, account_uuid, account_label, day and oslo_date computed at ingest, and cost NOT NULL, computed by the server from pricing.py rather than taken from the client. Keep the client-sent log cost in its own column so a log-provided cost stays distinguishable from a computed one.
- ingest_files(machine_id, file_path, mtime_ns, size, n_records, updated_at) so a re-push of an unchanged file is a no-op and a re-push of a grown file replaces that file rows.
- exchange_rates, the same shape exchange.py already caches in the client (date PK, rate), because the server converts to NOK for every client. Reuse exchange.py rather than reimplementing the Norges Bank walk-back and the negative cache.
- No unique constraint on the dedup key: two machines pushing the same synced log both keep their rows. Index (account_uuid, dk) so read-time dedup can collapse them and attribute each record to the machine that first reported it.

Configuration by environment variable, no config library: database path, bind address, port, and the networks allowed to reach the web UI (ccreport-4e9p).

Acceptance: just lint-all and just test pass; a test creates the schema in a tmp_path database and asserts the column tuple matches the CREATE TABLE, as tests/test_the_record_dict_matches_the_column_tuple does today.
notes: Landed: src/ccreport/server/{__init__,config,db,middleware,factory,fastapi_server}.py, justfile 'serve' recipe, fastapi+granian via uv add (httpx as a dev group dep for TestClient). exchange.py grew a swappable RateStore (use_rate_store) so the server converts against its own exchange_rates table without a second copy of the Norges Bank walk-back. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1158 passed, 43 of them new in tests/test_server_db.py and tests/test_server_app.py. The acceptance test is TestSchema::test_the_column_tuple_matches_the_create_table (PRAGMA table_info vs REC_COLS).
closed_reason: Server package, Granian entry and merged schema landed

title: Ingest endpoint and per-machine token auth
description:
POST /v1/ingest accepting one machine batch: hostname label, ccreport client version, and a list of files, each with path, mtime_ns, size and its records. A batch carries whole files only. A record is the ccreport_records field set (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) plus account_uuid and account_label, with the project name already resolved by the client. The client sends token counts and the model id; it sends a cost only when the session log itself carried one.

Auth: Bearer plus a token minted by the web UI (ccreport-4e9p). Look the presented token up by hash in machine_tokens and take the machine_id from that row; the batch never names its own machine. A token that is unknown or revoked gets 401 with no detail, so a revoked laptop stops writing on its next push. Update last_used_at on success. Ingest is deliberately NOT behind the UI IP allowlist: machines push from wherever they are.

Behaviour:
- Price every record at ingest with the server pricing.py, and convert with the server exchange.py at each record own Oslo date. A model id the server does not know must fail the file loudly and be reported in the response, never stored as zero: a silent zero is a week of money that looks like an idle week.
- A file whose (mtime_ns, size) already matches ingest_files for this machine is skipped and reported as skipped, so the client can stop resending it.
- A file that changed replaces its rows in one transaction: delete by (machine_id, file_path), insert the records that arrived in the same request. Because a request never carries part of a file, no crash can leave the delete committed without its re-insert. A JSONL only ever grows, but a rotated or truncated log must not leave stale rows. Deletes are scoped to the token machine and never touch another machine copy of the same synced log.
- Respond with per-file accepted, skipped or rejected plus record counts, so the push client updates its watermark from what the server stored rather than from what it hoped.
- Bound the request body size and return 413 above it, naming the limit in the response so a client with one oversized log can report it rather than retry forever.

GET /v1/health validates the token and returns version, the machine label it belongs to, and record count. ccreport server connect calls it to fail a bad token at setup time.

Acceptance: pytest tests using fastapi TestClient cover a good push, no token, an unknown token, a revoked token, an unknown model id, a re-push of an unchanged file, a re-push of a grown file, a truncated file leaving no stale rows, two machines pushing the same log path, and an oversized body.
notes: Landed: src/ccreport/server/ingest.py (POST /v1/ingest, GET /v1/health) and tokens.py. Auth is Bearer -> sha256 -> machine_tokens; the machine_id comes from the token row and the batch never names itself. Every failure is 401 with an empty detail. The server prices each record with its own pricing.py; an unpriced model rejects that file with the model named in the response and stores nothing, while the <...> pseudo-models cost a known zero. Unchanged file skipped on (mtime_ns, size); changed file replaced in one transaction scoped to (machine_id, file_path), so a truncated log leaves no stale rows and another machine's copy of the same synced path is untouched. Body limit is CCREPORT_SERVER_MAX_BODY (default 32 MiB), 413 naming the limit. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1234 passed, 27 new in tests/test_server_ingest.py covering every case the acceptance list names. Also exercised against a live Granian process: health, a good push and a no-token 401 all behaved. One thing to know: server_records.day is the SERVER's local day. A record carries an epoch and no zone offset, so a machine in another zone has its calls bucketed under the server's midnight. txq4 specified day as computed at ingest, so this follows the schema as accepted; if per-machine days matter for the read side, the push client has to send the offset.
closed_reason: Ingest endpoint and per-machine token auth landed

title: Push client: ccreport push, plus a 30-minute detached spawn from the statusline
description:
A new module src/ccreport/push.py that reads the local cache and sends new or changed files to the server, plus the two ways it runs.

Configuration comes from ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, written by ccreport server connect (ccreport-xx2g): one table per server URL holding the minted token, restricted, allow, salt and networks. No push.toml means no push and no spawn, so a machine that has not opted in pays nothing.

What it sends: for each file in ccreport_files whose (mtime_ns, size) differs from the local push watermark, that file records with account_uuid and account_label stamped from the account_events log the way ccreport already stamps them at read time (docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), and the project name already resolved through this machine project_overrides and pricing.project_scope(). The server treats that name as final and holds no merge rules of its own; a ccreport merge run therefore changes what past files should have sent, so fold the override rules into the policy hash that forces a full re-push in ccreport-55s6.

Send token counts and the model id, and a cost only where the session log itself carried one: the server prices everything else, so no client can write wrong money into the merged history. The batch carries no machine id: the server takes that from the token.

Batching: a request carries whole files only, never part of one, so the server delete-then-insert for a file is always one transaction and a crashed push can never leave a committed delete with a partial re-insert. Pack as many whole files per request as the body limit allows. A single log too large for the limit is the one case needing a staged upload; treat it as a follow-up rather than the default path.

Cache access: open cache.db read-only, buffer what the batch needs, and take a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged. A render must never wait on this process, and a long-held lock on cache.db is what makes it wait.

Local state: a push_state table in cache.db keyed by (server_url, file_path) holding the acknowledged (mtime_ns, size), plus per-server meta keys for the last attempt and the consecutive failure count. Never assume a push landed; write the watermark from the server response, and leave a rejected file unrecorded so the next run retries it.

Two triggers:
- ccreport push [--server URL] [--full], manual, prints what it sent, skipped and had rejected.
- A detached spawn from the statusline slow path, base interval 30 minutes. The child writes the attempt stamp on every outcome including failure and a blocked network gate, exactly as update_check.py does for its 12-hour interval (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules), and widens the interval on consecutive failures up to a cap, resetting to the base on the first success. A server down overnight must not be probed 20 times. The status line must not import push.py: it spawns the same way it spawns usage_api.py.

A 401 is terminal, not transient: a revoked token must stop the machine pushing and say so in ccreport server status rather than retry every interval forever.

Acceptance: tests cover the watermark skip, the changed-file resend, a rejected file being retried, whole-file batching at the body limit, account stamping, project resolution through an override rule, the read-only open, the attempt stamp written after a failure, the widened interval after consecutive failures and its reset on success, and a 401 stopping further attempts. A statusline render with no push.toml must spawn nothing; assert it.
notes: Landed: src/ccreport/push.py, the push_state table plus per-server meta in cache_db.py (SCHEMA_VERSION 9 -> 10), 'ccreport push [--server URL] [--full]', and _spawn_push on the statusline slow path. src/ccreport/accounts.py holds AccountTimeline, moved out of ccreport.py so a detached push resolves accounts without importing rich; it gained uuid_at so the payload carries both uuid and label. The client resolves the project through this machine's override rules and sends a cost only where the log carried one. Batches carry whole files, packed to the configured body limit. cache.db is opened read-only for the read; the only write is the watermark, taken from the server's response, so a rejected file stays unrecorded and is retried. The statusline gate is one meta key, push_next_at, that the child writes in a finally on every outcome — the statusline never imports push.py, and a test greps the source to keep it that way. A 401 sets a terminal stopped flag. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1323 passed, 51 new in tests/test_push.py covering every case the acceptance list names. Also ran it end to end against a live Granian server: minted a token, wrote push.toml, pushed a synthetic cache, confirmed the second run sent nothing, then rendered the merged daily and project reports back through 'ccreport --server' with NOK converted from a real Norges Bank rate.
closed_reason: push.py, ccreport push and the statusline spawn landed

title: Split report aggregation from rich rendering in ccreport.py
description:
Today the report commands in src/ccreport/ccreport.py both aggregate records and build rich tables in one pass. The server has to aggregate without rich, and the CLI has to render rows the server computed, so the two halves must separate before the read side can exist.

Work: for the day, month, project, session and account reports, extract a pure function that takes a record stream and returns rows as plain data, leaving the existing command to render those rows. No behaviour change and no output change on any existing report.

Watch the paths a report can take: a bare ccreport serves days older than ROLLUP_WINDOW_DAYS from ccreport_rollups while any filter, --json and adopt take the full record path (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules). The extracted aggregation must be the one place both paths meet, or the server and the CLI will disagree on the same numbers.

Acceptance:
- Existing tests pass untouched.
- New tests call the extracted functions directly and assert the row data.
- A golden test asserts the rendered output of each report is byte-identical to before the split.
- A parity test seeds one corpus that straddles ROLLUP_WINDOW_DAYS and asserts the rollup path and the full record path return identical rows. The golden fixtures alone can exercise one path only, which is exactly where a split like this diverges.
notes: Landed: src/ccreport/aggregate.py holds the record model (UsageRecord, TokenCounts, AggBucket, NokCtx) and the row builders daily_rows/monthly_rows/month_projection/project_rows/account_rows/session_rows, returning ReportRows(rows, total, n_all, all_total) as plain data. It imports no rich, so the server can fold the same records. ccreport.py's five report_* functions now only render those rows; _bucket_by, _accounts_worth_showing and record_oslo_date stay reachable there as re-exports so existing tests are untouched. load_rates_for_records stayed in ccreport.py: a test monkeypatches ccreport.load_rates and the server builds its NokCtx from its own rate table. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1187 passed (29 new in tests/test_reports.py, 2 in test_ccreport.py). tests/golden/reports-{wide,narrow}.txt were captured by running the pre-split HEAD code over tests/report_fixture.py; old and new output diffed byte-identical, and flipping the daily sort order makes the golden test fail, so it is not vacuous. Row-level rollup parity is TestRollupParityOfRows in tests/test_ccreport.py, on the existing rollup_corpus fixture.
closed_reason: Aggregation split into aggregate.py; golden output byte-identical

title: Read side: ccreport --server renders the merged reports
description:
Server endpoints that aggregate, plus the CLI flag that renders them.

Server: GET /v1/report/{day,month,project,session,account} taking the same filters the CLI already offers, running the aggregation extracted by ccreport-3a79 over server_records, and returning rows as JSON. Every response also breaks down by machine and by account, since that is the whole point of merging: one row set that says which machine and which account each number came from.

Client: ccreport --server URL <report> fetches those rows and renders them through the existing rich builders, so a merged report looks like a local one. Without --server, nothing about the local path changes.

Two points settled with the user, no longer open:
- Currency: the server converts. It carries exchange.py and its own exchange_rates table and converts each record at its own Oslo-date rate, so two clients cannot disagree about the same week. A client asking for a report receives both USD and NOK.
- Project grouping: the client resolves the name through its own project_overrides before pushing (ccreport-2r5m) and the server treats it as final. The server holds no merge rules and never re-resolves.

Failure behaviour: an unreachable server prints what it tried and exits non-zero. Never fall back to the local cache silently, since a merged report and a single-machine report differ by exactly the thing being asked for.

Acceptance: tests spin the app with a seeded server database holding two machines and two accounts, and assert each report groups and totals correctly across both; a test asserts NOK conversion uses each record own Oslo date; a client test asserts rendering from a canned server response and a clear non-zero exit when the server is down.
notes: Landed: src/ccreport/server/reports.py (load, dedup, attribute) and report_api.py (GET /v1/report/{day,month,project,session,account} with since/until/project/account/machine/limit/breakdown), plus src/ccreport/remote.py and 'ccreport --server URL' on the CLI. Rows go through aggregate.py, the same module a local report renders from; every row also carries a machines and an accounts split. Dedup is by (account_uuid, dk) keeping the lowest id, so a synced log neither double-counts nor erases a machine's copy. The server converts: nok_context reads its own exchange_rates and each record converts at the oslo_date stamped at ingest. Reports sit behind the network allowlist. An unreachable server prints the URL it tried and exits 1, never falling back to the local cache. ccreport.py's five report_* functions were split into report_*/render_*, and the render_* half is what the merged rows go through. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1272 passed, 38 new in tests/test_server_reports.py including the two-machine two-account seeding, the per-Oslo-date conversion, rendering from a canned response and the non-zero exit. Fixed on the way: 'ccreport --server URL daily' lost the URL, because a subparser argument with a default overwrites what the top-level parser put on the namespace; the subparser flags now use argparse.SUPPRESS. Before that fix the test drove the local path and scanned the real ~/.claude/projects, which is also why it took 52s instead of 0.4s.
closed_reason: Merged report endpoints and ccreport --server landed

title: Per-project opt-in on a restricted machine: redact identity, keep usage
description:
A work laptop must push complete usage while identifying only the projects opted in one at a time. Every record still goes to the server with its model, timestamps and token counts, and the server prices it as usual. What a project that is not opted in loses is identity: project, cwd, repo and session id.

Configuration lives in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, written by ccreport server connect (ccreport-xx2g), keyed per server URL and never in cache.db, so a cache wipe cannot silently unredact a work machine:

  [server."https://ccreport.example.net"]
  token = "<minted>"
  restricted = true
  allow = ["ccreport", "kantine"]
  salt = "<generated when restricted is first set>"
  networks = ["10.172.0.0/22"]

restricted defaults to false. With no push.toml the machine pushes nothing at all; with restricted false it pushes everything under real names, which is what the two personal machines want. Fail closed: a malformed or unreadable push.toml on a machine that has ever been restricted must redact everything rather than fall back to open. Store the last known restricted state where the parser can see it before it trusts the file.

Names in allow are matched through the identity rules ccreport merge already applies, project_identity.py plus pricing.project_scope(), so an alias resolves the same way a report groups it.

Redaction: project becomes a stable pseudonym, the first 8 hex of a hash over the salt and the resolved project name; cwd and repo become null; the session id is hashed with the same salt so sessions still group without carrying the original id. The salt never leaves the machine, so the server sees work-a1b2 as a durable grouping key it cannot reverse.

Interaction with the push watermark: changing restricted, allow, or the local project_overrides that resolve those names changes what past files should have sent. Store a hash of the effective policy alongside the watermark and force a full re-push when it changes, so a project moved out of allow stops being named on the server.

Acceptance: tests cover an unrestricted machine sending real names, a restricted machine redacting a project outside allow while its token counts match the source records exactly, an opted-in project surviving intact, the same project hashing to the same pseudonym across two runs, a malformed push.toml failing closed, and a policy change forcing a full re-push.
notes: Landed: push.redact, pseudonym/pseudo_session, policy_hash, the .restricted marker, and the replace flag on the ingest file object. A restricted machine sends every record's model, timestamps and token counts; a project outside allow loses project, cwd, repo and session id, with project and session becoming salted pseudonyms so the server can still group them. The salt never leaves the machine. Fail-closed is the .restricted marker beside push.toml, read before the file it guards: a push.toml that lost its 'restricted = true' redacts everything and trusts none of its allow list. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1380 passed, 56 new in tests/test_push_policy.py. One hole found and fixed while testing: clearing the watermark was not enough to take a name back off the server, because the server skips a file whose (mtime_ns, size) has not moved — and a closed session log's fingerprint never moves again. IngestFile now carries a 'replace' flag that the client sets on a policy change or --full, so those files are stored rather than skipped. That also changed what --full means: it now repairs the server's copy instead of only rebuilding the local watermark, and the test for it was updated to say so.
closed_reason: Per-project opt-in, redaction and the policy re-push landed

title: Network gate: push only from an allowed CIDR
description:
A work laptop must only send stats while it is on the office network. The gate is evaluated before every push, manual and spawned alike, and a machine that fails it does nothing and records nothing.

Test: some local interface holds an address inside one of the configured CIDRs. Stdlib only, no packets, using socket and ipaddress so the statusline spawn stays cheap; do not probe the server to decide. A VPN that hands out an address in the range counts as being on the network, which is the intended behaviour.

Configuration is the networks key in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, keyed per server URL and written by ccreport server connect --only-on-network (ccreport-xx2g):

  [server."https://ccreport.example.net"]
  networks = ["10.172.0.0/22"]

An absent or empty networks list means no gate, which is what the personal machines want. A malformed CIDR must fail closed for that server, not be skipped: a typo in a work laptop config must never turn into pushing from a hotel wifi.

Interaction with the push watermark (ccreport-2r5m): a blocked push writes no watermark, so everything queued goes out on the first run back inside the network. It does write the attempt stamp, so a machine that is off-network all day spawns one process per interval rather than one per render. Nothing is lost by being away for a week.

ccreport push run by hand while off-network prints which server was skipped and which CIDRs it wanted, and ccreport server status shows the same, so the silence is explained rather than mysterious.

Acceptance: tests cover an interface inside the CIDR passing, every interface outside it blocking with no request sent, an absent networks key allowing the push, a malformed CIDR blocking, IPv6 handled or explicitly refused, and a queued file going out on the first allowed run.
notes: Landed: push.on_allowed_network and the gate in run_once. A connected UDP socket per CIDR picks a route and a source address without putting a packet on the wire, so a VPN handing out an address in range counts as being on the network. Empty networks means no gate. A malformed CIDR blocks: every entry is parsed before any is probed, which was a real bug in the first cut — a machine matching the first CIDR returned True and never reached the typo in the second, so the same config would have passed at the office and failed nowhere else. IPv6 works (::1/128 tested). A blocked push sends no request and writes no watermark, so the queue goes out on the first allowed run; it does stamp the attempt with no failure increment, so a day off-network costs one process per interval. 'ccreport push' and 'ccreport server status' both name the CIDRs that were wanted. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1380 passed.
closed_reason: CIDR gate landed, evaluated before every push

title: Web interface: machines and minted per-machine tokens
description:
The server-rendered web app: its shell, its access control, and the machines and tokens pages. The merged spend dashboard mounts into this shell and is its own issue (see the dashboard child of ccreport-5epr).

Pages:
- Machines: machine label, machine_id, last seen, record count, and whether its token is active or revoked. This answers the question the page will actually be opened for, which is whether that laptop is still reporting.
- Mint: name the machine, submit, and the new token is shown once. It is stored hashed, so it cannot be shown again; a lost token is re-minted, never recovered. Show the exact ccreport server connect command to paste on the new machine, URL and token included, since that is the one moment both halves are known.
- Revoke: one action per token, effective immediately on the next push.

Access control: IP allowlist, no password. Allowed networks come from an environment variable, and the check is a FastAPI dependency, the shape ~/git/kantine uses at src/km2/web/middleware.py:33. The ingest endpoint keeps its own token auth and is NOT behind the allowlist: machines push from wherever they are. Anyone on an allowed network can mint, which is the accepted trade.

Tokens: 32 random bytes from secrets.token_urlsafe, stored as a hash with the machine_id it belongs to, created_at, last_used_at and revoked_at. Ingest looks a presented token up by hash and takes the machine_id from the row, so a machine can only ever write its own rows.

Rendering: server-rendered HTML with Jinja templates, the way ~/git/kantine does it, dark theme matching the dashboard reference. No JavaScript build step and no client framework; the only vendored script in the tree is the chart library the dashboard needs.

Acceptance: tests cover minting producing a token that ingest accepts, the token being unrecoverable from the database after minting, the connect command rendered on the mint page matching what ccreport server connect expects, revocation causing 401 on the next push, a request from a disallowed address getting 403 on every UI route, and ingest still working from a disallowed address.
notes: Landed: src/ccreport/server/pages.py, templates/{base,machines,machine,minted}.html and static/app.css (dark, no JS, no build step). Machines page shows label, id, last seen, last push, record count and token state; the machine page lists tokens with a revoke button. Minting uses secrets.token_urlsafe(32), stores only the sha256, shows the plaintext once with the exact 'ccreport server connect <url> --token <token>' line. Access control is the IP allowlist as a FastAPI dependency on the pages router and on /static; ingest is deliberately outside it. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1234 passed, 20 new in tests/test_server_pages.py covering mint->ingest accepts, the token being absent from a full dump of machine_tokens, the connect command's exact argv shape, revoke -> 401 on the next push, 403 on every UI route from a disallowed address, and ingest plus health still working from one. Also loaded the pages from a live Granian process. Note: the connect-command test asserts the shape rather than round-tripping it, since 'ccreport server connect' is ccreport-xx2g and does not exist yet.
closed_reason: Machines and minting pages landed behind the network allowlist

title: ccreport server connect: one command configures a machine
description:
One command sets up a machine end to end:

  ccreport server connect https://ccreport.example.net --token <minted> [--opt-in-repos ccreport,kantine] [--only-on-network 10.172.0.0/22]

It writes ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml at mode 0600, one table per server URL holding token, restricted, allow, salt and networks. Re-running for the same URL updates that table in place and leaves other servers untouched. This file replaces the environment variables the earlier issues assumed: server URL and token now live here with the policy they govern.

Flags:
- --token, the value minted by the web UI (ccreport-4e9p). connect calls /v1/health with it and refuses to write anything on 401, so a mistyped token fails now rather than silently at a background push 30 minutes later. Refuse to write if the config directory is group- or world-writable.
- --opt-in-repos, a comma-separated list. It sets restricted = true and seeds allow with those projects. Opt-in is per project: every project not named pushes its token counts and cost with project, cwd, repo and session id stripped, per ccreport-55s6. Passing the flag with an empty list is a valid work-laptop state, meaning nothing is identified at all. Names resolve through project_identity.py plus pricing.project_scope(), so an alias matches the way ccreport merge groups it. Generate the redaction salt here when restricted is first set.
- --only-on-network, a comma-separated CIDR list for the gate in ccreport-1ley. Omitted means no gate.

Two companions, because a config you can only rewrite wholesale is a config people edit by hand and get wrong:
- ccreport server allow <project> and ccreport server deny <project>, adding to or removing from the allow list and forcing the re-push that a policy change requires.
- ccreport server status, printing the configured servers, the machine name the server knows this machine as, the restricted state, the allowed projects, the CIDR gate and when the last push landed.

Acceptance: tests cover a fresh write, a re-run updating one server and leaving a second intact, file mode 0600, refusal on a bad token, refusal on a world-writable directory, --opt-in-repos setting restricted with the named projects resolved through an override rule, an empty opt-in list, allow and deny forcing a re-push, and status output on a machine that has never pushed.
notes: Landed: 'ccreport server connect|allow|deny|status' in ccreport.py, plus push.write_server/read_raw and remote.fetch_health. connect calls /v1/health first and writes nothing on a refused token; it refuses a group- or world-writable config directory; it writes mode 0600 with one [server."URL"] table each, merging into an existing entry so a re-run leaves other servers alone. --opt-in-repos sets restricted, resolves the names through this machine's merge rules and generates the salt once (a reconnect keeps it, since regenerating would re-pseudonymize everything already on the server). An empty list is a valid work-laptop state. allow/deny edit the list and clear the watermark, which the policy change requires. status prints what each server calls this machine, what it holds, the restriction, the allow list, the CIDR gate and the last push. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1380 passed. Also ran connect, deny, a refused token and status against a live Granian server and checked the file's mode and contents.
closed_reason: ccreport server connect, allow, deny and status landed

title: Dashboard: merged spend view in the web UI
description:
The reference the user chose is the T3 Code usage view: a dark page whose header carries the date range and 7/30/90-day toggles, a left column of source rows with cost, share bar and token count, a daily area chart toggling cost against tokens, a five-tile stat strip where each tile carries a derived subline, and a breakdown table that switches dimension.

Adapted to what this server holds:

- Header: date range label, 7/30/90-day toggles, refresh.
- Headline: total cost in USD, large, with NOK in the subline. Keep the reference footnote idea and say plainly that the figure is what the tokens would cost at full API rates, since the accounts here are subscriptions and that number is not an invoice.
- Left column: one row per account, personal and work, each with cost, a share bar, its percentage of total cost and its token count. Machines are a column in the breakdown table, not rows here.
- Chart: daily cost with a cost/tokens toggle and one series per account, legend entries filtering the chart. Drawn with uPlot vendored as a file under the server static directory, not a CDN, so the page works on a laptop with no internet. Record the version and source URL beside the file; nothing updates it automatically.
- Stat tiles, five, each with the derived subline that makes it worth reading: processed tokens (per active day), cached input (share of observed input), uncached input (cache writes), output, and cache savings (what those cache reads would have cost at the uncached input price, expressed as a multiple of the raw token cost). cache_read and cache_create are already columns on every record, so all five come from the same aggregation.
- Breakdown table with a dimension toggle: model, day, project, machine. Same columns throughout: cost, share, tokens.

Data: the aggregation extracted in ccreport-3a79, over server_records, plus a dashboard-only summary for the five tiles. The tiles do not reach the CLI; ccreport tables stay as they are.

Redacted projects (ccreport-55s6) appear under their pseudonym in the project breakdown, with real cost and token counts. That is the point of the redaction design and the dashboard must not special-case them away.

Acceptance: tests assert each range toggle bounds the query correctly, the account rows and the chart series total to the headline figure, cache savings matches a hand-computed fixture, every breakdown dimension totals to the same overall cost, a pseudonymous project renders with its numbers intact, and the page references no external origin.
notes: Landed: src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py, the / route, templates/dashboard.html, static/dashboard.js, the dashboard styles, and uPlot 1.6.32 vendored under static/vendor/ with a README recording the version, the source URLs and the fetch date. The machines table moved to /machines. Header carries the date range and 7/30/90 toggles; the headline is USD large with NOK in the subline and the footnote saying plainly that it is what the tokens would cost at full API rates, not an invoice. Left column is one row per account with cost, share bar, percentage and tokens; machines are a breakdown dimension alongside model, day and project. Five tiles, each with its derived subline; cache savings prices every cache read at what it would have cost as fresh input and shows it as a multiple. Also loaded the page in Firefox against a seeded two-machine server and read it: the chart, the toggles, the tiles and the pseudonymous project all render correctly.
closed_reason: Merged spend dashboard landed, uPlot vendored

title: Burn-rate exhaustion ETA for the rate-limit windows
description:
ccu compares usage against the clock and stops there: pace_line (src/ccreport/ccu.py:213) renders "6d 5h into 7-day window (pace: 5d) - 70%% expected, +8%%". Nothing says when the quota actually runs out at the current rate, which is what Claude Code Usage Monitor gives people and the reason they run it.

Data: rate_limit_snapshots (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:309), appended by slow-path status line renders from the live percentages, holds (ts, window, model, percent, resets_at). ccreport limits already reads it, grouping by (window, model, resets_at). The burn rate is the slope of percent against ts inside the current window instance.

Compute: fit the slope over the current window instance only, weighting recent snapshots, and project to 100%%. Report one of two outcomes, both concrete:
- Reaching 100%% before the reset: name the clock time it lands and how long before the reset that is.
- Resetting first: say so, since that is the answer people actually want.

Degradation matters more than precision here. An unobserved window leaves no history (AGENTS.md), and a window with one snapshot supports no slope at all. Under two snapshots, or a slope that is flat or negative, print nothing rather than extrapolate a number that will be wrong in an obvious way. A window whose sampling started late is already flagged in the schema; do not project across that gap as if it were observed.

Surfaces:
- ccu: one line under the existing pace line, in the same section as the bar it describes.
- Status line: a segment behind its own toggle in the env-var table, reading the same snapshots on the slow path only. It must not add a fetch, and it must not import anything new at module level.

Acceptance: tests cover a steady rise projecting a sensible time, a flat slope printing nothing, a single snapshot printing nothing, a projection past the reset saying so, and a late-started window not being extrapolated across its gap. The status line toggle off must render byte-identically to today.
notes: Landed: src/ccreport/burn.py (stdlib only), a line under each bar in ccu, and a CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_BURN segment on the statusline slow path. The slope is weighted least squares with a 30-minute half-life over the current window instance only, anchored at the last reading rather than at now — the gap since it is time nobody sampled, not time the window filled. It returns None on fewer than two samples, a flat or falling slope, a window already at 100% and one whose reset has passed. A window first seen part full is flagged partial and says 'sampled late'; the slope is fitted over observed samples alone and no origin is ever synthesized, which a test pins by comparing a late-started series against an identical one seen from zero. The statusline segment is off by default and reads no new source: it reads the snapshots that same render is about to append to. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1419 passed, 39 new in tests/test_burn.py including a test that the layout with the toggle off renders byte-identically to the call without it. _FAST_CACHE_SCHEMA went 6 -> 7 for the new cached segment.
closed_reason: burn.py plus the ccu line and the statusline segment landed

title: Spend forecast against per-account ceilings
description:
Project spend forward and show it against a ceiling. Display only: nothing notifies, nothing changes colour, no threshold machinery. The number is the feature.

Three horizons, each projected from the same record stream:
- Calendar month. Month-to-date extrapolated to month end. Early in the month one heavy day dominates, so weight recent days rather than dividing the total by days elapsed.
- Billing month. The same projection anchored to the subscription renewal day instead of the first, because that is the period the money is actually settled over. Check whether the usage API response carries a renewal date before adding configuration for it; if it does not, the renewal day is configured per account.
- Rate-limit windows. Projected cost for the current session and week windows, using pricing.ROLLING_WINDOWS and the window bounds the status line already tracks. This is the money counterpart of ccreport-o76s, which projects the quota percentage; the two answer different questions and neither replaces the other.

Ceilings are per account, since personal and work are separate money. Accounts already exist end to end: account_events stamps every record (docs/calculation-reference.md section 9) and every report groups by them. Set them with ccreport budget set <account> <amount> and list them with ccreport budget, stored in a small table beside the other per-account state rather than an environment variable, so two accounts on one machine each carry their own without a parsing convention.

Surfaces: the ccu dashboard, and the merged dashboard once ccreport-5ki6 exists, where a ceiling and a projection are one more row per account. An account with no ceiling shows the projection alone.

Degradation: a month with fewer than three active days projects nothing. A projection built on two data points is a guess with a decimal point on it.

Acceptance: tests cover a steady month projecting close to a hand-computed figure, recent-day weighting moving the projection after a spike, a billing month anchored to a renewal day other than the first, session and week window projections, an account with no ceiling rendering the projection alone, and a sparse month projecting nothing.
notes: Landed: src/ccreport/forecast.py, an account_budgets table in cache.db (SCHEMA_VERSION 10 -> 11) and 'ccreport budget [set|clear]'. Three horizons: the calendar month, the billing month anchored to a configured renewal day, and the session and week rate-limit windows. The daily rate is exponentially weighted with a 7-day half-life, so one heavy day early in the month does not decide the projection; fewer than three active days projects nothing. Ceilings are per account. Display only: no notification, no colour threshold, no alert state. Confirmed the usage API response carries no renewal date, so the day is configured per account as the issue allowed for. daily_costs takes an already-loaded record stream rather than re-reading the cache, so the dedup, merge rules and account stamping are the ones every report already applied. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1464 passed, 45 new in tests/test_forecast.py. Ran 'ccreport budget' against the real cache and it printed the calendar month plus both windows. SCOPE: the ccu surface is NOT done. ccu deliberately imports neither ccreport.py nor rich, and the weighted projection needs the loaded record stream that only load_all_records produces; wiring it would either pull rich into ccu or add a second subprocess to a manual dashboard. The CLI surface is 'ccreport budget'; the dashboard surface is ccreport-5ki6. Say the word and I will add the ccu line by whichever of those two routes you prefer.
closed_reason: forecast.py, account_budgets and ccreport budget landed; ccu surface dropped by decision

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: Decision (user, this session): the ccu surface stays out. ccu remains a quota dashboard that imports no rich and spawns one subprocess. The forecast's surfaces are 'ccreport budget' and the merged dashboard.

title: ccreport web interface
description:
The browser surface over ccreport: the merged spend dashboard and the forward-looking numbers that belong beside it.

Reference: the T3 Code usage view the user picked. Dark page, date range with 7/30/90-day toggles in the header, a left column of rows with cost, share bar and token count, a daily area chart toggling cost against tokens, a five-tile stat strip where each tile carries a derived subline, and a breakdown table that switches dimension.

- The left column splits by account, personal against work. Machines are a breakdown dimension alongside model, day and project.

This epic depends on that one being built first, and on the aggregation split in ccreport-3a79.

title: ccreport limits: show Extra usage spent on windows that hit the limit
description:
`ccreport limits` marks a window that filled with `yes` in the Hit column, but says nothing about what the overflow cost. Once a session window reaches 100%, further work bills against Extra usage (pay-as-you-go credits), and that spend is invisible in the report — the Spend column prices the quota fill, not the overflow.

The data is already stored. `cache_db.py` keeps `extra_usage_snapshots (ts, spent)` — a cumulative Extra-spend series appended by the status line on slow renders and pruned to 31 days (`cache_db.write_usage_cache`, cache_db.py:1495). `cache_db.compute_extra_window_deltas` (cache_db.py:1510) already does the same subtraction for the status line's live S/W deltas: take the newest snapshot at or before a start epoch as the baseline and subtract.

Proposed behaviour: for each `WindowInstance` with `hit_limit` true (ccreport.py:2139), compute Extra spent over the span from the moment the window first reached 100% to its reset (or to now for an open window), as `last_spent - baseline_spent`, and surface it in `report_limits` (ccreport.py:2588) plus `_limits_entry` (ccreport.py:2490) for `--json`.

Open design questions for whoever picks this up:
- Column vs caption. Only hit windows have a value, so a whole column would be one number over a stack of dashes in most reports — the same argument `_open_note` makes for putting the projection in a caption. A caption line per hit window is probably the right shape; decide with the user.
- Span start. From the first sample at 100%, or from the window's own start (`started_at`)? Extra only accrues after exhaustion, so the 100% sample is the honest baseline, but sampling is coarse (a slow render only) and the true crossing sits somewhere before it.
- Monthly billing reset. Extra is a monthly quota, so `spent` drops to 0 at rollover. `compute_extra_window_deltas` clamps a negative delta to 0; a window straddling the rollover needs the same treatment or an explicit unknown.
- Unknown vs zero. A window older than the 31-day retention, or one from before Extra snapshotting existed, has no baseline. That is unknown, not $0, and must render as the absent marker rather than a zero — the same rule `compute_extra_window_deltas` states for its None.
- Costs-only refreshes do not snapshot Extra (`snapshot_extra=False`), so the series is sparser than the rate-limit sample series. A hit window may have no snapshot inside its span at all.

Only the session (5h) window is in the ask, but week and scoped windows hit too; decide whether the same line applies to them.
acceptance:
- A hit session window in `ccreport limits` reports the Extra usd spent while it was over the limit, or the absent marker when no snapshot baseline covers it — never $0 for unknown.
- `ccreport limits --json` carries the same value as a raw float (or null) on the instance entry.
- A window with no Extra spend and a valid baseline reads $0, distinct from unknown.
- A window spanning an Extra billing reset does not report a negative or inflated figure.
- pytest coverage under `tests/` for: hit window with baseline, hit window without baseline, non-hit window, billing-reset straddle.
notes: REVISED twice. (1) Extra prices each window's own span, ungated by Hit — real data had a 99.0%-sampled session window billing $3.42 and week/scoped windows billing while at 44%/17%. (2) A cumulative reading of $0.00 is now its own baseline: without it the oldest window of every type read '—' however much it billed, because the snapshot series can only start after that window opened. The week table was short $4.57 against the sessions inside it. All three tables now total $6.70, the exact cumulative Extra spend. _fit_columns gained Extra as a last-resort drop for the scoped table at 80 columns. 1111 tests pass, ruff and pyright clean.
closed_reason: Extra column shipped; all three tables reconcile to $6.70

title: Tests inherit CLAUDE_* env vars from the developer's shell
description:
`tests/test_ccu.py::TestPaceLine` fails for anyone whose shell exports `CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS`. With `CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS=5` exported, 5 tests fail:

    assert self._pace(50, 3.5) == '3d 12h into 7-day window (pace: 7d) - 50% expected, +0%'
    AssertionError: got '... (pace: 5d) - 70% expected, -20%'

`pricing.pace_days()` (src/ccreport/pricing.py:1417) reads the variable at call time and the suite never clears it, so the pace tests assert against whatever the developer set for their own status line. `CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS=7 uv run pytest` passes; a bare `just test` does not.

The same hole is open for every other variable the code reads for configuration: CF_BADGE, CLAUDE_CACHE_DB_TIMEOUT, CLAUDE_CACHE_SANITY_ABORT, CLAUDE_CACHE_SANITY_DISABLE, CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_DEFER, CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_DIR, CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_KEEP, CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_TIMESTAMP_EPOCH, CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_TOTAL_TOKEN, CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_USAGE_JSON. None of them are cleared today.

Fix: an autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py that deletes them all before each test, ordered ahead of `isolate_cache_db` (which sets CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_DISABLE itself and must win). A test that wants one sets it with monkeypatch, the way `isolate_cache_db` documents for DB_PATH.

TZ, TMPDIR, COLUMNS and XDG_CONFIG_HOME are deliberately out of scope: Rich reads COLUMNS when the module-level console is built at import, before any fixture runs, and the date tests derive their expectations from the local zone rather than assuming one.

Acceptance criteria:
- `CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS=5 uv run pytest tests/` passes.
- A test asserts every name in the list is absent from os.environ.
acceptance: CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS=5 uv run pytest tests/ passes; a test asserts the list is cleared
notes: tests/conftest.py gained an autouse isolate_environment fixture that deletes all 12 configuration variables; isolate_cache_db takes it as a parameter so its own CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_DISABLE=1 is set after the wipe. tests/test_conftest.py asserts the list is cleared, that the list covers every environ.get/setdefault in src/ccreport, and that each of the four exemptions (COLUMNS, TMPDIR, TZ, XDG_CONFIG_HOME) is still read. Verified: CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS=5 CF_BADGE=x CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_KEEP=2 uv run pytest tests/ -> 1115 passed. Clean env -> 1115 passed.
closed_reason: Autouse isolate_environment fixture clears the 12 configuration variables

title: Dockerfile and docker-compose for the local ccreport server
description:
Run the ccreport server (src/ccreport/server/) in Docker for local development.

Deliverables:
- Dockerfile: uv alpine base, two stages, matching the house style used in ~/git/vekt, ~/git/krok and ~/git/magpie. Granian over ASGI (ccreport.server.factory:create_app --factory), not WSGI.
- docker-compose.yml: one service, named volume for the SQLite db at CCREPORT_SERVER_DB, port 8787 published on loopback, ./src bind-mounted read-only so edits apply without a rebuild.
- .dockerignore.
- Add the granian[reload] extra to pyproject/uv.lock. Without it granian refuses --reload, so both 'just serve' and the container's reload are broken today: '[ERROR] Using --reload requires the granian[reload] extra'.

Gotchas:
- CCREPORT_SERVER_NETWORKS gates the web UI (src/ccreport/server/middleware.py). Inside Docker a request from the host arrives from the compose bridge gateway, not 127.0.0.1, so the default loopback allowlist answers 403 to the browser. The compose file must allow the private ranges.
- /health requires a machine token, so it is not usable as an unauthenticated healthcheck.
- Development only. No TLS, no reverse proxy, no build-metadata args.

Acceptance: 'docker compose up --build' serves the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8787/ from a browser on the host, and the db survives a 'docker compose down'.
notes:
Done and verified on this machine.

Files: Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .dockerignore. pyproject/uv.lock gained the granian[reload] extra (watchfiles 1.2.0).

Verified:
- docker compose build && up: '[INFO] Listening at: http://0.0.0.0:8787'
- GET / -> 200, /machines renders with /static/app.css
- /data owned by app (uid 1000); server.db, -shm and -wal written there
- touch src/ccreport/server/pages.py -> '[INFO] Changes detected, reloading workers..' Reload works across the macOS bind mount because WATCHFILES_FORCE_POLLING is set; inotify alone does not cross it.
- Minted machine 'docker-smoke', ran docker compose down + up, it was still listed. Row deleted afterwards; 0 machines left.
- just lint-all: 'All checks passed!' + pyright '0 errors'. just test: 1500 passed.

The image also COPYs ./src, so it runs standalone under plain docker run; the compose bind mount overlays it.
closed_reason: Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml and .dockerignore added; granian[reload] pulled in. Verified end to end on this machine.

title: Bare `ccreport server` crashes: AttributeError on args.config
description:
Running `ccreport server` with no subcommand raises:

    File "src/ccreport/ccreport.py", line 3062, in main
        cmd_server_status(args)
    File "src/ccreport/ccreport.py", line 1754, in cmd_server_status
        path = Path(args.config or push.CONFIG_PATH)
    AttributeError: 'Namespace' object has no attribute 'config'

Why: main() routes a missing `server_command` to cmd_server_status (ccreport.py:3055-3062), but `--config` is added only to the four subparsers (connect/allow/deny/status) at ccreport.py:2977-2978. A bare `ccreport server` therefore never sets the `config` dest.

Fix: make cmd_server_status read the option defensively (getattr) or define `--config` on the `server` parser itself, so bare `ccreport server` behaves as `ccreport server status`.
acceptance: `ccreport server` prints the same status output as `ccreport server status` instead of a traceback; a pytest under tests/ covers the bare invocation; just lint-all and just test pass.
notes: Fixed in src/ccreport/ccreport.py:1749-1758 — cmd_server_status now reads getattr(args, 'config', None). Test: tests/test_push_policy.py::TestStatusCommand::test_a_bare_server_command_reads_the_default_config. just lint-all clean (ruff + pyright 0 errors), just test 1501 passed. Live check: 'uv run ccreport server' prints the status block.
closed_reason: cmd_server_status reads getattr(args, 'config', None); bare-invocation test added; lint and suite pass

title: Push failures report neither their reason nor their nature
description:
`ccreport server status` printed `last push 2026-08-13 19:24, 1 failures since` while the server held 0 records. The push had failed — the container was not listening yet — but the output reads as a success with a footnote.

Two causes:

- `push.py:597` catches PushError and stores only `failures + 1`. `str(exc)` carries the reason (connection refused, 413, 500) and is discarded, so nothing can ever tell the user which it was.
- `ccreport.py:1783` labels the attempt stamp `last push`. The stamp moves on every outcome by design, so the label is wrong whenever the count is non-zero.

Fix: persist the reason with the attempt, return it from `read_push_attempt`, and render a failed attempt as a failure with its reason.

title: Drop the work-laptop wording from the codebase
description:
The restricted-push code named its use case in comments, a docstring and the --opt-in-repos help text: 'a work-laptop state', 'True is the work laptop', 'unredact a work laptop', plus three test docstrings. Name the mechanism instead of the imagined owner.

Sites: src/ccreport/push.py (ServerConfig.restricted docstring, _marker_path), src/ccreport/ccreport.py (blocked-push comment, --opt-in-repos help), tests/test_push_policy.py (three docstrings, one test name).
acceptance: grep -ri 'work laptop|work-laptop|work machine' over the repo outside .dogcats returns nothing; lint and tests pass

title: A bare --opt-in-repos must set restricted with an empty allow list
description:
ccreport server connect --opt-in-repos required a value, so the shortest way to say 'restrict this machine and identify nothing' was --opt-in-repos '' — and the bare flag was an argparse error instead. Anyone reaching for the bare flag got a usage error and could reasonably retry without it, which connects the machine wide open.

Fix: nargs='?' with const='' on the argument, so the bare flag lands on the same path as the empty string: restricted = true, allow = [], a generated salt.

Caveat: with nargs='?', a bare --opt-in-repos placed before the positional url consumes the url as its value.
acceptance: ccreport server connect URL --token T --opt-in-repos writes restricted = true, allow = [] and a 32-char salt; a test covers the bare flag

title: Mint page: choose CIDRs and opt-in repos for the connect command
description:
The mint form on /machines and /machines/<id> only takes a machine id and a label, so the printed 'ccreport server connect' line never carries --only-on-network or --opt-in-repos. Whoever mints has to remember both flags and hand-edit the command, and a machine that should have been restricted connects wide open when they forget.

Add to both mint forms:
- Networks: comma-separated CIDRs, appended as --only-on-network.
- Restrict this machine: a checkbox that emits --opt-in-repos, plus a names field that fills it. Checked with an empty names field emits the bare flag, which is restricted with nothing identified.

The policy still lives on the machine — the server stores none of it, it only writes the command. Validate the CIDRs before rendering: a typo in one blocks every push from that machine and there is nothing on the server side to notice it.
acceptance: Both mint forms carry the two controls; tokens.connect_command appends the flags with shell-safe quoting; an unparseable CIDR is refused with a message instead of minting a broken command; tests cover the empty, named and invalid cases

title: Dashboard: an all-time range beside 7d, 30d and 90d
description:
The spend dashboard toggles between 7, 30 and 90 days, so total spend since the first push is unreachable from the page — the server holds every record a machine ever sent and nothing shows the sum.

Add an 'All' toggle: the span starts at the oldest stored record's local day and ends at the same next midnight the day counts use, so the headline, the tiles, the chart axis and the four breakdowns all cover the whole history. An empty database falls back to the default range rather than rendering a zero-day axis.
acceptance: /?days=0 renders every stored day; the toggle reads 'All' and highlights when selected; an empty database renders the default range; tests cover the bounds and the empty case

title: Dashboard page loads take 2-9s: the whole record corpus is materialized per render
description:
GET / on the merged server is slow: ~2.4s for the default 30d range and ~6.5s for ?days=0 (all time), measured with curl against the Docker container on 127.0.0.1:8787.

Cause is server-side, not SQLite. cProfile of ccreport.server.dashboard.build(conn, 0) against the live /data/server.db (613063 rows, 285069 after dedup) shows 8.8s wall, of which:

- reports.load (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:69) 6.9s -- it fetches every column of every row in range and builds a UsageRecord + MergedRecord per row (285069 calls to _as_merged, 1.4s just there), then sorts them.
- The folds that follow re-walk that list seven times: account report via reports.build, _chart, _tiles, and four _breakdown calls (3.3s across the four). aggregate.TokenCounts.__iadd__ alone is called 1710416 times.

The page never shows an individual record. Every number on it (five tiles, the account column, the daily chart series, and the four breakdown tables) is a sum over some subset of (machine, account, project, model, day, oslo_date). One GROUP BY over those columns, with the same lowest-id-per-(account_uuid, dk) dedup applied in SQL, returns 1129 rows in 1.2s against the same database -- verified by benchmark.

Note: an ad-hoc benchmark left CREATE INDEX idx_srec_ts ON server_records(ts) committed in the live /data/server.db. Either adopt it in db.py's DDL or drop it.

Acceptance criteria:
- dashboard.build folds from grouped SQL rows rather than from a list of MergedRecord, and keeps the same dedup semantics reports.load has (lowest id wins per (account_uuid, dk); a null dk is kept as it stands).
