- A result cache keyed on the range and on a stamp that ingest moves, so a second render of an unchanged database does no query.
- ?days=0 renders in about a second cold and effectively instantly warm; the narrower ranges stay under that.
- Every number on the page is unchanged: tiles, account shares, chart series and all four breakdowns must total the same as before.
- Tests under tests/ cover the new query path and the cache invalidation.
notes:
Fixed. dashboard.build now folds reports.load_grouped (one SQL GROUP BY over machine/account/project/model/day, dedup in SQL) instead of materializing every record, and pages.index calls dashboard.cached_build, which holds one view per range against db.content_stamp and the render's local date. Added idx_srec_ts and bumped SCHEMA_VERSION to 2, which also adopts the index the benchmark had left in the live db.

Measured against the live 613063-row database in the Docker container, HTTP total time:
  days=0   6.51s -> 1.13s cold, 0.006s warm
  days=30  2.36s -> 0.43s cold, 0.003s warm
  days=7   0.64s -> 0.26s

Numbers verified unchanged: total cost, token totals and call counts are identical to the old path for 0/7/30/90-day ranges, and every breakdown row matches to 1e-12 (float summation order is the only difference).

Tests: TestGroupedLoading in tests/test_server_reports.py (11 cases incl. totals equal load(), dedup, per-filter narrowing, group pricing instant), TestCachedBuild in tests/test_dashboard.py (7 cases incl. push and new-day invalidation, per-database keying), TestContentStamp and two index cases in tests/test_server_db.py. Full suite 1555 passed; just lint-all clean.
closed_reason: Dashboard now folds SQL-grouped rows behind a stamp-keyed cache; days=0 6.5s -> 1.1s cold, 0.006s warm

title: Drop burn.py: the ccu "At this rate" lines and the statusline BURN segment
ccreport server allow/deny: accept several projects and infer the single server
description:
`ccreport server allow macsetup dogcat py_project_template` fails with `unrecognized arguments: py_project_template`.

Two separate limits in the parser at src/ccreport/ccreport.py:3000-3002 (the `if name in ("allow", "deny")` branch):

1. `project` is a single positional, so only one project can be allowed or denied per invocation.
2. `url` is a required positional, so the URL must be typed even when push.toml names exactly one server. In the failing command above, `macsetup` was swallowed as the URL and `dogcat` as the project.

cmd_server_allow (src/ccreport/ccreport.py:1723) already calls _resolved_projects([args.project]) — a list of one — so the resolve, the set union/difference, the write_server call and the clear_push_state call all take a list unchanged.

Proposed shape:
- Replace the two positionals with one variadic `targets` (nargs="+").
- If targets[0] is a key in push.read_raw(path), it is the URL and the rest are projects.
- Otherwise, if push.toml names exactly one server, use it and treat every target as a project.
- If targets[0] starts with http:// or https:// and is not configured, that is still the unknown-server error it is today (tests/test_push_policy.py::TestAllowDenyCommands::test_an_unknown_server_is_an_error covers it) — do not fall through to treating a URL as a project name.
- Error when no project is left after the URL is consumed, and when several servers are configured and no URL was given (name them).
- Update the two --help strings for the new positional.

Note push.toml is written by `ccreport server connect` and the allow list is read back through push.load_config.
acceptance:
- `ccreport server allow <url> a b c` adds all three to that server's allow list; `deny` removes all three.
- With exactly one server in push.toml, `ccreport server allow a b c` works without a URL.
- `ccreport server allow https://nowhere.example x` still exits 1 when that URL is not configured.
- `ccreport server allow <url>` with no project exits 1 with a message naming the gap.
- With two servers configured and no URL, the command exits 1 and prints both URLs.
- The watermark is still cleared once per run (cache_db.clear_push_state).
- New tests in tests/test_push_policy.py::TestAllowDenyCommands cover multi-project allow, multi-project deny, and URL omission; `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.
closed_reason: One variadic targets positional; the URL is inferred when push.toml names one server

title: Server: an Accounts tab that sets a display alias per account
description: Screenshots of the dashboard leak the login email: an account renders as its email everywhere (post@rykroken.net). The server needs an /accounts page where each account gets an alias, and every server-rendered view then shows the alias instead. Decision (asked and answered): server-side only. The CLI's own reports and the statusline keep showing the email, and server_records.account_label keeps holding it — this renames what the server draws, it does not redact what it stores. Where the email comes from today: - The push client stamps each record with account_uuid and account_label from AccountTimeline (src/ccreport/accounts.py, called at src/ccreport/push.py:407). The label is the email. - Ingest stores both columns (src/ccreport/server/db.py:76-77). - Two places turn the pair into a display string, and both spell it the same way: src/ccreport/server/reports.py:116 (full record path) and src/ccreport/server/reports.py:213 (grouped path) — `account = account_label or account_uuid`. That single expression is where an alias lookup belongs, so the dashboard and `ccreport --server` inherit it together. - The account is also a filter: reports.py:61-63 matches `account_label = ? OR account_uuid = ?`. An alias typed as a filter should match too. Proposed shape: - New table `account_aliases(account_uuid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, alias TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at REAL NOT NULL)` in db.py's _SCHEMA_SQL, plus a SCHEMA_VERSION bump. - A db.py reader that returns {account_uuid: alias} and a writer that sets or clears one. - reports.py resolves the display name as alias -> account_label -> account_uuid, in both builders. - New page GET /accounts listing every account_uuid seen in server_records with its stored label, its alias, its record count and its total cost, each row a form that POSTs a new alias. Add `Accounts` to the nav in server/templates/base.html. - The page sits behind the network allowlist like every other page (factory.py wires that; ingest stays outside it). - dashboard.cached_build holds one view per range against db.content_stamp — setting an alias must invalidate that cache, or the page keeps drawing the email until the next push. content_stamp (db.py:328) is the hook. Related: ccreport-26kw is unrelated CLI work; this one is server-side only.
acceptance:
- /accounts lists one row per account_uuid in server_records, with label, alias, records and cost.
- Setting an alias renames that account on the dashboard (headline table, account column, chart series legend) and in `ccreport --server URL account` on the next render, with no push and no restart.
- Clearing an alias falls back to account_label, then to account_uuid.
- `--account <alias>` filters the same rows the email does.
- server_records is not rewritten: the stored account_label is untouched.
- The page is refused from outside the allowlisted networks, like /machines.
- Tests in tests/test_server_pages.py and tests/test_server_reports.py cover set, clear, fallback order, filtering by alias and the dashboard cache invalidation; `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.
closed_reason: Accounts page sets a per-account alias; every server view resolves alias -> label -> uuid

title: Server UI: delete a token and delete a machine outright
description:
The web UI can mint and revoke, and that is all. A machine minted by mistake — http://10.172.1.236:8787/machines/aa — stays in the list forever, and a revoked token stays in its machine's table forever. Both need a delete.

What exists now:
- db.revoke_token (src/ccreport/server/db.py:263) stamps revoked_at; nothing ever removes the row. The button is in server/templates/machine.html and posts to /tokens/{token_hash}/revoke (src/ccreport/server/pages.py:132).
- machine_tokens, server_records and ingest_files all declare `REFERENCES machines(machine_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, and db.connect sets `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` (db.py:214), so deleting the machines row already deletes all three. This is why the confirmation matters: a machine with records holds real money.

Decision (asked and answered): one delete removes everything — the machine, its tokens, its ingest_files and every server_record it pushed — behind typing the machine id to confirm.

Proposed shape:
- db.delete_token(conn, token_hash) -> bool, deleting the row rather than stamping it. Keep revoke: revoking is what you do to a machine that is still out there, deleting is what you do to a mistake.
- db.delete_machine(conn, machine_id) -> int, returning the record count it destroyed, letting the cascade do the rest.
- POST /tokens/{token_hash}/delete beside the existing revoke route, and a Delete button in machine.html's token table next to Revoke.
- POST /machines/{machine_id}/delete, guarded by a form field the person must type the machine id into; a mismatch re-renders the page with an error and deletes nothing. Redirect to /machines on success with a line naming what went: "Deleted aa and its 0 records."
- A machine that no longer exists is a 404 on GET /machines/{id} already (pages.py:68-79); after deletion that is the correct state.
- dashboard.cached_build keys on db.content_stamp — deleting records must move that stamp or the dashboard keeps drawing the deleted machine's spend.

Related: ccreport-1fz1 adds an Accounts tab to the same UI; the two touch pages.py and base.html but not the same routes.
acceptance:
- The token table has a Delete button; deleting removes the row entirely, and the machine's next push with that token is rejected.
- Revoke still exists and still only stamps revoked_at.
- POST /machines/{id}/delete with the typed id matching deletes the machine, its tokens, its ingest_files and its server_records, then redirects to /machines naming the record count destroyed.
- A mismatched or empty confirmation deletes nothing and re-renders with an error.
- Deleting a machine that pushed records changes db.content_stamp, so the dashboard drops its spend on the next render.
- GET /machines/{id} for the deleted machine is a 404.
- Tests in tests/test_server_pages.py cover token delete, machine delete with records, the refused confirmation and the 404; `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.
closed_reason: Token delete beside revoke; machine delete behind the typed id, cascading to records

title: Restricted push: fold every unallowed project into one per-account bucket, no pseudonyms
description:
Today a restricted machine sends each unallowed project under its own salted pseudonym (src/ccreport/push.py:248 `redact`), and the server draws a row per pseudonym with real cost and tokens. The dashboard therefore shows how many private projects exist and what each one costs. That is the leak: the count and the shape of the work.

Wanted: the server renders no unallowed project at all. Every unallowed record folds into ONE bucket per account, named from the account.

Client side (src/ccreport/push.py):
- `redact` sets project=None, sid=None, cwd=None, repo=None for a record whose project is not in `allow`. No per-project pseudonym, no per-session pseudonym.
- `pseudonym` and `pseudo_session` (push.py:227, :238) lose their only caller. The `salt` field in push.toml and the salt written by `ccreport server connect` become dead — decide in the change whether to keep writing it (harmless, and re-adding a pseudonym later needs it) or drop it from the config and from ServerConfig.
- `policy_hash` (push.py:268) must move when this ships, or every already-pushed file keeps its pseudonym rows: the material it hashes is unchanged by a code edit. Add a redaction-shape constant to that material and bump it. Ingest replaces a file's rows wholesale, and a policy change already sets `replace` on every file, so the old pseudonym rows disappear as the re-push walks the corpus. No server-side purge is needed.

Server side (src/ccreport/server/reports.py):
- A record with project NULL renders as the bucket name instead of NULL. Both builders spell the project the same way today — reports.py:116 (full record path) and reports.py:213 (grouped path) — so the fold belongs there, beside the account resolution.
- Assumed name: `<account display>/aggregated`, where the account display is the alias from ccreport-1fz1 when one is set, and the account label or uuid otherwise. So `post@rykroken.net/aggregated` before an alias and `personal/aggregated` after. The other reading of the request — `<account-id>/<alias>-aggregated`, keeping both — is one f-string away if that is what was meant.
- The bucket must group: two unallowed projects on the same account are one row, one project entry in the dashboard breakdown and one entry in `ccreport --server URL project`.
- The server holds no policy, so it cannot tell a NULL project from a restricted machine apart from a NULL from anything else. NULL only ever arrives from redaction today; if that stops being true the bucket needs a marker column instead.

Depends on ccreport-1fz1 for the alias half of the name; ships without it by falling back to account_label.
acceptance:
- A restricted machine's unallowed projects arrive with project, sid, cwd and repo all NULL, and no salted value anywhere in the request.
- The dashboard's project breakdown shows exactly one row per account for all unallowed spend, and the cost and token totals are unchanged from today.
- That row is named `<account label>/aggregated` while the account has no alias, and `<alias>-aggregated` once it has one. `post@rykroken.net/personal-aggregated` is never rendered.
- An account whose records carry no label falls back to `<account uuid>/aggregated`.
- `ccreport --server URL project` shows the same single row under the same name.
- Setting or clearing an account alias renames the bucket on the next render, with no push and no restart.
- Shipping the change forces a full re-push (a redaction-shape constant moves policy_hash), and after it no pseudonym row remains on the server.
- The salt is still written by `ccreport server connect` and still in the policy_hash material, with no caller.
- An allowed project is untouched: real name, real cwd, real repo, real session id.
- tests/test_push_policy.py covers the fold and the policy_hash move; tests/test_server_reports.py and tests/test_dashboard.py cover both name forms, the uuid fallback, the grouping and the alias rename; `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.
notes:
DECIDED — bucket name (supersedes the assumed name in the description):

  alias set      ->  `<alias>-aggregated`        e.g. `personal-aggregated`
  no alias       ->  `<account label>/aggregated` e.g. `post@rykroken.net/aggregated`

The email appears only while nothing better exists. Setting an alias removes it
from the string entirely, so `post@rykroken.net/personal-aggregated` must never
be rendered — the alias replaces the whole account segment, slash included.
Fall back to the account uuid where a record carries no label.

One row per account in the project breakdown either way.

DECIDED — salt: keep it. `ccreport server connect` still generates and writes
it, `ServerConfig.salt` stays, and it stays in the policy_hash material, with no
caller once `redact` stops pseudonymizing. `pseudonym` and `pseudo_session`
stay in push.py unused, so re-introducing a pseudonym later needs no config
migration. Because the salt no longer changes when the redaction shape does, the
redaction-shape constant in the policy_hash material is what forces the
re-push — it is not optional.

Sessions are not exempt: sid goes to NULL with project, cwd and repo. A session
count per bucket is itself a signal about the hidden work.
closed_reason: redact nulls project, sid, cwd and repo; server folds them into one bucket per account

title: Versioned migration runner shared by cache.db and the server database
description:
The server database has no migration path. src/ccreport/server/db.py:227 compares
PRAGMA user_version against SCHEMA_VERSION and, when they differ, runs _SCHEMA_SQL --
which is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS throughout. On an existing server file every one
of those creates is a no-op, so a column added to server_records never appears and
bumping SCHEMA_VERSION changes nothing. The docstring at db.py:21 tells the next agent
to bump it, which reads as a working mechanism and is not one. That file is the only
copy of a machine's records once its JSONL logs have rotated, so the failure mode is a
query against a missing column on a database nothing can rebuild.

cache.db does migrate, ad hoc: _ADDED_COLUMNS (cache_db.py:379) for plain ADD COLUMN,
plus five meta-flagged steps in _run_migrations (cache_db.py:607-781). Each step
hand-rolls its own BEGIN IMMEDIATE, rollback handler and post-hoc verification, and
the flag write is what makes it once-only. It works; it is copy-pasted per step and
has no ordering, no log and no guard against an edited step.

Reference implementation studied: /Users/ove/Trash/migrate (src/migra/db/migration/).
Four things there fit ccreport:

1. A numbered chain validated at load -- gaps and duplicate versions are hard errors
   (migrations.py:361, _validate_migrations).
2. The step and its version bump applied in ONE executescript, so a crash cannot land
   between the schema change and the pointer update (migrations.py:480).
3. A migration_checksum table: refuse to start when a version that was already applied
   no longer matches the code that ran (migrations.py:432).
4. An flock file beside the database, taken for the whole run (migrations.py:144).
   ccreport needs this: statusline, push and ccu open cache.db from separate processes
   concurrently, and today two of them can enter the bootstrap at once.

Do NOT copy from it: the .sql-file format (ccreport migrations carry Python logic --
migration 2b at cache_db.py:651 matches model names by substring, which SQL cannot
express), the 1:1 testfile pairing, the symlink/BOM/filename-case hardening (that
guards an operator-supplied directory; ccreport ships its steps in its own package),
or the psqtie DB wrapper.

Shape agreed with the user: one shared module (e.g. src/ccreport/migrations.py) that
both databases call. Steps are Python callables in a numbered list, one list per
database. PRAGMA user_version stays the pointer -- both files already use it. The
existing cache_db meta flags must keep working: a database that already ran
migrated_dedup_keys_pk_order must not re-run it as step N.

Constraint from AGENTS.md: statusline.py imports nothing outside the stdlib and defers
cache_db into the functions that touch the DB. The new module is imported by cache_db,
not by statusline, and everything it does stays behind the user_version gate so a warm
render pays nothing.
acceptance:
- A shared migration runner exists, with steps declared as an ordered numbered list per
  database, and a gap or duplicate version raises at load rather than skipping a step.
- Each step and its version bump commit atomically; a crash mid-step leaves the DB on
  either the old or the new version, never between.
- An applied version whose step source or name has since changed is detected and
  refuses to run further, naming the version.
- Concurrent processes cannot both apply the same step (file lock beside the DB file,
  with a bounded wait that raises rather than hanging).
- server/db.py routes schema changes through the runner; adding a column to
  server_records reaches an existing server database, proven by a test that opens a DB
  at the old schema, adds a step, reopens and asserts the column and the preserved rows.
- cache_db.py routes schema changes through the runner above baseline 11. The frozen
  pre-baseline bootstrap still runs for a database below it, and a database carrying
  the old meta flags re-runs none of the five legacy steps (test with a pre-seeded
  meta table).
- SCHEMA_VERSION in both files is derived from the chain head, not hand-edited, and a
  test fails if either is set independently.
- just lint-all and just test pass; every new public function has a pytest test.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED

New: src/ccreport/migrations.py, tests/test_migrations.py (40 tests).
Wired: server/db.py (MIGRATION_BASELINE 3, chain empty), cache_db.py
(MIGRATION_BASELINE 11, chain empty). Both SCHEMA_VERSIONs now read
migrations.head(MIGRATION_CHAIN, MIGRATION_BASELINE).

One deviation from the design note: Step has no legacy_flag field. The chosen
numbering keeps the five meta-flagged repairs below the baseline, so nothing
would have read it, and a dead field on a frozen dataclass reads as a mechanism
the next agent has to rule out.

One addition: run() takes timeout_s, and cache_db passes _db_timeout(). Without
it a status line render could wait the full 60 s on another process's migration,
where today it fails fast on the SQLite write lock and prints a stale figure.

Verified: just lint-all clean (ruff + pyright, 0 errors), just test 1612 passed.
closed_reason: Shared runner in src/ccreport/migrations.py, both databases wired, user tested ccreport and the server against their real files

title: Delete-machine confirm block reads as three stacked lines
description:
The 'Delete this machine' section on /machines/{id} (src/ccreport/server/templates/machine.html:50-59) renders 'Type', 'sbnmbp', 'to confirm' on three separate lines with the input and button below.

Cause: the global rule in src/ccreport/server/static/app.css:66 sets 'label { display: flex; flex-direction: column }'. The confirm label wraps the machine-id span and the input, so every child becomes its own row.

The most destructive action on the server also has the weakest visual framing: no panel, no boundary, same weight as the mint form above it.
acceptance: The confirm sentence reads as one line, the input and the Delete machine button sit on a row together, the block is visually separated as a destructive action, and tests/test_pages.py still passes.
closed_reason: Confirm block is one panel with the label, input and button on a row

title: Move the machines and accounts pages under /settings
description:
The web UI's admin pages sit at the root beside the dashboard. Move them:

  /machines                       -> /settings/machines
  /machines/{id}                  -> /settings/machines/{id}
  /machines/mint            (POST) -> /settings/machines/mint
  /machines/{id}/delete     (POST) -> /settings/machines/{id}/delete
  /accounts                       -> /settings/accounts
  /accounts/{uuid}/alias    (POST) -> /settings/accounts/{uuid}/alias

Touch points: src/ccreport/server/pages.py (route decorators and the two RedirectResponse URLs), the nav in templates/base.html, the form actions and links in templates/machine.html, machines.html, accounts.html, minted.html, and the route strings in tests/test_server_pages.py.

The /tokens/{hash}/revoke and /delete endpoints stay where they are; they redirect through Referer.

The whole UI already sits behind the network allowlist in factory.py, so the prefix changes no gate.
acceptance: Every UI page is reachable under /settings, the nav links there, minting and deleting still redirect to a live URL, and just lint-all and just test pass.
closed_reason: Pages, forms, redirects, nav, tests and AGENTS.md moved to /settings

title: Dashboard toggles are lost on refresh
description:
The breakdown tabs (model, day, project, machine) and the chart's Cost/Tokens toggle live in JS state alone, so a refresh drops back to model + cost. Only ?days= survives.

Put both in the query string: /?days=30&by=project&metric=tokens.

Files:
- src/ccreport/server/pages.py: index() takes by and metric, validates by against dashboard.DIMENSIONS and metric against cost|tokens, and passes both to the template. Neither belongs in dashboard.cached_build's key: the view already carries all four breakdowns and both chart series, so this only picks what renders visible.
- templates/dashboard.html: the range links carry by and metric; the dimension tabs become real hrefs so the page works with no JS; the table for by renders unhidden and its tab gets 'on'.
- static/dashboard.js: each toggle rewrites the URL with history.replaceState instead of reloading, so switching stays instant.
acceptance: Switching a breakdown tab or the chart metric updates the address bar, a reload lands on the same tab and series, a range switch keeps both, and an unknown or missing value falls back to model and cost.
closed_reason: days, by and metric all round-trip through the query string

title: Detail pages per breakdown entity, with charts
description:
Every breakdown row on the dashboard should open a page for that entity, scoped to the same range: /account/{key}, /model/{key}, /day/YYYY-MM-DD, /project/{key}, /machine/{key}.

Shape (decided with the user): the dashboard narrowed to one entity — headline, tiles, account bars, breakdown tables for the OTHER four dimensions — plus several charts that combine different metrics rather than one chart with a toggle:
  1. cost over time, one series per account
  2. cost over time, one series per model
  3. tokens over time by kind (input, output, cache write, cache read)
  4. calls per bucket

The day page charts by hour instead of by day, which needs reports.load (per-record timestamps) rather than load_grouped (which folds the hour away).

Notes:
- The scope matches the string the breakdown table shows, so redacted project buckets and account aliases link to a page that finds their rows.
- A scoped build must not enter dashboard.cached_build's cache: that is keyed on (db path, days) and holds the whole-server view.
- The catch-all route means /static has to be mounted before pages.router in factory.py, or the asset URLs match /{dimension}/{key} first.
- Chart palette: the current dashboard.js COLORS fail the dataviz validator on our dark surface (deutan dE 4.6 for green vs amber). The reference dark palette #3987e5,#d95926,#199e70,#c98500,#d55181,#008300 passes every check on #191c24.
acceptance: Each of the five dimensions has a detail page reachable from its breakdown row, the range toggle carries over, the day page charts hourly, an unknown dimension is a 404, an entity with no records renders an empty page rather than an error, and just lint-all and just test pass.
closed_reason: Five detail pages with four charts each, linked from every breakdown row

title: The /static mount is outside the network allowlist
description:
factory.py gates the routers with Depends(restrict_remote_addr_dep(...)), but app.mount('/static', StaticFiles(...)) takes no dependencies argument, so the mount is reachable from any address while every page it styles answers 403.

What leaks is app.css, dashboard.js, detail.js, palette.js and the vendored uPlot build — no records and no tokens — so this is a claim that is wrong rather than a disclosure. AGENTS.md says '/static is behind the gate with the pages it styles', which is what made it look covered.

Fix: wrap StaticFiles in an ASGI app that runs the same ip_allowed check (middleware.ip_allowed is already importable), or serve the assets from a gated route. Then a test that an outside address gets 403 for /static/app.css the way it does for /settings/machines — tests/test_server_pages.py::TestAccessControl is where the sibling cases live.
acceptance: An address outside the configured networks gets 403 for /static/app.css, an allowed one still gets 200 with the right content type, and the AGENTS.md sentence matches what the code does.
closed_reason: NetworkGated wraps the static mount; 403 outside the allowlist, 200 inside

title: Drop the statusline fast cache on ConfigChange
description:
Claude Code fires a ConfigChange hook when a settings file changes (user, project, local, policy) or a skills file changes. The payload carries session_id, transcript_path, cwd, config_source and config_path. Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#configchange

The status line caches its fetch results per session for FAST_TTL_S (15 s) in $TMPDIR/claude-statusline-<uid>-<sid>.json (statusline._fast_cache_path). Two of the cached values are read out of settings files: the sbx/!sbx badge, which walks local -> project -> user settings in statusline._render_sandbox (src/ccreport/statusline.py:1189), and the CLAUDE_CODE_STATUSLINE_* segment toggles that settings 'env' feeds. After an edit they stay stale for up to 15 s.

Wire a ConfigChange hook that deletes that file, so the next render takes the slow path and re-reads the settings. The memo file (.memo.json) is not touched: its DSP verdict comes from the claude process argv and its ~/.claude.json stamp is invalidated by that file's own mtime/size.

Model it on bin/clear-statusline-memo.sh: read stdin, jq the session_id, sanitize it the same way _session_state_path does, rm -f, print nothing, exit 0 on every path. Exit 0 matters twice over here — a ConfigChange hook that exits 2 blocks the config change from taking effect.

Also add a README section covering both status line hooks (the existing SessionStart memo one and this one), and wire the hook into ~/git/macsetup/claude/mbp2022/settings.json and ~/git/macsetup/claude/sbnorge/settings.json.
acceptance:
- bin/clear-statusline-cache.sh deletes the fast cache file for the session id on stdin and leaves the .memo.json file in place.
- It exits 0 and prints nothing for missing stdin, malformed JSON, an absent session_id and a missing file.
- A test under tests/ asserts the filename the script builds equals statusline._fast_cache_path(sid).name, as tests/test_statusline.py:778 does for the memo script.
- README documents both hooks with the settings.json block to paste.
- Both macsetup settings.json files carry the ConfigChange hook.
- just lint-all and just test pass.
closed_reason: Shipped: bin/clear-statusline-cache.sh wired as ConfigChange in both macsetup settings.json files, README hooks section, 9 tests. lint-all, shellcheck and 1670 tests pass.

title: Show 15 rows in the dashboard breakdown scrollbox
description: The breakdown table on the dashboard (/) sits in .breakdown-clip, capped at max-height: 17rem in src/ccreport/server/static/app.css:269, which shows about six rows before the scrollbar takes over. Raise the cap so 15 body rows plus the sticky header fit, and keep the clip so a longer list still scrolls instead of pushing the page.
acceptance: A range whose breakdown has 15 or more rows shows 15 of them without scrolling; a 16th row is reachable by scrolling; the sticky header still covers the rows under it.
notes: Scope changed mid-session: the dashboard breakdown is no longer clipped at all (one table on that page), and the 15-row clip moved to the detail page's stacked tables as .table-clip (40.5rem). Verified 15 fully visible rows in the day table on /project/radgiver?days=0.
closed_reason: 15-row clip landed on the detail page's stacked tables; the dashboard breakdown runs unclipped

title: Make every server table sortable by column
description: Tables in src/ccreport/server/templates/ (dashboard.html breakdown, detail.html breakdowns, machines.html, machine.html tokens, accounts.html) render in one server-chosen order and cannot be re-sorted. Add a progressive-enhancement script under src/ccreport/server/static/ loaded from base.html that makes every data table's header cells sort the rows on click. Sort on the raw values the cells already carry (data-usd, data-int, data-ts, data-day) and fall back to numeric-or-text parsing for the rest; leave the actions column and the empty-state row alone. The vendored uPlot legend also renders as a table (.u-legend) and must be skipped.
acceptance: Clicking a header sorts the table by that column and clicking again reverses it; aria-sort reflects the state; numeric columns sort by value, not by formatted text; the uPlot legends and the actions column are untouched; a test asserts base.html links the script and that no template or asset gained a remote origin.
notes: sort.js + app.css th.sortable rules, linked from base.html after format.js. Verified in Firefox against the running server: dashboard breakdown sorts by tokens, /settings/machines sorts by last seen, the accounts rename column and the token actions column stay plain, uPlot legends untouched. Tests: TestSortableTables in tests/test_dashboard.py.
closed_reason: sort.js sorts every server-rendered table; verified in Firefox and covered by TestSortableTables

title: CI/CD: gate master, publish the server image on a tag
description:
The repo has no .github/ at all. Every lint and test run is local, and the server image exists only as ccreport:dev, built by `just docker-up` on whichever machine runs it.

Two release tracks on different clocks:

1. The server is a deployed service and wants a named, reproducible artifact — a multi-arch image on GHCR, built for a `server-v*` tag.
2. The CLI and status line are a checkout. `src/ccreport/update_check.py` measures 'an update' in commits past origin/master and `ccreport update --pull` fast-forwards it. That model does not change; the CLI track gets a test gate and nothing else.

Decisions already taken with the user:
- Image is built for a `server-v*` tag only. No `:edge` build on master pushes.
- The sea deployment keeps its branch-based infra playbook. `.deploy.remote.settings.toml` and $INFRA_DIR are out of scope — nothing outside this repo is touched.
- The CLI keeps master-as-release. No tags, no PyPI, no homebrew formula.

Reference material: /Users/ove/git/dogcat/.github/ (uv + just + SHA-pinned actions, dependabot) and https://github.com/kluzzebass/gastrolog/ (.github/workflows/publish.yml — QEMU + buildx + GHCR multi-arch).

Full plan: /Users/ove/.claude/plans/parsed-doodling-treehouse.md
acceptance: All six children closed. A pull request runs lint and tests on GitHub. A `server-v*` tag produces ghcr.io/oroddlokken/ccreport:<version> and :latest for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

title: Add the CI workflow and dependabot
description:
No GitHub Actions run today, so a pull request lands with no lint or test signal. Add the gate that both release tracks share.

Files to create:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `.github/dependabot.yml`

Also edited: `justfile`, one line — see the pyright pin below.

ci.yml shape, modelled on /Users/ove/git/dogcat/.github/workflows/ci.yml:
- Triggers: `push: branches: [master]` and `pull_request: branches: [master]`. Note master, not main — dogcat's uses main.
- `concurrency: group: ci-${{ github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: true`.
- One ubuntu-latest job: actions/checkout, astral-sh/setup-uv, `uv python install 3.13`, `uv sync --group dev --frozen`, `uvx --from rust-just just lint-all`, `uv run pytest --timeout 30 -n 8 tests`.
- Pin every action by commit SHA with a trailing version comment. Reuse the SHAs dogcat already carries.

`--frozen` on the sync is deliberate and differs from dogcat: the Dockerfile already builds that way, and without it a uv.lock that has drifted from pyproject.toml resolves silently, so CI tests a version set no one has run.

Pin pyright too. `just lint-pyright` runs `PYRIGHT_PYTHON_FORCE_VERSION=latest uv run pyright`, which downloads whatever pyright shipped most recently — a release upstream turns master red with no change here. Change that recipe to `PYRIGHT_PYTHON_FORCE_VERSION=${PYRIGHT_PYTHON_FORCE_VERSION:-latest}` and have ci.yml set the variable to 1.1.411, the version uv.lock resolves. A local run still tracks latest, and CI keeps calling `just lint-all`, so one command means the same thing in both places. Bump the CI value when the lock moves pyright.

Python 3.13 only, no matrix: pyproject.toml sets requires-python = '>=3.13' and ruff target-version = 'py313'.

Do NOT copy dogcat's pnpm and `pnpm install` steps. This repo has no package.json and `just lint-all` is ruff plus pyright, nothing else. Its `fetch-depth: 0` is also unnecessary: every git call in the suite is a stubbed subprocess.run (tests/test_update_check.py, tests/test_update_command.py), so a shallow checkout tests the same thing.

dependabot.yml: the github-actions ecosystem, weekly, all patterns in one group — a straight copy of dogcat's.

Deliberately skipped: dogcat's validate-issues.yml. It runs `uv run dcat doctor`, and dcat is not in this repo's uv.lock.
acceptance: The pull request that adds these files shows a green CI check on GitHub. `just lint-all` and `just test` pass locally against the same tree, and `just lint-pyright` with no PYRIGHT_PYTHON_FORCE_VERSION set still type-checks against latest.

title: Split the Dockerfile CMD from docker-compose's dev command
description:
The Dockerfile's CMD is development-shaped and cannot be published as-is. It ends in:

    CMD ["python", "-m", "ccreport.server.fastapi_server", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--reload"]

`--reload` starts a watchfiles reloader over a bind mount a published image does not have. In src/ccreport/server/fastapi_server.py it also forces one worker, through `workers=1 if args.reload else args.workers` — which is what one SQLite file wants, so today the correct worker count is an accident of the reload flag.

Changes:
1. `Dockerfile`: CMD becomes `["python", "-m", "ccreport.server.fastapi_server", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--workers", "1"]`. --workers 1 is explicit because argparse defaults it to 2 in the same file.
2. `Dockerfile`: the comment block above that CMD explains that --reload drops the server to one worker. That behaviour moves to docker-compose.yml, so rewrite the comment with the CMD — left alone it describes a flag the line below it no longer carries.
3. `docker-compose.yml`: add a `command:` on the ccreport-server service carrying the --reload form, so `just docker-up` keeps the behaviour its own comments describe and the read-only ./src mount stays useful.
4. `tests/test_docker_image.py`: new test in the spirit of tests/test_dashboard.py's remote-origin guard. Parse both files and assert the image CMD carries --workers 1 and no --reload, and the compose command carries --reload. They are a pair; an edit to one alone either ships a reloading server or breaks local development with no failing test.

This blocks the release workflow — a tag must not publish a reloading image.
acceptance: `just docker-up` still reloads the container on an edit under src/. `docker build -t ccreport:prod .` then `docker run --rm -p 8788:8787 -e CCREPORT_SERVER_NETWORKS='0.0.0.0/0' ccreport:prod` answers on curl and logs one worker with no reloader. tests/test_docker_image.py passes.

title: Publish the server image to GHCR on a server-v* tag
description:
The server image exists only on the machine that built it. Give it a named, reproducible artifact on GHCR, cut from a tag.

File to create: `.github/workflows/release-server.yml`

- Trigger: `push: tags: ['server-v*']`. The prefix keeps server versions clear of the CLI's commit-count model — the CLI has no tags and is not affected.
- `permissions: contents: write, packages: write`.
- Two jobs. A `test` job repeating the CI steps (uv sync --group dev, just lint-all, pytest), and an `image` job with `needs: test`, so a tag cannot ship an untested tree.
- image job: docker/setup-qemu-action, docker/setup-buildx-action, docker/login-action against ghcr.io with secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN, then docker/build-push-action with `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64`.
- Tags: `ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${VERSION}` and `:latest`, where VERSION is GITHUB_REF_NAME with the `server-v` prefix stripped. github.repository is oroddlokken/ccreport, already lowercase, so no case fix is needed.
- docker/metadata-action supplies the OCI labels so the image records its version and revision.
- Final step: softprops/action-gh-release for the tag with `generate_release_notes: true`. This repo has no CHANGELOG.md, unlike dogcat — do not port dogcat's awk extraction.
- Pin every action by commit SHA with a trailing version comment. dogcat carries the checkout and setup-uv pins; the docker/*, metadata-action and softprops SHAs come from gastrolog's publish.yml (link below), which is not checked out locally — read it over the network or resolve each tag through the GitHub API.

Model: https://github.com/kluzzebass/gastrolog/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml (QEMU + buildx + GHCR multi-arch). Its scratch-image and homebrew jobs do not apply here.

The arm64 leg runs under QEMU and downloads rather than compiles: uv.lock carries musllinux aarch64 wheels for granian, watchfiles, orjson, pydantic-core and markupsafe, and the base is ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-alpine.

Out of scope: the sea deployment. It keeps pulling the ccreport_server branch through the $INFRA_DIR playbook, and .deploy.remote.settings.toml is not edited.
acceptance: Pushing tag server-v0.1.0 produces ghcr.io/oroddlokken/ccreport:0.1.0 and :latest with linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 manifests, plus a GitHub Release with generated notes. `docker run` of the pulled image serves the dashboard. The workflow is tag-triggered, so its first real run is that tag push — gh workflow run cannot exercise it.

title: Document the two release tracks in README and AGENTS.md
description:
Once a server-v* tag publishes an image, two statements in the tree are wrong or incomplete.

1. `AGENTS.md` pipeline rules, the update_check bullet, says 'There are no tags and no releases — master is the release and the unit is a commit.' That is true of the CLI and now false of the server. Qualify it in place, and add to the pipeline rules: a server-v* tag is what builds ghcr.io/oroddlokken/ccreport, and the Dockerfile CMD is the production one while docker-compose.yml overrides it with --reload for development.

2. `README.md` documents installing from a checkout and the commit-count updater (the Install and Updates sections around line 173). Add a section under the server documentation for running the published image:

    docker run -p 8787:8787 -v ccreport-data:/data \
      -e CCREPORT_SERVER_DB=/data/server.db \
      -e CCREPORT_SERVER_NETWORKS='127.0.0.1/32 192.168.0.0/16' \
      ghcr.io/oroddlokken/ccreport:latest

   plus one line saying a server-v* tag is what builds it. Leave the CLI's Install and Updates sections alone — that track is unchanged.

Prose follows earn-the-line: say what the reader cannot see from the command.
acceptance: AGENTS.md no longer claims the repo has no releases without saying which track it means. README explains how to run the server from GHCR. Nothing in the CLI Install or Updates sections changed.

title: Quota guard hook: stop the session before extra usage
description:
A quota guard that stops a session before it crosses into extra usage, so an
org account never pays for overflow it did not choose.

Armed by environment only: `CCQUOTA_STOP` unset makes both hooks exit 0 before
they touch Python, so an unarmed session pays one bash spawn per prompt.
`CCQUOTA_WARN=85 CCQUOTA_STOP=95 claude` arms one session; the environment is
read at launch, so a launcher alias is how it gets used in practice.

Hook input carries no quota data — only session_id, transcript_path, cwd,
permission_mode, hook_event_name and effort. The readings come from the local
cache instead: the statusline writes `five_hour` and `seven_day` to
rate_limit_snapshots from Claude Code's own stdin on every render, and the
usage row holds sonnet_percent and scoped_percent from the 10-minute API fetch.

Two hooks, one shared verdict module:

- UserPromptSubmit: over the warn line emits systemMessage; over the stop line
  emits `{"continue": false, "stopReason": ...}`, which halts processing and
  leaves the session open for input.
- PreToolUse: same verdict, so a turn already running halts at its next tool
  call rather than burning to the end of the window.

No hook can exit the CLI. `continue: false` is the strongest stop the harness
offers, and stopReason reaches the person, never Claude.

Fail-closed on an unknown reading, with two distinctions that decide whether
the guard is usable:

- A quota the API nulls because the plan does not have it (see the
  _API_QUOTA_FIELDS comment in usage_api.py) is not applicable, not unknown.
  Conflating them blocks the first prompt of every plan without a Sonnet cap.
- Unknown carries an age. The fetch TTL is 600s, so a reading younger than ~15
  minutes counts and anything older or absent blocks. Say so in the stopReason:
  the way out is unsetting the variable and restarting.

Warnings dedupe on the window instance. Key a TMPDIR memo on resets_at, the
same shape bin/clear-statusline-memo.sh already uses, so one warning lands per
window and a fresh one lands after the window rolls.

Scope note: the quota is per account, not per session. This stops the sessions
that carry the variable on this machine, and nothing else.
acceptance:
- With CCQUOTA_STOP unset, both hooks exit 0 without starting Python.
- Over CCQUOTA_STOP on any watched window, UserPromptSubmit emits continue:
  false and the prompt does not reach the model.
- Over CCQUOTA_STOP mid-turn, PreToolUse halts the next tool call.
- Between CCQUOTA_WARN and CCQUOTA_STOP, one systemMessage lands per window
  instance, not per prompt.
- A quota the API omits or nulls for the plan does not block.
- A reading older than the staleness budget, or no reading at all, blocks, and
  the stopReason names the environment variable to unset.
- Tests cover each verdict against the existing SQLite fixtures.
notes:
Built as src/ccreport/quota_guard.py plus bin/quota-guard.sh, wired to both events by one wrapper. Two departures from the issue text, both agreed with the user first:

1. Freshness for S and W comes from a new per-session TMPDIR file (.quota) that statusline._save_quota_reading writes on slow renders while CCQUOTA_STOP is set. rate_limit_snapshots writes a row only when a reading moves a whole percent, so its newest ts dates the last change, not the last observation, and a quiet session would have read as stale at any quota level. Snapshots and the usage row remain fallbacks.
2. Staleness is per source: NATIVE_MAX_AGE_S 900s for the stdin reading, API_MAX_AGE_S 3600s for Sonnet and scoped. The 600s fetch TTL is not the ceiling on the usage row's age - statusline.USAGE_HEARTBEAT_S is, since a render skips the API while nothing on the line needs it.

Tests: tests/test_quota_guard.py, 58 cases. Full suite 1742 passed, just lint-all clean. README has a 'The quota guard' section; AGENTS.md has the module entry and a pipeline rule.
closed_reason: Quota guard shipped: quota_guard.py, bin/quota-guard.sh, statusline .quota stamp, 58 tests

title: Generate synthetic session logs for the JSONL reader
description:
No test parses a Claude Code session log. The suite seeds cache.db directly with fabricated file paths (tests/test_cache_db.py, tests/report_fixture.py), and test_forecast.py keeps its subject off the real ~/.claude/projects. `parse_jsonl_file` in src/ccreport/ccreport.py is the front of the whole pipeline and has no end-to-end coverage, so nobody knows whether `just test` passes on a machine that has never run Claude Code. A GitHub runner is exactly that machine, which is why this blocks ccreport-25in: a red first CI run would not say whether the workflow or the suite is wrong.

Add `tools/make_synthetic_logs.py`, alongside the existing tools/ scripts:

- Takes an output directory and writes a projects/ tree of JSONL session logs into it — several projects, several sessions each, more than one model, and enough days for a report to have rows to group.
- Derive the record shape from `parse_jsonl_file` and the JSONL fields it actually reads, not from memory of Claude Code's format. A generator that writes fields the reader ignores proves nothing.
- Runnable by hand for reproducing a parse bug outside pytest, and importable so a test can build a corpus into tmp_path.
- Nothing is committed as data. The corpus is generated per run; only the script lives in the repo.

Then at least one test that points the reader at a generated tree and asserts what comes back: token counts, model, session and project per record.
acceptance: `python tools/make_synthetic_logs.py <dir>` writes a tree that parse_jsonl_file reads into records. A test builds a corpus into tmp_path and asserts the parsed records match what the generator wrote. `just test` passes with HOME pointed at an empty directory, which is the state a CI runner starts in. No generated JSONL is committed.

title: Qualify README's no-tagged-versions claim as CLI-only
description:
README.md opens the Updates section (around line 189) with "There are no tagged versions." That is a repo-wide claim and the first `server-v*` tag makes it false, even though the sentence is about the CLI: the section below it explains `ccreport update --pull` and the fast-forward model, which does not change.

ccreport-4a7u adds the server's GHCR section and is scoped to leave Install and Updates untouched, so this sentence is nobody's job there. It is tracked here instead, and depends on 4a7u so the two README edits land in order rather than in each other's way.

The change: say which track has no tags. One clause — "the CLI has no tagged versions" — and leave the fast-forward instructions, the `ccreport update` commands and the Install section as they are. The server's tag scheme is already stated in the section 4a7u adds; do not repeat it here.

Prose follows earn-the-line: the reader is in this section because they are updating a checkout, so tell them what applies to that and nothing more.
acceptance: README's Updates section no longer claims the repo has no tagged versions without naming the CLI. The fast-forward instructions, the `ccreport update` commands and the Install section are unchanged. `just lint-all` and `just test` still pass.

title: Serve the previous render's project costs instead of walking the project inline
description:
A slow render whose cost summary has aged past COST_SUMMARY_MAX_AGE (900 s) re-reads the project's JSONL logs on the render thread, in the frame Claude Code is waiting on.

Path: src/ccreport/statusline.py:2030 -> src/ccreport/pricing.py:1383 (compute_project_rolling_costs).

Measured on an 8 GB A18 Pro (2 performance cores, fanless): the walk takes 0.566 s cold against a 0.08 s full render, measured with

    python3 -c "import sys,time; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from ccreport.pricing import compute_project_rolling_costs as f; t=time.monotonic(); f('$PWD'); print(time.monotonic()-t)"
    just bench

0.566 s is a floor, not a worst case: it ran directly after 'ccreport --json' had refreshed the record cache. This project is 73 MB across 98 .jsonl files; the largest single log on the machine is 54.8 MB. The record cache is refreshed by CLI runs alone, so an active session's log never matches cached_meta and always takes the full-parse branch.

The cadence is worse than once per 900 s. When is_costs_refresh_blocked() suppresses the detached --costs-only spawn (src/ccreport/statusline.py:748), the summary is never rewritten while the inline walk still runs, so a project that loses the machine-wide costs lock pays this every slow render.

Chosen approach: render the previous cycle's project costs, already held in _Fetched, and pick up the fresh summary on the next render - what the 15 s fast cache already does for every other slow value. Costs land one render behind rather than stale.

Rejected: widening COST_SUMMARY_MAX_AGE. That leaves the cost windows stale instead of one render behind.
acceptance: A slow render with an expired cost summary spawns the detached refresh and returns without calling compute_project_rolling_costs. The project cost segment shows the previous cycle's figure on that render and the fresh one on the next. 'just bench' shows no regression in phase 1 wall time. Tests under tests/test_statusline.py cover the expired-summary path and assert no inline walk.
closed_reason: The render serves the stored project split; no inline walk

title: Thin cache.db snapshots to weekly past the recent few days
description:
The daily snapshot is a whole-file copy of a database that only grows, and retention is counted in files rather than bytes.

Path: src/ccreport/cache_db.py:993 (_maybe_snapshot), :37 (_SNAPSHOT_KEEP_DEFAULT = 14), :36 (_DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_DIR).

Measured on this machine: ~/.local/share/ccreport/snapshots holds 1.8 GB, one 155.7 MB .db per day, 14 kept. The copy alone writes ~57 GB/year to a soldered SSD. Both figures grow with tables the schema comments describe as never pruned - ccreport_records ('only ever grows'), rate_limit_snapshots ('Never pruned'), exchange_rates ('never pruned').

The render does not take the copy itself: src/ccreport/statusline.py:2525 sets CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_DEFER=1, so the detached refresh does. The write still happens once a day.

Chosen approach: keep the last few days daily, then thin older snapshots to weekly, in _maybe_snapshot's retention step.

Do not disable the pre-bootstrap copy. get_connection takes it as the pre-image for the only code that rewrites existing rows, and _sanity_check compares against it.

CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_KEEP is a per-machine workaround for the resident 1.8 GB, but it does not change the daily 155.7 MB write.
acceptance: Retention keeps N recent dailies and one per week beyond them, configurable through the existing CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_KEEP and a new weekly bound. The pre-bootstrap copy and _sanity_check are untouched. Tests under tests/test_cache_db.py cover the thinning boundary with a fixed clock, including the day a daily becomes the week's keeper.
closed_reason: Retention keeps 7 dailies then one per ISO week

title: Collapse the quota guard's four snapshot queries into one
description:
The PreToolUse hook fires before every tool call, and past the CCQUOTA_STOP gate each one starts a CPython interpreter, opens cache.db and runs nine queries.

Paths: bin/quota-guard.sh:9 (the CCQUOTA_STOP gate is the only early exit), src/ccreport/quota_guard.py:182, :241 (four separate 'ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1' queries against rate_limit_snapshots, one per window).

Measured on an 8 GB A18 Pro (2 performance cores, fanless): 39.3 ms wall and 25.6 ms user CPU per invocation, over 100 runs:

    time (for i in $(seq 1 100); do CCQUOTA_STOP=99 bash bin/quota-guard.sh <<< '{"session_id":"probe"}' >/dev/null; done)

The multiplier - tool calls per agentic turn - is not measured. On a fanless chassis this is a sustained-load cost, not a peak one.

Chosen approach: replace the four per-window queries with one grouped statement.

The module is already careful and none of that changes: stdlib only, sqlite3 deferred into the functions that need it, its own read-only connection rather than cache_db.get_connection (whose bootstrap and daily snapshot do not belong before every tool call), DB_TIMEOUT_S = 2.0.

Deferred, not chosen here: serving the whole verdict from the .quota file a slow render writes, when that file is inside NATIVE_MAX_AGE_S, so the sqlite open happens only when it is not. Same shape of fix as ccreport-2pty for the render path.
acceptance: read_windows issues one grouped query for the four windows in place of the four LIMIT 1 queries, and returns identical readings - same percent, same resets_at, same source, same ts per window. The per-window staleness budgets (NATIVE_MAX_AGE_S for session and week, API_MAX_AGE_S for sonnet and scoped) are unchanged. Tests under tests/test_quota_guard.py cover a window with no rows, a window whose newest row is past its budget, and four windows with different newest timestamps.
closed_reason: One grouped query replaces the four per-window snapshot queries

title: Count the detached children a render spawns in the energy bench
description:
The energy bench cannot see the three processes that matter, so the render's real child count has never been observed.

Path: tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py:19-21 and :63-80 (measure_child). Its docstring says it outright: the detached spawns use start_new_session, escape the process tree, and os.wait4 rusage never counts them.

What phase 1 does measure on this machine: wall 0.08 s, cpu 0.09 s, rss 38.9 MB - the reaped children alone, so 3 git plus 'ps -Aww', with battery off per bin/statusline-command_x.sh:15.

What it misses: ccreport.usage_api (src/ccreport/statusline.py:760), ccreport.update_check (:977, which itself spawns 'git remote get-url'), and ccreport.push (:2450). None is gated on test_mode, so a '-t' render does spawn them.

That leaves a derived count of up to 8 concurrent children per slow render against 2 performance cores, never observed. Two further wrinkles for whoever builds this: the three spawns are interval-gated (600 s, 43200 s, push_next_at), so the warmup at :133 fires them and the following timed runs mostly skip them; and 'ccreport.update_check' spawns a grandchild.

Chosen approach: extend the bench with a phase that counts the processes a render spawns with start_new_session, and their own children, without touching statusline.py's hot path.

Rejected: a probe inside statusline.py behind an env flag. It puts diagnostic code on the path this work is about keeping cheap.
acceptance: The bench reports the number of detached children a slow render spawns, and their descendants, separately from the reaped-tree figures phase 1 already prints. The count is taken with the three interval gates reset so the run is not measuring a skipped spawn. statusline.py is unchanged. The existing phase 1 and phase 2 output is unchanged.
notes:
Phase 4 added to tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py; statusline.py untouched.

How it counts: the render is started with start_new_session, so its reaped children carry its pid as their pgid and each detached spawn carries its own. A poll of 'ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,state=' (no command column, ~8 ms) sorts one group from the other; ps is asked about a single pid only to name a process or to test a leader met after the render exited (marker CCREPORT_ENERGY_BENCH_RUN, inherited through _refresh_env).

Gates: each run gets a private HOME (tempfile.mkdtemp) holding only .config/ccreport/push.toml pointed at a closed port. That leaves the usage row, update_checked_at and push_next_at cold without writing to ~/.cache/ccreport/cache.db.

Observed on this machine (3 cold renders):
  detached children (outside the figures above, 3 cold renders):
    spawned by a render     3   ccreport.push, ccreport.update_check, ccreport.usage_api
    spawned by those        2   security x2
    peak live at once       4   (sampled, the reaped tree included)

Runs last, after phase 2, so the forced spawns cannot land in the power window. --child-runs N controls it, 0 skips. --json carries it as detached_children.

Tests: tests/test_benchmark_tool.py gains TestProcessLabels, TestBenchHome and TestDetachedChildren; the last runs two cold renders and asserts the detached set is exactly the three modules. just lint-all clean, just test 1752 passed.
closed_reason: Phase 4 counts the three detached spawns and their descendants against a private HOME; observed peak is 4 concurrent, not the derived 8

title: Compress rotated cache.db snapshots with stdlib lzma
description:
Snapshots are stored as whole, uncompressed SQLite files: ~/.local/share/ccreport/snapshots holds 1.8 GB, one 163.3 MB .db per day, 14 kept. SQLite pages compress about ten to one, so compressing the rotated ones cuts the resident bytes by roughly that factor.

Measured on 2026-08-15.db (163,266,560 bytes) on this machine:
  stdlib lzma, preset 1 - 16,364,208 bytes, 1.8 s
  zstd -3 -T0           - 18,898,765 bytes
  gzip -6               - 21,560,638 bytes, 1.2 s

lzma wins on ratio and ships with Python, so there is no reason to probe for an installed zstd or xz binary and no subprocess. Python 3.13 has no stdlib zstd; compression.zstd lands in 3.14, and pyproject requires-python is >=3.13.

Path: src/ccreport/cache_db.py:1037 (the rotation step in _maybe_snapshot), :1125 and :1131 (_sanity_check's glob and read-only open), :1096 (the restore hint).

Two constraints on where the compression goes.

1. The newest snapshot from a prior day has to stay a plain .db. _sanity_check opens it read-only at :1131 for the ccreport_records counts, and _warn_on_drop prints 'Restore with: cp <snapshot> <DB_PATH>' at :1096. Decompressing 163 MB to run two COUNT(*) queries would put that cost on every migrate run and every day's snapshot run.

2. Compress during rotation, not at write time. conn.backup already writes the full 163 MB; compressing in the same pass adds a 163 MB read plus a 16 MB write to that day. Compressing a file that is already days old moves the work off the write path and touches each file once.

This is separate from ccreport-2bbk (thin snapshots to weekly) and multiplies with it: thinning alone still keeps the same number of files, just spread over more days, so it widens coverage rather than cutting the 1.8 GB. Neither change cuts the daily 163 MB write - only not copying every day would.

Adjacent, in the same rotation step: the glob '????-??-??.db' at :1038 unlinks the .db and leaves the -shm and -wal sidecars a read-only connection created beside it. 11 orphans at 32K each are in the directory now, the oldest for 2026-07-06, whose .db has already been rotated away. Whatever the compressed extension is, the rotation and the glob in _sanity_check both need to know about it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Snapshots older than the plain-file window are stored compressed with stdlib lzma; the newest prior-day snapshot stays a readable .db.
- _sanity_check picks the newest prior-day plain .db and never decompresses.
- Rotation counts compressed and plain snapshots as one series, and removes the -shm and -wal sidecars along with the .db.
- The restore hint names a command that works for the file it points at.
- Tests under tests/test_cache_db.py cover the rotation boundary with a fixed clock: the day a plain snapshot becomes a compressed one, and a directory holding both kinds.
closed_reason: Rotated snapshots are stored as .db.xz at lzma preset 1

title: Show the armed quota guard on the status line
description:
The quota guard (bin/quota-guard.sh, src/ccreport/quota_guard.py) arms on CCQUOTA_STOP, read from the claude process environment at launch. Nothing on the status line says whether this session is armed, so a launcher alias that was meant to cap the session is indistinguishable from one that was not.

Render a Q segment in the rate-limit group of src/ccreport/statusline.py, beside S/W: 'Q:85/95' with CCQUOTA_WARN and CCQUOTA_STOP, or 'Q:95' where only the stop line is set. Subdued by default, yellow once a known window is at or past warn, red once one is at or past stop. An unparseable CCQUOTA_STOP blocks every prompt in the guard, so render it red as 'Q:!'.

The statusline must not import quota_guard: that module refuses to import statusline for the same reason, and a per-render import costs every frame the tokenizing of 470 lines. Parse the thresholds inline and assert in tests that the parse agrees with quota_guard.threshold, the way tests/test_quota_guard.py already pins _session_state_path and the file schema.
acceptance:
- The segment renders while CCQUOTA_STOP is set and nothing renders while it is unset
- Colour follows the highest known window percent against the two thresholds
- An unparseable CCQUOTA_STOP renders red
- statusline.py gains no import of quota_guard
- A test pins the inline threshold parse against quota_guard.threshold
- just lint-all and just test pass, tests/golden unchanged
closed_reason: Q segment renders beside S/W when the guard is armed

title: Price the three detached children the energy bench now counts
description:
Phase 4 of tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py counts the processes a slow render detaches (ccreport.usage_api, ccreport.update_check, ccreport.push, plus their own children) but prices none of them. The report's 0.2 J/render covers the reaped tree alone, because os.wait4 rusage never sees a start_new_session child — the point ccreport-5ig8 was opened over.

So the per-render energy figure understates a slow render by however much those three cost, and nobody knows the number. usage_api is network-bound and does a keychain read (two 'security' children observed); update_check runs a git remote get-url and a network call; push connects to each configured server.

Path: tools/benchmark_statusline_energy.py, _detached_run and measure_detached (the watcher), and the 'energy per render' block in main() (the figure that would gain a second line).

Two wrinkles for whoever takes this. The watcher already knows each detached group by pgid, so wall time per group is available from the poll it runs; CPU seconds are not, since the bench is not their parent and cannot wait4 them. Reading them may mean a 'ps -o time=' sample per poll, which has 10 ms granularity and would floor a short child at zero. And the phase runs against a private HOME with an unreachable push target, so a measured push is a failed push — a real one costs more.

Acceptance criteria:
The bench reports what the detached children cost, per group, beside the count phase 4 already prints. The method's granularity limit is stated in the output or the docstring where a floored reading could be mistaken for a free process. statusline.py is unchanged, and phase 1, 2 and 4's existing output is unchanged.
closed_reason: Phase 4 prices each detached group, floors and all

title: The push spawn sends only what a prior ccreport run parsed
description:
A day where the ccreport CLI is never run pushes nothing new, while every scheduled push reports success.

push.changed_files reads ccreport_files, and the only writer of that table is ccreport.py's _refresh_changed_files (ccreport.py:542). The status line's detached push spawn never parses a log, so the cache holds no record for the session that is running and the push has nothing to offer.

Observed 2026-08-15 on sbnmbp: push_success stamped 15:52:20 with zero failures, and 51 files holding 3735 records still pending afterwards, spanning 08-14 and all of 08-15. The server's /day/2026-08-15 showed neo alone until a manual ccreport daily (which parsed) followed by push_to sent all 3735.

Fix direction: move the rich-free parse cluster (discover_jsonl_files, parse_jsonl_file, _refresh_changed_files and their helpers) into its own module, as accounts.py was moved for the same reason, and refresh the cache in push.run_once before it reads what is pending.
acceptance: A push spawn with no ccreport run behind it sends the records of a session that is still open; tests cover run_once refreshing the cache first; push.py still imports no rich.

title: Rename a machine from /settings/machines
description:
A machine's display name is set once, at mint time (src/ccreport/server/pages.py:207, tokens.mint). Nothing edits it afterwards, so a machine minted as 'mac-mini-2' is drawn that way forever on the dashboard's machine breakdown, its /machine/<label> detail page and 'ccreport --server URL'. db.upsert_machine already refuses to let a push overwrite the label, so the column is server-owned and free to edit.

Give /settings/machines a Name column with one inline form per row, mirroring /settings/accounts (templates/accounts.html, pages.set_alias): the field holds the current label, saving an empty field goes back to the machine_id, which is what every reader already falls back to (reports.load: labels.get(machine_id, machine_id), pages._machine_page: label or machine_id).

Files: src/ccreport/server/db.py (set_machine_label, content_stamp, machines DDL + MIGRATION_CHAIN), src/ccreport/server/pages.py (POST /settings/machines/{machine_id}/label), src/ccreport/server/templates/machines.html, tests/test_server_pages.py, tests/test_server_db.py, tests/test_dashboard.py.

The one non-obvious part: dashboard.cached_build is keyed on db.content_stamp, which reads ingest_files and account_aliases. A rename has no push behind it, so without a part in that stamp the dashboard keeps drawing the old name until the next machine pushes -- the same reason account_aliases is in there. machines has no updated_at column to hang it on, so this needs a label_updated_at column added through a numbered migrations.Step in db.MIGRATION_CHAIN (currently empty; baseline 3), per the migration rule in AGENTS.md.
acceptance:
- POST /settings/machines/{id}/label sets the label and redirects 303 to /settings/machines
- An empty field clears the label back to the machine_id everywhere it is drawn
- A rename moves db.content_stamp, so dashboard.cached_build rebuilds without a push
- A label on a machine_id nothing was minted for is a 404, as the machine page already is
- just lint-all and just test pass; new route and new db function each have a test
notes: Implemented: machines.label_updated_at (db.py DDL + MIGRATION_CHAIN step 4, tolerant of a fresh database that already has the column), db.set_machine_label, the sixth part of db.content_stamp, POST /settings/machines/{machine_id}/label in pages.py, a Name column and hint in templates/machines.html, and an AGENTS.md bullet. Tests: 6 in TestRenamingAMachine (test_server_pages.py), 3 in TestMachinesAndTokens and 2 in TestContentStamp (test_server_db.py). just lint-all clean, just test 1770 passed.
closed_reason: Rename field shipped on /settings/machines; user confirmed

title: Merge two machines' project names on the server
description:
The dashboard draws one row per project string a machine pushed. The same repo checked out under two names — neo pushes it as project1, mbp as project2 — is two rows, and no server-side rename exists to fold them: reports.project_display (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:60) returns the pushed name verbatim. The two rename tables the server already has are account_aliases and machines.label; neither covers a project.

Add a third, project_aliases, keyed on (machine_id, project) so two machines that use one name for different repos stay separable. Typing the same alias for neo/project1 and mbp/project2 folds them into one row. The client's push policy and the stored records are untouched — an alias renames the view.

Touch points:
- src/ccreport/server/db.py: DDL, project_aliases()/projects_with_alias()/set_project_alias()/project_overview(), a content_stamp part so the dashboard cache rebuilds on a rename, and a MIGRATION_CHAIN step one version above the last.
- src/ccreport/server/reports.py: project_display() takes the machine and the alias map; _clauses() widens the project filter over the aliased (machine, project) pairs, and _dedup_clause repeats it as it repeats every non-date filter.
- src/ccreport/server/pages.py + templates: a /settings/projects page listing every (machine, project) that has pushed, each with a name field, and the POST that writes it.
- AGENTS.md: the alias rules paragraph.
acceptance: Two machines' differently-named projects render as one dashboard row and one /project/<name> page once the same alias is typed for both; the alias also selects those rows when passed as a project filter. A rename rebuilds the dashboard cache without a push. Clearing the field restores the pushed name. just lint-all and just test pass, with tests for every new db function and route.
closed_reason: project_aliases table, /settings/projects page, filter widening and docs; lint and 1849 tests pass

title: Configurable push interval per server in push.toml
description:
The push interval is fixed at 30 minutes: push.py:35 `BASE_INTERVAL_S = 30 * 60`. A fast machine on a wired network can push every 5 minutes and keep the merged view fresh; a mobile machine on a metered link wants 15 minutes or more. The interval is a property of the machine and its link, not of the server, so it belongs in that machine's push.toml entry beside `networks` and `max_body`.

Add a per-server field (suggested `interval_minutes`, an int) to `[server."URL"]`:

- `ServerConfig` (push.py:61) gains the field; `load_config` (push.py:139) parses it, falling back to `BASE_INTERVAL_S` when absent or unparseable. `write_server` and `_toml_value` (push.py:185, 210) already handle ints.
- `due()` (push.py:571) and `next_attempt_at()` (push.py:648) each recompute `min(BASE_INTERVAL_S * (2 ** failures), MAX_INTERVAL_S)` inline. Both must use the configured base, so factor the doubling into one helper both call.
- `MAX_INTERVAL_S` (8 h) is the failure-widening ceiling. A configured base above it must not be clamped below itself: the ceiling is `max(MAX_INTERVAL_S, base)`.
- Give `ccreport server connect` a flag that writes it (cmd_server_connect, ccreport.py:1363; its parser, ccreport.py:2706) so nobody has to hand-edit a 0600 file, and print the interval in `ccreport server status` (ccreport.py:1463) beside `network gate`.
- The status line gates its spawn on the `push_next_at` meta key that push.py writes, so it needs no change — confirm that by reading statusline.py:992 onward.

AGENTS.md lists push.toml's keys as "server, token, restricted, allow, salt, networks"; add the new one there.
acceptance:
- push.toml with `interval_minutes = 5` makes a machine due 5 minutes after the last attempt; an entry without the key still uses 30 minutes.
- One failure doubles the configured interval, not the default one, in both `due()` and `next_attempt_at()`.
- An interval above 8 h is honoured rather than clamped down to MAX_INTERVAL_S.
- A non-integer or non-positive value falls back to the default instead of raising.
- `ccreport server connect` writes the value and `ccreport server status` prints it.
- Tests under tests/test_push.py cover the above; the existing interval tests (tests/test_push.py:316-337, 586-606) still pass.
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.
closed_reason: interval_minutes per server, one widening helper, connect flag and status line

title: Spend leaderboard: ccreport servers push anonymized totals to a shared board
description:
A ccreport server is a terminal today: machines push to it and nothing leaves. This epic adds a second service that several ccreport servers push aggregated totals to, and that ranks those servers by spend.

What crosses the wire: one row per (day, model) carrying input, output, cache-creation and cache-read tokens plus a call count. No project, session, machine, account, cwd or repo. The pushing server's owner types a handle when the token is minted, because nothing in the payload can derive one.

Decisions taken with the user on 2026-08-16:
- Ranking is raw spend, not an efficiency measure.
- One row per pushing server, not per account. A shared server's users stay merged, which also raises the re-identification floor.
- The board is a separate service: its own package, database, migration chain and entry point, living in this repo beside src/ccreport/server/.

Cross-cutting design points the children carry:
- The board prices the counts with its own pricing.py, so one price table ranks every participant and a client with a stale table cannot distort the order.
- A machine pushes old logs late, so a day already sent changes afterwards. Ingest upserts (handle, day, model) rather than appending, and the push watermark is a content stamp rather than a max timestamp.
- day is the pushing machine's calendar day, carried through server_records. The board stores it as received and never re-derives it from an instant.
- Nothing audits the counts. A token proves which server sent a row and no more, so the board shows a handle's join date and day count beside its total.
acceptance: Every child issue is closed and two ccreport servers appear on a board ranked by spend.

title: Leaderboard service skeleton: package, config, database and migration chain
description:
First child of the leaderboard epic (ccreport-3s7z). Nothing else in the epic can start until the package and its database exist.

Create src/ccleaderboard/ beside src/ccreport/, with its own SQLite file, its own FastAPI factory and its own entry point. Model it on src/ccreport/server/ — config.py reading CCLEADERBOARD_* environment variables alone, db.py holding the CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS scripts, factory.py wiring the app, and a just recipe running it under Granian beside the existing 'just serve'.

Schema, minimum:
- participants: handle, token hash, joined_at, last_push_at.
- board_rows: (participant, day, model, input, output, cache_creation, cache_read, calls, cost_usd), unique on (participant, day, model) so ingest can upsert.
- The same migrations.py contract the two existing databases use: a numbered Step appended to MIGRATION_CHAIN, SCHEMA_VERSION as the chain head, and no hand-edit of a shipped entry.

Read AGENTS.md 'Pipeline rules' on migrations before writing the chain, and reuse src/ccreport/migrations.py rather than copying it.
acceptance: The service starts under Granian against an empty database, creates its schema, and a second start re-runs the chain without error. Tests cover the factory and the migration chain head.

title: Leaderboard ingest: upsert a day of counts and price them server-side
description:
Child of the leaderboard epic (ccreport-3s7z). This is the write side of the board.

An authenticated POST carries rows of (day, model, input, output, cache_creation, cache_read, calls). The endpoint validates the shape, rejects any field the payload should not carry, and upserts on (participant, day, model) — a machine pushes old logs late, so a day already sent gains records afterwards and an append would double it.

Pricing is the board's own, not the sender's. Import ccreport's pricing.py and compute cost_usd at ingest, so one price table orders every participant. Follow the rule the ccreport server already keeps: a model with no known price fails the whole request with a reason in the response, never a stored zero, since a zero is a week of money that looks like an idle week. The <...> pseudo-models are the one known zero.

Store day exactly as received. It is the pushing machine's calendar day, and a participant on another clock keeps days that do not line up with the board's own.

Ingest sits outside any network allowlist the pages get, the same split factory.py already makes for the ccreport server: a participant pushes from wherever it is and its token is what admits it.
acceptance: A push of two days upserts idempotently — pushing the same payload twice leaves the row count and the totals unchanged. An unpriced model returns an error naming the model and stores nothing. Tests cover both.

title: Leaderboard participants: handle typed at mint, token issued, join date shown
description:
Child of the leaderboard epic (ccreport-3s7z).

Nothing in the payload identifies a participant — that is the point of the epic — so the handle is typed by a human on the board's mint page and stored beside the token. Model the page and the token handling on src/ccreport/server/tokens.py and pages.py: hash at rest, show the secret once, print the connect line the operator pastes into their ccreport server.

The mint page also prints what the sender will and will not transmit, in the payload's own field names. An operator joining a public board decides on that list, so it belongs where they decide, not only in the docs.

Revoke and delete both apply, with the same split the ccreport server keeps: revoking stamps revoked_at and stops the next push, deleting removes the participant and, through ON DELETE CASCADE, every row it pushed. Which one to reach for is whether the server is still out there.
