Store joined_at and expose it with the participant's day count, because nothing audits the counts and a handle with a large total and three days of history should read as one.
acceptance: Minting produces a working token and a handle on the board. A revoked token is refused by ingest. Deleting a participant removes its board rows. Tests cover mint, revoke, delete and the refusal.

title: Push direction: ccreport server sends its aggregated day/model totals to a leaderboard
description:
Child of the leaderboard epic (ccreport-3s7z). This is the new direction: src/ccreport/server/ has only ever received.

Build the sender inside the ccreport server package. It groups server_records into one row per (day, model) with summed input, output, cache-creation and cache-read tokens and a call count, and drops project, session, machine, account, cwd, repo and every cost column. Group in SQL, the way reports.load_grouped already does, rather than folding records in Python.

Configuration mirrors push.toml: one table per board URL holding the URL, the token and nothing else, at mode 0600, written by a connect subcommand that takes the line the mint page printed. No environment variables.

The watermark cannot be a max timestamp. A machine pushes old logs late, so a day already sent gains records afterwards; key the state on db.content_stamp and resend every day the stamp touched. Store the outcome of each attempt with its reason, as push.write_push_attempt does, and treat a 401 as terminal.

Scheduling is the open question in this issue: a Granian background task inside the running server, or a subcommand the operator puts in cron. Decide with the user before writing it — the server has no scheduler today and adding one is the larger of the two changes.
acceptance: A ccreport server with a board configured sends its grouped totals and the board shows them. A second run after new records resends only the affected days. A 401 stops further attempts. Tests cover the grouping, the redaction (no identifying field present in the payload) and the terminal 401.

title: Leaderboard board pages: ranked by spend, with charts over the same palette
description:
Child of the leaderboard epic (ccreport-3s7z). This is what a visitor opens.

The board ranks participants by summed cost_usd over a range toggle — day, week, month, all time. Each row carries the handle, the spend, the token counts and the join date with the participant's day count beside it, because nothing audits a total.

A participant's own page charts its spend over time and its model mix. Follow the rules the ccreport dashboard already keeps, in AGENTS.md: series colours come from static/palette.js in fixed order so a filter that drops one series repaints nothing else, a seventh series folds into Other, each chart has one scale rather than a shared axis with a toggle, and the chart library is vendored rather than fetched from a CDN so the page draws with no internet.

Link every stylesheet and script through the asset() template global, which stamps the URL with the file mtime — StaticFiles sends no Cache-Control.

Cache the whole-board view per range against a content stamp and the render's local date, as dashboard.cached_build does, since this is the page a browser opens over and over. A participant page is not cached.
acceptance: The board renders three participants in spend order, the range toggle changes the order, and a participant page draws its charts. tests assert no template or asset carries a remote origin.

title: Hide untiered rate-limit windows from the limits table
description:
`ccreport limits` shows window instances whose Tier column reads as absent: their first sample predates the account_events tier columns, so nothing recorded what the account was entitled to while the window filled. Eight of them on this machine — six session windows, one week, one scoped, 2026-08-08 through 2026-08-10 — plus two year-2286 placeholder instances the reader already drops. They carry a peak and a spend with no tier to read either against.

Filter them out of the rendered tables in src/ccreport/ccreport.py. Nothing is deleted: the rows stay in rate_limit_snapshots, and --json keeps printing every instance, which is what makes the early history still reachable.

- A window's tier is attributed at its earliest sample, the rule report_limits already renders by (src/ccreport/ccreport.py:2469): accounts.tier_at(_as_local(inst.first_ts)).
- Select in cmd_limits, before report_limits, so the renderer keeps drawing whatever it is handed.
- Say the count out loud on stderr, the way the implausible-reset note at src/ccreport/ccreport.py:2571 does, and name --json as where the hidden windows are.
- Every recorded window untiered is exit 1 with a note, like the no-samples-match path.
acceptance:
- A bare `ccreport limits` shows only windows with a recorded tier; the footer counts and totals cover the shown set alone
- stderr carries a note counting the hidden windows and naming --json
- --json output is unchanged: every instance, tiered or not
- All windows untiered exits 1 with a note rather than printing empty tables
- pytest coverage for: mixed history, all-untiered history, empty account_events, --json unaffected
- just lint-all and just test pass
notes:
Done in src/ccreport/ccreport.py: _tiered() beside _partial_note, selection in cmd_limits before report_limits. Both stderr notes are gone at the user's request — the untiered windows and the year-2286 placeholders are dropped silently, and stderr carries the three exit-1 reasons alone. Docs section 9.6 updated (the placeholder bullet, the blank-tier paragraph, the Account/Tier row).

Verified: `ccreport limits` prints the tables and nothing else — Session 15, Week 2, Scoped 2, down from 21/3/2. `--json` still lists all 28 instances including the untiered ones.

Tests: TestLimitsUntiered in tests/test_ccreport.py, 5 cases (mixed history, a quiet run, --json unaffected, no-tier-at-all exit 1, an untiered capture). The two placeholder-note tests in TestCmdLimits now assert an empty stderr instead. Two existing tests seed a tiered account event through the new TestCmdLimits._account helper, which _corpus also calls. just lint-all clean, just test 1853 passed.
closed_reason: Untiered windows hidden from the limits tables; --json unchanged

title: Remove the open-window caption from ccreport limits
description:
The caption under each limits table read as shorthand nobody could decode:

  open at 10.0% (2026-08-17 11:56), seen from 0.0%; 38.8 pp/h → 193% by reset 2026-08-17 16:40; 90.0 pp left ≈ $91
  open at 1.0% (2026-08-17 11:46), seen from 0.0%; 10.3 pp/h → 1595% by reset 2026-08-23 22:00; 99.0 pp left ≈ $362

Rewriting it in plain sentences was tried first and the user's answer to the result was that the line is worthless whatever it says: the projection answers a question nobody reading the table asked, and 1595% comes from carrying a rate measured over five minutes across seven days. So the caption goes.

- ccreport._open_note deleted, with _projection, _thinly_watched, _PROJECTION_MIN_FRACTION, WindowInstance.runs_out_at and the three caption formatters (_fmt_when, _fmt_pct, _window_name).
- report_limits loses its now parameter with it — the partial-window caption needs no clock.
- WindowInstance.projected_pct stays: --json carries it as projected_used_pct.
- The partial-window caption (_partial_note) stays. It explains the * in the Peak column, which would otherwise be an unexplained mark.
acceptance:
- No caption under a table for an open window
- The partial-window caption still renders with its *
- --json still carries projected_used_pct
- just lint-all and just test pass
notes:
Done. The tables now end at their footer; the * caption is the only line left under one. src/ccreport/ccreport.py and docs/calculation-reference.md section 9.6 (the 'Below each table' paragraph).

Verified on this machine: `ccreport limits` prints three tables and nothing under them. `ccreport limits --json` still carries projected_used_pct.

Tests: test_an_open_window_gets_no_caption_of_its_own replaces the four caption tests in TestLimitsRendering. just lint-all clean, just test 1850 passed.
closed_reason: Open-window caption removed

title: Delete the orphaned compute_project_rolling_costs
description:
compute_project_rolling_costs (src/ccreport/pricing.py:1305) has no caller in src/ or bin/. The status line was its only one: _merge_cost_data now takes the *_project_cost split from the stored cost summary instead of deriving it on the render thread, and the import is gone from statusline.py.

compute_costs derives the same figures into rolling_proj (pricing.py:1938 writes every {name}_project_cost key), through the same project_scope, the same fingerprint reuse and the same orphan passes, so the standalone walk duplicates logic that runs in the detached --costs-only refresh.

What deleting it touches:
- src/ccreport/pricing.py:1305-1414, plus the reference to it in the compute_costs comment at pricing.py:1789
- tests/test_pricing.py: roughly 30 assertions reach it (lines 921, 929-937, 944-967, 973-985, 1025-1031, 1140-1183, 1212-1225, 1440-1462 and nearby)
- docs/calculation-reference.md section 5.6: the 'Cost computation reads it too' bullet already names compute_costs alone, so no doc line depends on the function

Before deleting, confirm the compute_costs tests cover what only these tests reach: the sibling-prefix rejection (/tmp/proj-other against /tmp/proj), a merge target folding two project directories, orphaned records attributed by project name, and the all_time shortcut for a file written before the widest window opened. Port any case that has no equivalent rather than dropping it.
acceptance: The function is deleted, no src/ reference remains, every project-scoping case it alone covered has a compute_costs test, and just lint-all plus just test pass.
closed_reason: Function deleted; scoping cases now run against compute_costs

title: Warm caches make a rolling window exceed all_time in compute_costs
description:
compute_costs can return a 24h window larger than all_time for the same corpus, when a cached record carries a stored cost that differs from what its tokens price.

Where: src/ccreport/pricing.py:1483, inside _try_cached_file branch 3 (the branch for a file whose file_costs fingerprint and ccreport_files fingerprint both match). It prices each cached record with _rec_cost(), which returns the record's stored cost whenever that is non-zero and only falls back to tokens otherwise. ccreport_records.cost is the log's costUSD verbatim (scan.py:276), so for a log that carried costUSD the rolling windows are filled from costUSD.

Meanwhile all_time, week and month for that same file come from cached_entry, which compute_costs wrote from _scan_jsonl_file -> _line_cost -> calc_cost, i.e. from tokens. The JSONL parse path never reads costUSD at all.

So one call's result is internally inconsistent, and two calls over an unchanged corpus disagree with each other:

- cold (file_costs empty): every file is scanned, everything priced from tokens
- warm (both caches fresh): all_time from tokens, rolling windows from costUSD

Observed while porting a test in ccreport-4lmq: a four-record project totalled all_time 0.07 and twenty_four_hour 1.035 on the warm call, where the cold call gave 0.07 for both. The fixture's cached records carried cost 0.5 each against tokens worth 0.0175.

Repro sketch (see the fixtures in tests/test_pricing.py TestLiveFilesPricedFromTheCcreportCache): write a JSONL file, save_ccreport_file it with a matching (mtime_ns, size) and a record whose stored cost disagrees with its tokens, call compute_costs(cwd=...) twice, compare.

The now-deleted compute_project_rolling_costs used _rec_cost_from_tokens for exactly this case, with the reason in its own comment: the raw path recomputes, so a file still on disk has nothing to lose by recomputing too. The orphan and purged-session paths (pricing.py:1052, 1152, 1234) must keep _rec_cost - there is no file left to re-price from, so the stored cost is the only surviving figure.

Candidate fix: use _rec_cost_from_tokens at pricing.py:1483. Weigh it first: for a corpus whose logs carry costUSD this moves the printed window figures, and costUSD is arguably the biller's own number. The alternative is to make the scan path prefer costUSD too, which changes far more.

Note pricing.py:1440-ish (_orphan_alltime_fingerprint's docstring) states almost no cached record carries a stored cost at all, which is why this has gone unnoticed - Claude Code's current logs appear not to write costUSD.

description.new:
Serve a cache hit entirely from the bash wrapper, so a render costs no Python process at all.

Today every render execs python and goes through src/ccreport/statusline.py, even on the fast path: renders within FAST_TTL_S (15 s) already skip subprocess spawns and db reads by reusing the previous render's fetch results from a per-session temp file, and the wrapper bin/statusline-command_x.sh already skips the uv resolver. Prior measurement on an M-series machine, warm: ~110 ms before those two changes, ~25-30 ms after. What remains is interpreter startup and module import.

Proposal: cache the fully rendered line, with placeholders for the segments that must stay live. bin/statusline-command_x.sh serves that line on a hit and fills the placeholders itself — clock from $EPOCHSECONDS plus printf strftime, ctx% via jq from the stdin JSON. On a miss it falls through to Python as now. Estimated ~10 ms per hit.

Cost, which is why this is priority 3: a second formatting path in bash, and placeholder splicing that has to be kept in sync with the Python renderer whenever a segment's format changes. Only worth doing if ~25-30 ms still bothers us in practice. Requires bash 5 for $EPOCHSECONDS and printf %(fmt)T — /bin/bash is 3.2, so pin the shebang to the Homebrew bash — and jq on PATH.

The code does something else. pricing._encode_session_state stores a versioned JSON blob: a version field, a per-file _FileCursor (mtime_ns, size, offset, tail) and dedup-key digests. pricing._decode_session_state:897 names the md5 shape explicitly as 'the pre-incremental md5 fingerprint' - the legacy form it still reads. A file that grew is resumed from its stored offset and tail digest, not re-parsed from the top.

Why it matters: the doc describes full invalidation where the code does incremental resume. A maintainer chasing a wrong session cost looks for the wrong failure mode, and the real one (a cursor that drifted from the file) is not documented at all.

title.new: Explain the constants a maintainer would tune wrong

description.new:
This tree explains nearly every constant. These are the holes, each judged against its own neighbours in the same file.

1. cache_db.py:535 - PRAGMA cache_size = -2000. The comment explains only why the three pragmas sit outside the version gate, never that the negative sign is SQLite's KiB-versus-pages switch. 'Fixing' it to 2000 means 2000 pages, roughly 8 MB, per connection - on a path the status line opens every render.
2. ccreport.py:121 - CACHE_VERSION = 2 has no bump policy, while cache_db.SCHEMA_VERSION ('BUMP THIS on any change to...') and cache_db.CACHE_SCHEMA_SALT ('Bump this when...') both state theirs. It is also non-obviously not redundant with _script_hash(), which already hashes ccreport.py. So a maintainer either never bumps it or deletes it as dead weight.
3. The 10-minute usage TTL is spelled as a bare literal at four sites with nothing saying they must agree: usage_api.CACHE_MAX_AGE = 600, two max_age: int = 600 defaults in cache_db (:1172, :3044), and statusline.USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S = 600. That is a departure from this tree's rule of deriving key lists from one source and guarding drift with a test. Tuning one leaves the TTL check and the countdown the user reads describing different intervals.
4. statusline.py:125 - COST_SUMMARY_MAX_AGE = 900 is described as how long a cached compute_costs result stays usable, but nothing says it is what actually paces the costs-only refresh (via _fetch_usage's cost_summary is None branch), nor that the 300 s gap from USAGE_FETCH_INTERVAL_S is deliberate. Aligning it to 600 changes how often a detached subprocess rescans the whole JSONL corpus.
5. cache_db.py:1203 - _BACKOFF_SCHEDULE = [45, 120, 240] names the unit and the index but gives no ceiling reasoning. Nothing says the last step must stay under the 600 s fetch interval; past that, one transient failure suppresses fetching indefinitely.
6. cache_db.py:43-44 - _SANITY_DROP_THRESHOLD_PCT = 10.0 and _SANITY_MIN_PRIOR_COUNT = 100 have no comment and are stranded under the legacy-paths block, so they read as belonging to it. The 10% is what decides whether real loss of unrebuildable orphan records gets reported.
7. cache_db.py:1503 - the 31-day snapshot prune. The comment restates the line and leaves 31 unexplained; the deltas this table feeds are the 5 h and 7 d windows, so 31 looks arbitrary. It is there because Extra usage is a monthly quota.

description.new:
src/ccreport/statusline.py _weekly_pace emits a hardcoded /7d in its label - f'{elapsed_str}/7d({cd})' and f'{elapsed_str}/7d' - while the expected percentage it compares against is computed from pricing.pace_days(), which reads CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS and defaults to 7.

- The literal is the real week window and only the delta is paced. Then the label is right and the docstring's {N} placeholder is what is wrong.
- The label should follow the knob. Then the literal should be the pace value, matching what ccu prints.

Found during the comment-cop documentation sweep; the docstring was left alone pending this decision.

description.new:
A DSP verdict of False is memoized for the session id's whole life, but the
verdict only holds for one claude process. `--resume` reuses the session id, so
a session first launched without --dangerously-skip-permissions and restarted
with it never shows the badge.

Chain, in src/ccreport/statusline.py:

- The non-DSP launch writes {"dsp": false} to the per-session memo (_memo_path,
  keyed by session_id in TMPDIR).
- The resumed claude resolves the same memo path.
- _start_dsp_check (:432) returns None when `memoized is not None`, and
  False is not None, so `ps -Aww` never spawns again.
- _collect_dsp returns None, and :2267 falls back to memo.get("dsp", False).

Observed on session 9039cf27-6302-4b0c-8be4-33083d6ee07e, running as
`claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --resume 9039cf27-...` with a memo
holding {"dsp": false}. Running the ancestor walk live from a child of that
session returns True, so detection itself is correct.

Only a True verdict is safe to memoize permanently. A False one needs
invalidating when the ancestor claude process changes.

Workaround: delete the session's .memo.json from TMPDIR.

description.new:
The status line should print a line under the cost-window line when the local ccreport checkout is behind GitHub's master.

Target render, under `24H $14/$417 · 7D $154/$1963 · 30D $154/$10259 · AT $154/$12587`:

    ↑ 12 commits behind · git pull

Decisions taken with the user (2026-08-12):

- No tags, no GitHub releases, no PyPI. master is the release; `version` in pyproject.toml stays a placeholder nobody reads. The unit of 'update available' is a commit.
- The remote state comes from the GitHub REST API, not from git. No fetch, nothing written into the user's .git, and it works when the checkout has no usable remote credentials.
- The check runs twice a day (12 h TTL), from a detached process on the slow render path, never inline. A network call on the render path is the one thing the status line's whole design avoids.

The endpoint is the compare API, which answers ancestry and count in one request:

    GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{local_sha}...master

It returns `status` (behind | ahead | identical | diverged) and `ahead_by`. `status == 'ahead'` means master is ahead of the local commit by `ahead_by` commits, which is the number to render. Unauthenticated the API allows 60 requests per hour per IP; this spends 2 per day.

Children carry the work. Nothing here is implemented yet.

title.new: update_check.py: ask GitHub how far master is ahead of the local commit

description.new:
New module `src/ccreport/update_check.py`, run as a detached subprocess (`python3 -m ccreport.update_check`), never imported by a render.

What it does, in order:

1. Find the checkout root from its own location: `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`. If there is no `.git` directory there, exit 0 and write nothing — the user installed with `uv tool install .` and has no checkout to update.
2. Read the local HEAD SHA. Prefer parsing `.git/HEAD` plus the ref file (and `.git/packed-refs` as fallback) over forking git, so the same helper can serve the render path.
3. Derive owner/repo from `git remote get-url origin` — do not hardcode oroddlokken/ccreport, a fork has its own. Accept both `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` and `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`.
4. GET `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{local_sha}...master` with urllib, `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`, timeout 10 s. Follow the pattern already in `src/ccreport/exchange.py:131`.
5. Write to the `meta` table (`src/ccreport/cache_db.py:55`, helpers `_get_meta` at :3067 and `_set_meta` at :3091): the local SHA it compared, the commits-ahead count, and the epoch stamp of the check.

Failure is silence. A 404 (the local commit is not on GitHub — an unpushed commit, which is the normal state for whoever develops this), a network error, a rate-limit 403, a body that does not parse: write the stamp so the 12 h TTL still advances, write no count, exit 0. Nothing this module does may ever surface as an error on a render.

Storing the local SHA alongside the count is what keeps the render honest: if the user pulls, the render sees its own SHA no longer matches the compared one and suppresses the line until the next check, rather than claiming a stale 'behind'.

Acceptance: tests under `tests/` covering the SSH and HTTPS remote-URL forms, the loose-ref and packed-refs HEAD reads, a mocked 'ahead' response writing the count, and each failure mode writing the stamp but no count.

description.new:
A new module src/ccreport/push.py that reads the local cache and sends new or changed files to the server, plus the two ways it runs.

What it sends: for each file in ccreport_files whose (mtime_ns, size) differs from the local push watermark, that file records with account_uuid and account_label stamped from the account_events log the way ccreport already stamps them at read time (docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), and cost frozen to what each record cost() answered. Two triggers:
- ccreport push [--server URL] [--full], manual, prints what it sent.
- A detached spawn from the statusline slow path, at most one per 30 minutes, gated on a stored stamp the child writes on every outcome including failure, exactly as update_check.py does for its 12-hour interval (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules). title.new: Per-project opt-in on a restricted machine: redact identity, keep usage

description.new:
A work laptop must push complete usage while revealing only the projects the user opted in to. Every record still goes to the server with its model, timestamps, token counts and cost. What a non-allowed record loses is identity: project, cwd and repo.

Configuration lives in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, not in cache.db, so a cache wipe cannot silently unredact a work machine:

  restricted = true
  allow = ["ccreport", "kantine"]
  salt = "<generated once on first run>"

restricted defaults to false. When the file is absent, the machine pushes everything with real names, which is what the two personal machines want. When restricted is true, a project not in allow is redacted. Fail closed: a malformed or unreadable push.toml on a machine that has ever been restricted must redact everything rather than fall back to open. Store the last known restricted state where the parser can see it before it trusts the file.

Names in allow are matched through the identity rules ccreport merge already applies, project_identity.py plus pricing.project_scope() (AGENTS.md), so an alias resolves the same way a report groups it.

Redaction: project becomes a stable pseudonym, the first 8 hex of a hash over the salt and the resolved project name; cwd and repo become null. The salt never leaves the machine, so the server sees work-a1b2 as a durable grouping key it cannot reverse. Session ids of redacted records are hashed with the same salt, so sessions still group without carrying the original id.

Interaction with the push watermark: changing restricted or allow changes what past files should have sent. Store a hash of the effective policy alongside the watermark and force a full re-push when it changes, and have the server replace that machine rows rather than merge them, so a project moved from allow to redacted stops being named on the server.

Acceptance: tests cover an unrestricted machine sending real names, a restricted machine redacting a non-allowed project while its tokens and cost match the source records exactly, an allowed project surviving intact, the same project hashing to the same pseudonym across two runs, a malformed push.toml failing closed, and a policy change forcing a full re-push.

A work laptop must only send stats while it is on the office network. The gate is evaluated before every push, manual and spawned alike, and a machine that fails it does nothing and records nothing.

Test: some local interface holds an address inside one of the configured CIDRs. Stdlib only, no packets, using socket and ipaddress so the statusline spawn stays cheap; do not probe the server to decide. A VPN that hands out an address in the range counts as being on the network, which is the intended behaviour.

Configuration in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, keyed per server URL alongside the restricted and allow keys from ccreport-55s6:

  [server."https://ccreport.example.net"]
  networks = ["10.172.0.0/22"]
  restricted = true
  allow = ["ccreport"]

An absent or empty networks list means no gate, which is what the personal machines want. A malformed CIDR must fail closed for that server, not be skipped: a typo in a work laptop config must never turn into pushing from a hotel wifi.

Interaction with the push watermark (ccreport-2r5m): a blocked push writes no watermark and no failure stamp beyond the 30-minute interval stamp, so everything queued simply goes out on the first run back inside the network. Nothing is lost by being off-network for a week.

ccreport push run by hand while off-network prints which server was skipped and which CIDRs it wanted, so the silence is explained rather than mysterious.

Acceptance: tests cover an interface inside the CIDR passing, every interface outside it blocking with no request sent, an absent networks key allowing the push, a malformed CIDR blocking, IPv6 handled or explicitly refused, and a queued file going out on the first allowed run.

title.new: Network gate: push only from an allowed CIDR

title: Network gate: push only from an allowed CIDR

description.old:
A work laptop must push complete usage while revealing only the projects the user opted in to. Every record still goes to the server with its model, timestamps, token counts and cost. What a non-allowed record loses is identity: project, cwd and repo.

Configuration lives in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, not in cache.db, so a cache wipe cannot silently unredact a work machine:

  restricted = true
  allow = ["ccreport", "kantine"]
  salt = "<generated once on first run>"

restricted defaults to false. When the file is absent, the machine pushes everything with real names, which is what the two personal machines want. When restricted is true, a project not in allow is redacted. Fail closed: a malformed or unreadable push.toml on a machine that has ever been restricted must redact everything rather than fall back to open. Store the last known restricted state where the parser can see it before it trusts the file.

Names in allow are matched through the identity rules ccreport merge already applies, project_identity.py plus pricing.project_scope() (AGENTS.md), so an alias resolves the same way a report groups it.

Redaction: project becomes a stable pseudonym, the first 8 hex of a hash over the salt and the resolved project name; cwd and repo become null. The salt never leaves the machine, so the server sees work-a1b2 as a durable grouping key it cannot reverse. Session ids of redacted records are hashed with the same salt, so sessions still group without carrying the original id.

Interaction with the push watermark: changing restricted or allow changes what past files should have sent. Store a hash of the effective policy alongside the watermark and force a full re-push when it changes, and have the server replace that machine rows rather than merge them, so a project moved from allow to redacted stops being named on the server.

Acceptance: tests cover an unrestricted machine sending real names, a restricted machine redacting a non-allowed project while its tokens and cost match the source records exactly, an allowed project surviving intact, the same project hashing to the same pseudonym across two runs, a malformed push.toml failing closed, and a policy change forcing a full re-push.

title: Per-project opt-in on a restricted machine: redact identity, keep usage

description.old:
Goal: an HTTP server in this repo that receives the full record stream from every machine and merges it, so one report covers machine 1 on account A, machine 2 on account B, and one person running Claude Code on several machines.

Decisions taken with the user, not to be relitigated:
- Payload: full ccreport_records rows, not rollups.
- Read surface: server-side CLI. ccreport renders tables the server computed. Remote records are NOT mirrored into the local cache.db.
- Auth: one shared bearer token over HTTPS. The server binds a machine_id to the first client that used it and refuses a later push claiming it from a different client fingerprint, so a leaked token can add rows but cannot rewrite an existing machine history.
- Pricing: the server re-prices on ingest. Clients send token counts and the model id; the server computes cost with its own pricing.py, passing through only a cost the session log itself carried. One pricing source, so a machine that has not pulled cannot write wrong money into the merged history.
- Duplicates: every machine copy is stored. Reports collapse records by dedup key and attribute each to the machine that first reported it, so a synced home directory neither double-counts nor silently erases one machine contribution.
- Stack: FastAPI plus Granian, in this repo, following ~/git/kantine (src/km2/web/factory.py app factory, src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py Granian entry point, src/km2/web/middleware.py dependency-style access control).
- Push trigger: both. A detached spawn from the statusline slow path at most every 30 minutes, plus a manual ccreport push.
- Restricted machines: per-project opt-in with identity redaction, child issue ccreport-55s6.

Constraints the existing code imposes:
- ccreport_records (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) carries neither account nor machine. Account comes from the account_events change log at read time (AGENTS.md, docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), so the push client stamps account and machine onto each record before sending.
- statusline.py imports nothing outside the stdlib and must keep doing so. The pusher is a separate detached process, like usage_api.py and update_check.py, and it opens cache.db read-only, taking a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged.

Children: server package and schema, ingest endpoint and auth, push client, aggregation refactor, read-side CLI, restricted-machine redaction.

title: ccreport server: merge records from many machines and accounts

description.old:
Server endpoints that aggregate, plus the CLI flag that renders them.

Server: GET /v1/report/{day,month,project,session,account} taking the same filters the CLI already offers, running the aggregation extracted by the refactor issue over server_records, and returning rows as JSON. Every response also breaks down by machine and by account, since that is the whole point of merging: one row set that says which machine and which account each number came from.

Client: ccreport --server URL <report> fetches those rows and renders them through the existing rich builders, so a merged report looks like a local one. Without --server, nothing about the local path changes.

Open points to settle while implementing:
- NOK conversion: exchange.py converts each record at its own Oslo-date rate. Decide whether the server converts (it needs the exchange_rates table and network) or returns USD and the client converts. Prefer server-side, so two clients cannot disagree.
- Project grouping: ccreport merge rules live in project_overrides on each client. Decide whether the server stores its own rules or the client sends resolved project names. Prefer resolving on the client at push time and treating the server name as final, so a merged report does not depend on which laptop asked.

Acceptance: tests spin the app with a seeded server database holding two machines and two accounts, and assert each report groups and totals correctly across both; a client test asserts rendering from a canned server response.

title: Read side: ccreport --server renders the merged reports

description.old:
A new module src/ccreport/push.py that reads the local cache and sends new or changed files to the server, plus the two ways it runs.

What it sends: for each file in ccreport_files whose (mtime_ns, size) differs from the local push watermark, that file records with account_uuid and account_label stamped from the account_events log the way ccreport already stamps them at read time (docs/calculation-reference.md section 9). Send token counts and the model id, and a cost only where the session log itself carried one: the server prices everything else, so no client can write wrong money into the merged history. Chunk by record count so no request trips the server body limit.

Cache access: open cache.db read-only, buffer what the batch needs, and take a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged. A render must never wait on this process, and a long-held lock on cache.db is what makes it wait.

Local state: a push_state table in cache.db keyed by (server_url, file_path) holding the acknowledged (mtime_ns, size), plus a last_push_ts meta key per server URL. Never assume a push landed; write the watermark from the server response, and leave a rejected file unrecorded so the next run retries it.

Machine identity: a uuid generated once and stored in the cache meta table, with the hostname sent alongside as a human label and a client fingerprint the server binds on first push. Hostnames change and collide across networks; the uuid is what rows key on.

Two triggers:
- ccreport push [--server URL] [--full], manual, prints what it sent, skipped and had rejected.
- A detached spawn from the statusline slow path, at most one per 30 minutes, gated on a stored stamp the child writes on every outcome including failure, exactly as update_check.py does for its 12-hour interval (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules). The status line must not import push.py: it spawns the same way it spawns usage_api.py.

Configuration: server URL and token from environment variables. Absent means no push and no spawn, so a machine that has not opted in pays nothing.

Acceptance: tests cover the watermark skip, the changed-file resend, a rejected file being retried, the chunking boundary, account stamping, the read-only open, and the 30-minute gate holding when the stamp is fresh. A statusline render with no server configured must spawn nothing; assert it.

title: Push client: ccreport push, plus a 30-minute detached spawn from the statusline

description.old:
POST /v1/ingest accepting one machine batch: machine_id, hostname, client fingerprint, ccreport client version, and a list of files, each with path, mtime_ns, size and its records. A record is the ccreport_records field set (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) plus account_uuid and account_label. The client sends token counts and the model id; it sends a cost only when the session log itself carried one.

Behaviour:
- Reject a batch whose Authorization header is not Bearer plus the configured shared token, with 401 and no detail. Auth is a FastAPI dependency, the shape ~/git/kantine uses at src/km2/web/middleware.py:33.
- Price every record at ingest with the server pricing.py. A model id the server does not know must fail the file loudly and be reported in the response, never stored as zero: a silent zero is a week of money that looks like an idle week.
- Bind machine_id to the client fingerprint on first sight. A push claiming a known machine_id with a different fingerprint gets 409 and writes nothing, so one leaked token cannot rewrite another machine history.
- A file whose (mtime_ns, size) already matches ingest_files is skipped and reported as skipped, so the client can stop resending it.
- A file that changed replaces its rows in one transaction: delete by (machine_id, file_path), insert the batch. A JSONL only ever grows, but a rotated or truncated log must not leave stale rows. Deletes are scoped to the pushing machine and never touch another machine copy of the same synced log.
- Respond with per-file accepted, skipped or rejected plus record counts, so the push client updates its watermark from what the server stored rather than from what it hoped.
- Bound the request body size and return 413 above it. A full first push from a machine with 98k records must therefore be chunked by the client.

GET /v1/health returns version and record count without auth.

Acceptance: pytest tests using fastapi TestClient cover a good push, a wrong token, a fingerprint mismatch, an unknown model id, a re-push of an unchanged file, a re-push of a grown file, a second machine pushing the same log path, and an oversized body.

title: Ingest endpoint and shared bearer token auth

description.old:
Create src/ccreport/server/ holding the FastAPI app and its own SQLite database, separate from ~/.cache/ccreport/cache.db. The client cache stays a per-machine artifact; the server database is the merged one.

Follow ~/git/kantine: an app factory create_app() (src/km2/web/factory.py), a Granian entry point taking host/port/workers (src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py), and a justfile recipe. Add fastapi and granian with uv add, so uv.lock records them. Keep them out of the status line import path: statusline.py must still import stdlib only.

Schema, in a new module mirroring cache_db.py style (one column tuple driving SELECT, INSERT and row mapping, as _CCR_FIELD_COLS does at src/ccreport/cache_db.py:1938):
- machines(machine_id PK, hostname, client_fingerprint, first_seen, last_seen). client_fingerprint is recorded on the first push under that machine_id and is what a later push must match, since one shared token cannot tell two clients apart.
- server_records: the ccreport_records columns plus machine_id, account_uuid, account_label, day and oslo_date computed at ingest, and cost NOT NULL, computed by the server at ingest from pricing.py rather than taken from the client. Keep the client-sent log cost in its own column so a log-provided cost stays distinguishable from a computed one.
- ingest_files(machine_id, file_path, mtime_ns, size, n_records, updated_at) so a re-push of an unchanged file is a no-op and a re-push of a grown file replaces that file rows.
- No unique constraint on the dedup key: two machines pushing the same synced log both keep their rows. Index (account_uuid, dk) so read-time dedup can collapse them and attribute each record to the machine that first reported it.

Configuration by environment variable, no config library: database path, bind address, port, and the shared token (the token itself belongs to ccreport-23zb).

Acceptance: just lint-all and just test pass; a test creates the schema in a tmp_path database and asserts the column tuple matches the CREATE TABLE, as tests/test_the_record_dict_matches_the_column_tuple does today.

title: Server package: FastAPI factory, Granian entry, merged SQLite schema

description.new:
A small server-rendered web interface whose one job is machine credentials: list machines, mint a token for a new one, revoke a token, rename a machine.

Pages:
- Machines: machine label, machine_id, last seen, record count, and whether its token is active or revoked. This is what answers the question the page will actually be opened for, which is whether that laptop is still reporting.
- Mint: name the machine, submit, and the new token is shown once. It is stored hashed, so it cannot be shown again; a lost token is re-minted, never recovered.
- Revoke: one action per token, effective immediately on the next push.

Access control: IP allowlist, no password. Allowed networks come from an environment variable, and the check is a FastAPI dependency, the shape ~/git/kantine uses at src/km2/web/middleware.py:33. The ingest endpoint keeps its own token auth and is NOT behind the allowlist: machines push from wherever they are. Anyone on an allowed network can mint, which is the accepted trade.

Tokens: 32 random bytes from secrets.token_urlsafe, stored as a hash with the machine_id it belongs to, created_at, last_used_at and revoked_at. Ingest looks a presented token up by hash and takes the machine_id from the row, so a machine can only ever write its own rows and the client fingerprint binding is unnecessary.

Rendering: server-rendered HTML with Jinja templates, the way ~/git/kantine does it. No JavaScript build step and no client framework for four pages of tables and two forms.

Acceptance: tests cover minting producing a token that ingest accepts, the token being unrecoverable from the database after minting, revocation causing 401 on the next push, a request from a disallowed address getting 403 on every UI route, and ingest still working from a disallowed address.

title.new: ccreport server connect: one command configures a machine

description.new:
One command sets up a machine end to end:

  ccreport server connect https://ccreport.example.net --token <minted> [--opt-in-repos ccreport,kantine] [--only-on-network 10.172.0.0/22]

It writes ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml at mode 0600, one table per server URL holding token, restricted, allow, salt and networks. Re-running for the same URL updates that table in place and leaves other servers untouched. This file replaces the environment variables the earlier issues assumed: server URL and token now live here with the policy they govern.

Flags:
- --token, the value minted by the web UI (ccreport-4e9p). connect calls /v1/health with it and refuses to write anything on 401, so a mistyped token fails now rather than silently at a background push 30 minutes later. Refuse to write if the config directory is group- or world-writable.
- --opt-in-repos, a comma-separated list. It sets restricted = true and seeds allow with those projects. Opt-in is per project: every project not named pushes its token counts and cost with project, cwd, repo and session id stripped, per ccreport-55s6. Passing the flag with an empty list is a valid work-laptop state, meaning nothing is identified at all. Names resolve through project_identity.py plus pricing.project_scope(), so an alias matches the way ccreport merge groups it. Generate the redaction salt here when restricted is first set.
- --only-on-network, a comma-separated CIDR list for the gate in ccreport-1ley. Omitted means no gate.

Two companions, because a config you can only rewrite wholesale is a config people edit by hand and get wrong:
- ccreport server allow <project> and ccreport server deny <project>, adding to or removing from the allow list and forcing the re-push that a policy change requires.
- ccreport server status, printing the configured servers, the machine name the server knows this machine as, the restricted state, the allowed projects, the CIDR gate and when the last push landed.

Acceptance: tests cover a fresh write, a re-run updating one server and leaving a second intact, file mode 0600, refusal on a bad token, refusal on a world-writable directory, --opt-in-repos setting restricted with the named projects resolved through an override rule, an empty opt-in list, allow and deny forcing a re-push, and status output on a machine that has never pushed.

description.old:
POST /v1/ingest accepting one machine batch: machine_id, hostname, client fingerprint, ccreport client version, and a list of files, each with path, mtime_ns, size and its records. A batch carries whole files only. A record is the ccreport_records field set (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) plus account_uuid and account_label, with the project name already resolved by the client. The client sends token counts and the model id; it sends a cost only when the session log itself carried one.

Behaviour:
- Reject a batch whose Authorization header is not Bearer plus the configured shared token, with 401 and no detail. Auth is a FastAPI dependency, the shape ~/git/kantine uses at src/km2/web/middleware.py:33.
- Price every record at ingest with the server pricing.py, and convert with the server exchange.py at each record own Oslo date. A model id the server does not know must fail the file loudly and be reported in the response, never stored as zero: a silent zero is a week of money that looks like an idle week.
- Bind machine_id to the client fingerprint on first sight. A push claiming a known machine_id with a different fingerprint gets 409 and writes nothing, so one leaked token cannot rewrite another machine history.
- A file whose (mtime_ns, size) already matches ingest_files is skipped and reported as skipped, so the client can stop resending it.
- A file that changed replaces its rows in one transaction: delete by (machine_id, file_path), insert the records that arrived in the same request. Because a request never carries part of a file, no crash can leave the delete committed without its re-insert. A JSONL only ever grows, but a rotated or truncated log must not leave stale rows. Deletes are scoped to the pushing machine and never touch another machine copy of the same synced log.
- Respond with per-file accepted, skipped or rejected plus record counts, so the push client updates its watermark from what the server stored rather than from what it hoped.
- Bound the request body size and return 413 above it, naming the limit in the response so a client with one oversized log can report it rather than retry forever.

GET /v1/health returns version and record count without auth.

Acceptance: pytest tests using fastapi TestClient cover a good push, a wrong token, a fingerprint mismatch, an unknown model id, a re-push of an unchanged file, a re-push of a grown file, a truncated file leaving no stale rows, a second machine pushing the same log path, and an oversized body.

description.old:
A new module src/ccreport/push.py that reads the local cache and sends new or changed files to the server, plus the two ways it runs.

What it sends: for each file in ccreport_files whose (mtime_ns, size) differs from the local push watermark, that file records with account_uuid and account_label stamped from the account_events log the way ccreport already stamps them at read time (docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), and the project name already resolved through this machine project_overrides and pricing.project_scope(). The server treats that name as final and holds no merge rules of its own; a ccreport merge run therefore changes what past files should have sent, so fold the override rules into the policy hash that forces a full re-push in ccreport-55s6.

Send token counts and the model id, and a cost only where the session log itself carried one: the server prices everything else, so no client can write wrong money into the merged history.

Batching: a request carries whole files only, never part of one, so the server delete-then-insert for a file is always one transaction and a crashed push can never leave a committed delete with a partial re-insert. Pack as many whole files per request as the body limit allows. A single log too large for the limit is the one case needing a staged upload; treat it as a follow-up rather than the default path.

Cache access: open cache.db read-only, buffer what the batch needs, and take a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged. A render must never wait on this process, and a long-held lock on cache.db is what makes it wait.

Local state: a push_state table in cache.db keyed by (server_url, file_path) holding the acknowledged (mtime_ns, size), plus per-server meta keys for the last attempt and the consecutive failure count. Never assume a push landed; write the watermark from the server response, and leave a rejected file unrecorded so the next run retries it.

Machine identity: a uuid generated once and stored in the cache meta table, with the hostname sent alongside as a human label and a client fingerprint the server binds on first push. Hostnames change and collide across networks; the uuid is what rows key on.

Two triggers:
- ccreport push [--server URL] [--full], manual, prints what it sent, skipped and had rejected.
- A detached spawn from the statusline slow path, base interval 30 minutes. The child writes the attempt stamp on every outcome including failure and a blocked network gate, exactly as update_check.py does for its 12-hour interval (AGENTS.md, Pipeline rules), and widens the interval on consecutive failures up to a cap, resetting to the base on the first success. A server down overnight must not be probed 20 times. The status line must not import push.py: it spawns the same way it spawns usage_api.py.

Configuration: server URL and token from environment variables. Absent means no push and no spawn, so a machine that has not opted in pays nothing.

title: Ingest endpoint and per-machine token auth

description.old:
Goal: an HTTP server in this repo that receives the full record stream from every machine and merges it, so one report covers machine 1 on account A, machine 2 on account B, and one person running Claude Code on several machines.

Decisions taken with the user, not to be relitigated:
- Payload: full ccreport_records rows, not rollups. A request carries whole files only, never part of one, so every ingest transaction covers a complete file.
- Read surface: server-side CLI. ccreport renders tables the server computed. Remote records are NOT mirrored into the local cache.db.
- Auth: one shared bearer token over HTTPS. The server binds a machine_id to the first client that used it and refuses a later push claiming it from a different client fingerprint, so a leaked token can add rows but cannot rewrite an existing machine history.
- Pricing: the server re-prices on ingest. Clients send token counts and the model id; the server computes cost with its own pricing.py, passing through only a cost the session log itself carried. One pricing source, so a machine that has not pulled cannot write wrong money into the merged history.
- Currency: the server converts, owning exchange.py and its own exchange_rates table, each record at its own Oslo-date rate. Two laptops asking the same question get the same number.
- Grouping: the client resolves the project name through its own ccreport merge rules before pushing, and the server treats the pushed name as final. A merged report does not depend on which laptop asked.
- Duplicates: every machine copy is stored. Reports collapse records by dedup key and attribute each to the machine that first reported it, so a synced home directory neither double-counts nor silently erases one machine contribution.
- Stack: FastAPI plus Granian, in this repo, following ~/git/kantine (src/km2/web/factory.py app factory, src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py Granian entry point, src/km2/web/middleware.py dependency-style access control).
- Push trigger: both. A detached spawn from the statusline slow path at most every 30 minutes, plus a manual ccreport push. The child writes an attempt stamp on every outcome and widens the interval on consecutive failures, so an unreachable server costs one process per interval rather than one per render.
- Restricted machines: per-project opt-in with identity redaction (ccreport-55s6) and a CIDR gate on pushing at all (ccreport-1ley).

Constraints the existing code imposes:
- ccreport_records (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) carries neither account nor machine. Account comes from the account_events change log at read time (AGENTS.md, docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), so the push client stamps account and machine onto each record before sending.
- statusline.py imports nothing outside the stdlib and must keep doing so. The pusher is a separate detached process, like usage_api.py and update_check.py, and it opens cache.db read-only, taking a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged.

Children: server package and schema, ingest endpoint and auth, push client, aggregation refactor, read-side CLI, restricted-machine redaction, network gate.

title: ccreport server: merge records from many machines and accounts

description.old:
A work laptop must push complete usage while revealing only the projects the user opted in to. Every record still goes to the server with its model, timestamps and token counts, and the server prices it as usual. What a non-allowed record loses is identity: project, cwd and repo.

Configuration lives in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, not in cache.db, so a cache wipe cannot silently unredact a work machine. Keys are per server URL, the same table the network gate in ccreport-1ley uses:

  [server."https://ccreport.example.net"]
  restricted = true
  allow = ["ccreport", "kantine"]
  salt = "<generated once on first run>"

restricted defaults to false. When the file is absent, the machine pushes everything with real names, which is what the two personal machines want. When restricted is true, a project not in allow is redacted. Fail closed: a malformed or unreadable push.toml on a machine that has ever been restricted must redact everything rather than fall back to open. Store the last known restricted state where the parser can see it before it trusts the file.

Names in allow are matched through the identity rules ccreport merge already applies, project_identity.py plus pricing.project_scope() (AGENTS.md), so an alias resolves the same way a report groups it.

Redaction: project becomes a stable pseudonym, the first 8 hex of a hash over the salt and the resolved project name; cwd and repo become null. The salt never leaves the machine, so the server sees work-a1b2 as a durable grouping key it cannot reverse. Session ids of redacted records are hashed with the same salt, so sessions still group without carrying the original id.

Interaction with the push watermark: changing restricted or allow changes what past files should have sent. Store a hash of the effective policy alongside the watermark and force a full re-push when it changes, so a project moved from allow to redacted stops being named on the server.

Acceptance: tests cover an unrestricted machine sending real names, a restricted machine redacting a non-allowed project while its token counts match the source records exactly, an allowed project surviving intact, the same project hashing to the same pseudonym across two runs, a malformed push.toml failing closed, and a policy change forcing a full re-push.

title: Per-project opt-in on a restricted machine: redact identity, keep usage

description.old:
A work laptop must only send stats while it is on the office network. The gate is evaluated before every push, manual and spawned alike, and a machine that fails it does nothing and records nothing.

Test: some local interface holds an address inside one of the configured CIDRs. Stdlib only, no packets, using socket and ipaddress so the statusline spawn stays cheap; do not probe the server to decide. A VPN that hands out an address in the range counts as being on the network, which is the intended behaviour.

Configuration in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, keyed per server URL alongside the restricted and allow keys from ccreport-55s6:

  [server."https://ccreport.example.net"]
  networks = ["10.172.0.0/22"]
  restricted = true
  allow = ["ccreport"]

An absent or empty networks list means no gate, which is what the personal machines want. A malformed CIDR must fail closed for that server, not be skipped: a typo in a work laptop config must never turn into pushing from a hotel wifi.

Interaction with the push watermark (ccreport-2r5m): a blocked push writes no watermark and no failure stamp beyond the 30-minute interval stamp, so everything queued simply goes out on the first run back inside the network. Nothing is lost by being off-network for a week.

ccreport push run by hand while off-network prints which server was skipped and which CIDRs it wanted, so the silence is explained rather than mysterious.

Acceptance: tests cover an interface inside the CIDR passing, every interface outside it blocking with no request sent, an absent networks key allowing the push, a malformed CIDR blocking, IPv6 handled or explicitly refused, and a queued file going out on the first allowed run.

A VPN that hands out an address in the range counts as being on the network, which is the intended behaviour.

Configuration is the networks key in ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml, keyed per server URL and written by ccreport server connect --only-on-network (ccreport-xx2g):

  [server."https://ccreport.example.net"]
  networks = ["10.172.0.0/22"]

An absent or empty networks list means no gate, which is what the personal machines want. A malformed CIDR must fail closed for that server, not be skipped: a typo in a work laptop config must never turn into pushing from a hotel wifi.

Interaction with the push watermark (ccreport-2r5m): a blocked push writes no watermark, so everything queued goes out on the first run back inside the network. It does write the attempt stamp, so a machine that is off-network all day spawns one process per interval rather than one per render. Nothing is lost by being away for a week.

ccreport push run by hand while off-network prints which server was skipped and which CIDRs it wanted, and ccreport server status shows the same, so the silence is explained rather than mysterious.

Acceptance: tests cover an interface inside the CIDR passing, every interface outside it blocking with no request sent, an absent networks key allowing the push, a malformed CIDR blocking, IPv6 handled or explicitly refused, and a queued file going out on the first allowed run.

title.new: Dashboard: merged spend view in the web UI

description.new:
The reference the user chose is the T3 Code usage view: a dark page whose header carries the date range and 7/30/90-day toggles, a left column of source rows with cost, share bar and token count, a daily area chart toggling cost against tokens, a five-tile stat strip where each tile carries a derived subline, and a breakdown table that switches dimension.

Adapted to what this server holds:

- Header: date range label, 7/30/90-day toggles, refresh.
- Headline: total cost in USD, large, with NOK in the subline. Keep the reference footnote idea and say plainly that the figure is what the tokens would cost at full API rates, since the accounts here are subscriptions and that number is not an invoice.
- Left column: one row per account, personal and work, each with cost, a share bar, its percentage of total cost and its token count. Machines are a column in the breakdown table, not rows here.
- Chart: daily cost with a cost/tokens toggle and one series per account, legend entries filtering the chart. Drawn with uPlot vendored as a file under the server static directory, not a CDN, so the page works on a laptop with no internet. - Stat tiles, five, each with the derived subline that makes it worth reading: processed tokens (per active day), cached input (share of observed input), uncached input (cache writes), output, and cache savings (what those cache reads would have cost at the uncached input price, expressed as a multiple of the raw token cost). cache_read and cache_create are already columns on every record, so all five come from the same aggregation.

title: Dashboard: merged spend view in the web UI

description.old:
A small server-rendered web interface whose one job is machine credentials: list machines, mint a token for a new one, revoke a token, rename a machine.

Pages:
- Machines: machine label, machine_id, last seen, record count, and whether its token is active or revoked. This is what answers the question the page will actually be opened for, which is whether that laptop is still reporting.
- Mint: name the machine, submit, and the new token is shown once. It is stored hashed, so it cannot be shown again; a lost token is re-minted, never recovered.
- Revoke: one action per token, effective immediately on the next push.

Access control: IP allowlist, no password. Allowed networks come from an environment variable, and the check is a FastAPI dependency, the shape ~/git/kantine uses at src/km2/web/middleware.py:33. The ingest endpoint keeps its own token auth and is NOT behind the allowlist: machines push from wherever they are. Anyone on an allowed network can mint, which is the accepted trade.

Tokens: 32 random bytes from secrets.token_urlsafe, stored as a hash with the machine_id it belongs to, created_at, last_used_at and revoked_at. Ingest looks a presented token up by hash and takes the machine_id from the row, so a machine can only ever write its own rows and the client fingerprint binding is unnecessary.

Rendering: server-rendered HTML with Jinja templates, the way ~/git/kantine does it. No JavaScript build step and no client framework for four pages of tables and two forms.

Acceptance: tests cover minting producing a token that ingest accepts, the token being unrecoverable from the database after minting, revocation causing 401 on the next push, a request from a disallowed address getting 403 on every UI route, and ingest still working from a disallowed address.

title: Web interface: machines and minted per-machine tokens

description.old:
Goal: an HTTP server in this repo that receives the full record stream from every machine and merges it, so one report covers machine 1 on account A, machine 2 on account B, and one person running Claude Code on several machines.

Decisions taken with the user, not to be relitigated:
- Payload: full ccreport_records rows, not rollups. A request carries whole files only, never part of one, so every ingest transaction covers a complete file.
- Read surface: server-side CLI. ccreport renders tables the server computed. Remote records are NOT mirrored into the local cache.db.
- Auth: one token per machine, minted in the web UI, stored hashed, shown once. Ingest takes the machine_id from the token row, so a machine can only write its own rows and a revoked laptop stops writing on its next push. There is no shared token.
- Web UI: machines and tokens only, server-rendered, reachable from an IP allowlist with no password. Ingest is not behind that allowlist, since machines push from anywhere.
- Setup: ccreport server connect <url> --token <minted> [--opt-in-repos ...] [--only-on-network ...] writes ~/.config/ccreport/push.toml at mode 0600. That file holds the server, the token and the policy; there are no environment variables for any of it.
- Pricing: the server re-prices on ingest. Clients send token counts and the model id; the server computes cost with its own pricing.py, passing through only a cost the session log itself carried. One pricing source, so a machine that has not pulled cannot write wrong money into the merged history.
- Currency: the server converts, owning exchange.py and its own exchange_rates table, each record at its own Oslo-date rate.
- Grouping: the client resolves the project name through its own ccreport merge rules before pushing, and the server treats the pushed name as final.
- Duplicates: every machine copy is stored. Reports collapse records by dedup key and attribute each to the machine that first reported it, so a synced home directory neither double-counts nor silently erases one machine contribution.
- Stack: FastAPI plus Granian, in this repo, following ~/git/kantine (src/km2/web/factory.py app factory, src/km2/web/fastapi_server.py Granian entry point, src/km2/web/middleware.py dependency-style access control).
- Push trigger: both. A detached spawn from the statusline slow path at a base 30 minutes, plus a manual ccreport push. The child writes an attempt stamp on every outcome and widens the interval on consecutive failures, so an unreachable server costs one process per interval rather than one per render.
- Restricted machines: opt-in per project. A project not opted in still pushes its token counts and cost, with project, cwd, repo and session id stripped (ccreport-55s6), and the machine pushes at all only from an allowed CIDR (ccreport-1ley).

Constraints the existing code imposes:
- ccreport_records (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:139) carries neither account nor machine. Account comes from the account_events change log at read time (AGENTS.md, docs/calculation-reference.md section 9), so the push client stamps the account onto each record before sending; the machine comes from the token.
- statusline.py imports nothing outside the stdlib and must keep doing so. The pusher is a separate detached process, like usage_api.py and update_check.py, and it opens cache.db read-only, taking a write transaction only to record the watermark the server acknowledged.

Children: server package and schema, ingest and token auth, web UI and minting, connect command, push client, aggregation refactor, read-side CLI, restricted-machine redaction, network gate.

description.new:
ccu compares usage against the clock and stops there: pace_line (src/ccreport/ccu.py:213) renders "6d 5h into 7-day window (pace: 5d) - 70%% expected, +8%%". Nothing says when the quota actually runs out at the current rate, which is what Claude Code Usage Monitor gives people and the reason they run it.

Data: rate_limit_snapshots (src/ccreport/cache_db.py:309), appended by slow-path status line renders from the live percentages, holds (ts, window, model, percent, resets_at). ccreport limits already reads it, grouping by (window, model, resets_at). The burn rate is the slope of percent against ts inside the current window instance.

Compute: fit the slope over the current window instance only, weighting recent snapshots, and project to 100%%. Report one of two outcomes, both concrete:
- Reaching 100%% before the reset: name the clock time it lands and how long before the reset that is.
- Resetting first: say so, since that is the answer people actually want.

Degradation matters more than precision here. An unobserved window leaves no history (AGENTS.md), and a window with one snapshot supports no slope at all. Under two snapshots, or a slope that is flat or negative, print nothing rather than extrapolate a number that will be wrong in an obvious way. A window whose sampling started late is already flagged in the schema; do not project across that gap as if it were observed.

Surfaces:
- ccu: one line under the existing pace line, in the same section as the bar it describes.
- Status line: a segment behind its own toggle in the env-var table, reading the same snapshots on the slow path only. It must not add a fetch, and it must not import anything new at module level.

Acceptance: tests cover a steady rise projecting a sensible time, a flat slope printing nothing, a single snapshot printing nothing, a projection past the reset saying so, and a late-started window not being extrapolated across its gap. The status line toggle off must render byte-identically to today.

title.new: Burn-rate exhaustion ETA for the rate-limit windows

title: Burn-rate exhaustion ETA for the rate-limit windows

description.new:
Project spend forward and show it against a ceiling. Display only: nothing notifies, nothing changes colour, no threshold machinery. The number is the feature.

Three horizons, each projected from the same record stream:
- Calendar month. Month-to-date extrapolated to month end. Early in the month one heavy day dominates, so weight recent days rather than dividing the total by days elapsed.
- Billing month. The same projection anchored to the subscription renewal day instead of the first, because that is the period the money is actually settled over. Check whether the usage API response carries a renewal date before adding configuration for it; if it does not, the renewal day is configured per account.
- Rate-limit windows. Projected cost for the current session and week windows, using pricing.ROLLING_WINDOWS and the window bounds the status line already tracks. This is the money counterpart of ccreport-o76s, which projects the quota percentage; the two answer different questions and neither replaces the other.

Ceilings are per account, since personal and work are separate money. Accounts already exist end to end: account_events stamps every record (docs/calculation-reference.md section 9) and every report groups by them. Set them with ccreport budget set <account> <amount> and list them with ccreport budget, stored in a small table beside the other per-account state rather than an environment variable, so two accounts on one machine each carry their own without a parsing convention.

Surfaces: the ccu dashboard, and the merged dashboard once ccreport-5ki6 exists, where a ceiling and a projection are one more row per account. An account with no ceiling shows the projection alone.

Degradation: a month with fewer than three active days projects nothing. A projection built on two data points is a guess with a decimal point on it.

Acceptance: tests cover a steady month projecting close to a hand-computed figure, recent-day weighting moving the projection after a spike, a billing month anchored to a renewal day other than the first, session and week window projections, an account with no ceiling rendering the projection alone, and a sparse month projecting nothing.

acceptance.new:
- A hit session window in `ccreport limits` reports the Extra usd spent while it was over the limit, or the absent marker when no snapshot baseline covers it — never $0 for unknown.
- `ccreport limits --json` carries the same value as a raw float (or null) on the instance entry.
- A window with no Extra spend and a valid baseline reads $0, distinct from unknown.
- A window spanning an Extra billing reset does not report a negative or inflated figure.
- pytest coverage under `tests/` for: hit window with baseline, hit window without baseline, non-hit window, billing-reset straddle.

title.new: ccreport limits: show Extra usage spent on windows that hit the limit

description.new:
`ccreport limits` marks a window that filled with `yes` in the Hit column, but says nothing about what the overflow cost. Once a session window reaches 100%, further work bills against Extra usage (pay-as-you-go credits), and that spend is invisible in the report — the Spend column prices the quota fill, not the overflow.

The data is already stored. `cache_db.py` keeps `extra_usage_snapshots (ts, spent)` — a cumulative Extra-spend series appended by the status line on slow renders and pruned to 31 days (`cache_db.write_usage_cache`, cache_db.py:1495). `cache_db.compute_extra_window_deltas` (cache_db.py:1510) already does the same subtraction for the status line's live S/W deltas: take the newest snapshot at or before a start epoch as the baseline and subtract.

Proposed behaviour: for each `WindowInstance` with `hit_limit` true (ccreport.py:2139), compute Extra spent over the span from the moment the window first reached 100% to its reset (or to now for an open window), as `last_spent - baseline_spent`, and surface it in `report_limits` (ccreport.py:2588) plus `_limits_entry` (ccreport.py:2490) for `--json`.

Open design questions for whoever picks this up:
- Column vs caption. Only hit windows have a value, so a whole column would be one number over a stack of dashes in most reports — the same argument `_open_note` makes for putting the projection in a caption. A caption line per hit window is probably the right shape; decide with the user.
- Span start. From the first sample at 100%, or from the window's own start (`started_at`)? Extra only accrues after exhaustion, so the 100% sample is the honest baseline, but sampling is coarse (a slow render only) and the true crossing sits somewhere before it.
- Monthly billing reset. Extra is a monthly quota, so `spent` drops to 0 at rollover. `compute_extra_window_deltas` clamps a negative delta to 0; a window straddling the rollover needs the same treatment or an explicit unknown.
- Unknown vs zero. A window older than the 31-day retention, or one from before Extra snapshotting existed, has no baseline. That is unknown, not $0, and must render as the absent marker rather than a zero — the same rule `compute_extra_window_deltas` states for its None.
- Costs-only refreshes do not snapshot Extra (`snapshot_extra=False`), so the series is sparser than the rate-limit sample series. A hit window may have no snapshot inside its span at all.

Only the session (5h) window is in the ask, but week and scoped windows hit too; decide whether the same line applies to them.

description.new:
`tests/test_ccu.py::TestPaceLine` fails for anyone whose shell exports `CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS`. With `CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS=5` exported, 5 tests fail:

    assert self._pace(50, 3.5) == '3d 12h into 7-day window (pace: 7d) - 50% expected, +0%'
    AssertionError: got '... (pace: 5d) - 70% expected, -20%'

`pricing.pace_days()` (src/ccreport/pricing.py:1417) reads the variable at call time and the suite never clears it, so the pace tests assert against whatever the developer set for their own status line. `CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS=7 uv run pytest` passes; a bare `just test` does not.

The same hole is open for every other variable the code reads for configuration: CF_BADGE, CLAUDE_CACHE_DB_TIMEOUT, CLAUDE_CACHE_SANITY_ABORT, CLAUDE_CACHE_SANITY_DISABLE, CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_DEFER, CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_DIR, CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_KEEP, CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_TIMESTAMP_EPOCH, CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_TOTAL_TOKEN, CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_USAGE_JSON. None of them are cleared today.

Fix: an autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py that deletes them all before each test, ordered ahead of `isolate_cache_db` (which sets CLAUDE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_DISABLE itself and must win). A test that wants one sets it with monkeypatch, the way `isolate_cache_db` documents for DB_PATH.

TZ, TMPDIR, COLUMNS and XDG_CONFIG_HOME are deliberately out of scope: Rich reads COLUMNS when the module-level console is built at import, before any fixture runs, and the date tests derive their expectations from the local zone rather than assuming one.

Acceptance criteria:
- `CLAUDE_CODE_PACE_DAYS=5 uv run pytest tests/` passes.
- A test asserts every name in the list is absent from os.environ.

notes.new: Landed: push.on_allowed_network and the gate in run_once. A connected UDP socket per CIDR picks a route and a source address without putting a packet on the wire, so a VPN handing out an address in range counts as being on the network. Empty networks means no gate. A malformed CIDR blocks: every entry is parsed before any is probed, which was a real bug in the first cut — a machine matching the first CIDR returned True and never reached the typo in the second, so the same config would have passed at the office and failed nowhere else. IPv6 works (::1/128 tested). A blocked push sends no request and writes no watermark, so the queue goes out on the first allowed run; it does stamp the attempt with no failure increment, so a day off-network costs one process per interval. 'ccreport push' and 'ccreport server status' both name the CIDRs that were wanted. Verified: 'just lint-all' clean, 'just test' 1380 passed.

title.new: Bare `ccreport server` crashes: AttributeError on args.config

description.new:
Running `ccreport server` with no subcommand raises:

    File "src/ccreport/ccreport.py", line 3062, in main
        cmd_server_status(args)
    File "src/ccreport/ccreport.py", line 1754, in cmd_server_status
        path = Path(args.config or push.CONFIG_PATH)
    AttributeError: 'Namespace' object has no attribute 'config'

Why: main() routes a missing `server_command` to cmd_server_status (ccreport.py:3055-3062), but `--config` is added only to the four subparsers (connect/allow/deny/status) at ccreport.py:2977-2978. A bare `ccreport server` therefore never sets the `config` dest.

Fix: make cmd_server_status read the option defensively (getattr) or define `--config` on the `server` parser itself, so bare `ccreport server` behaves as `ccreport server status`.

description.new:
`ccreport server status` printed `last push 2026-08-13 19:24, 1 failures since` while the server held 0 records. The push had failed — the container was not listening yet — but the output reads as a success with a footnote.

Two causes:

- `push.py:597` catches PushError and stores only `failures + 1`. `str(exc)` carries the reason (connection refused, 413, 500) and is discarded, so nothing can ever tell the user which it was.
- `ccreport.py:1783` labels the attempt stamp `last push`. The stamp moves on every outcome by design, so the label is wrong whenever the count is non-zero.

Fix: persist the reason with the attempt, return it from `read_push_attempt`, and render a failed attempt as a failure with its reason.
