Value vs plan prices a scoped page over the whole server's history
description:
## What happens

On a project, model, machine or account page the "Value vs plan" tile prices
the subscription over the page's range bounds, and on the all-time toggle those
come from `dashboard.all_time_bounds`, which reads `db.oldest_record_ts` — the
oldest record on the *server*, not the oldest record the page is about.

A project first seen in August is therefore set against six months of
subscription it did not exist for, and reads as barely having paid for itself
when over its own life it paid many times over. The 90-day toggle distorts the
same way: ninety days of subscription against twenty days of one project.

Shipped in c507fe5 and deployed.

## The rule

A scoped page prices the subscription over the span its own records cover,
clipped to the page's range. The denominator then covers the same period as the
numerator, which is the only way the multiple means anything.

Period pages are the exception and keep the whole period. A month page charges
the whole month whether or not every day of it was worked — the month was paid
for either way, and shortening it to the days with records would flatter every
quiet month.

The whole-server page is unaffected either way: its records are all the
records, so the bound it would compute is the bound it already has.

## Notes

- The span the tile prints comes from the same bounds, so it will say "across
  20 days" on a page whose toggle reads all-time. That is the tile describing
  itself, and is what stops the figure being read against the wrong period.
- A scope with records on one day has a span of one day, not zero: the bound is
  the first record's local midnight to the last record's next local midnight.

## Acceptance criteria

- A project whose records start in August prices against August onward, not
  from the server's oldest record.
- The same on model, machine and account pages.
- A month page still prices the whole month, including one with records on
  three days.
- The whole-server page's figure is unchanged.
- pytest coverage for a scope narrower than the server's history, and for the
  period exception.

description:
## Symptom

/settings/projects shows opentd2 on machine `mbp` as 50,762 records / $7,643.10.
/project/opentd2 (all-time, the default range) shows the same project as
~23,472 calls / $3,273.52. Ratio 2.16x. Every project row on that page is
inflated the same way, so the page cannot be used to compare projects against
the dashboard.

The duplicates are within one machine, not across two: opentd2 has only ever
pushed from `mbp`. The same call sits in server_records twice, under two file
paths, and the read-time dedup is what collapses them.

## Cause

`db.project_overview` (src/ccreport/server/db.py:634) runs a raw
`COUNT(*)`/`SUM(r.cost)` over server_records grouped by (machine_id, project).
It never goes through `reports._dedup_clause`, which every other total on the
server does. This is the same defect that was fixed for /settings/accounts,
where the raw sum drew 2.2x what the dashboard drew — see
`reports.account_overview` and its docstring.

## Fix

Move the query out of db.py into reports.py (that is where anything summing or
counting server_records lives, per AGENTS.md) and wrap it in
`_dedup_clause(Filters())`, modelled on `account_overview`:

- alias the table as `a` so the clause's `a.dk` / `a.id` references resolve
- keep the machine label and project alias correlated subqueries as they are
- `pages.projects` (src/ccreport/server/pages.py:262) calls the new
  `reports.project_overview` instead of `db.project_overview`

Note the trade the dedup makes, and do not try to avoid it: the surviving copy
is the lowest id per (account_uuid, dk) across the whole table, so when two
machines pushed the same call, the row lands on whichever machine's copy won.
That is what account_overview already accepts and what the dashboard shows.

Decided: the Records column counts deduped calls, not what the machine pushed.
Both columns then describe the same set of records and the row matches the
project page. Leave the column header 'Records' as it is; 'Pushed' is
/settings/machines' word for its deliberately raw count
(`db.machine_overview`), and that one stays raw because deleting a machine
takes away exactly what it pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

- /settings/projects' cost for a project on one machine equals what
  /project/<name> shows for the all-time range when only that machine pushed it
- The Records column equals the deduped call count for the same row
- `project_overview` lives in server/reports.py and uses `_dedup_clause`
- A pytest under tests/ ingests the same call twice from one machine and
  asserts the page's row counts it once — the existing account_overview dedup
  test is the model
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass
acceptance: See the acceptance criteria section of the description.

Detail pages take 4.3s: _Plans scans the corpus for two account names, and nothing caches them
description:
Every /{dimension}/{key} page on the merged server takes ~4.6s over the wire
against the production database on sea (815061 rows in server_records, 599 MB).
The dashboard at / answers in 0.135s, because `dashboard.cached_build` holds it
against `db.content_stamp`; `pages.detail` calls `dashboard.build` directly and
so pays full price on every visit.

Reproduced:

    /                                 0.135s
    /model/claude-opus-5?days=0       4.568s
    /project/opentd2                  4.602s
    /account/personal?days=0          4.586s

cProfile of `dashboard.build(conn, 0, scope=Scope("model", "claude-opus-5"))`
inside the running container: 4.30s total, of which 3.79s is
`sqlite3.Connection.execute`. Two calls account for all of it.

1. 2.23s in `dashboard._Plans.__init__` (src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py:546),
   which calls `reports.account_overview(conn)`
   (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:351). That query runs the full
   `_dedup_clause` scan over all 815k rows and sums cost per account, and
   `_Plans` reads only `account_uuid` and `label` off the result — the spend,
   the record count, the tier and the declared count are all discarded. The two
   fields it wants cost 0.07s:
   `SELECT DISTINCT account_uuid FROM server_records`, with the existing
   newest-label subquery per uuid.

2. 2.06s in `reports.load_grouped` (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:276).
   EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows `SCAN a USING INDEX idx_srec_file` plus
   `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY`. Adding a covering index over the seven
   GROUP_COLS plus ts, cost, the four token columns, dk and id removes the temp
   b-tree: the query drops from 2.04s to 1.02s and the plan becomes
   `SCAN a USING COVERING INDEX`. The index costs 3.1s to build and +174 MB on
   a 599 MB database.

Filter pushdown is not the lever here. With the index in place the
model-filtered grouped query is 0.955s against 1.02s unfiltered, because
`_dedup_clause` deliberately drops the date bounds and its subquery scans the
whole table either way. Pushing a scope filter into SQL would also change which
copy of a synced call survives the dedup, which `_dedup_clause`'s docstring
calls out as intentional — so leave the Python-side scope filter alone.

Three fixes, in the order they pay:

1. `_Plans.__init__` stops calling `account_overview` and reads the (uuid,
   label) pairs it needs directly. `account_overview` keeps its own callers on
   /settings/accounts, which want the totals.
2. A new numbered `Step` on `server/db.py`'s MIGRATION_CHAIN creating the
   covering index, plus the `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` in the schema script
   so a fresh database gets it too.
3. `pages.detail` goes through a cached build the way `index` does. Unlike
   `cached_build`'s one entry per range toggle, a detail cache is keyed on
   (database, days, dimension, key) and is unbounded in principle — one key per
   model, project, machine, account, day, week and month this server holds — so
   it needs an eviction bound. Same invalidation as `cached_build`:
   `db.content_stamp` plus the render's local date.
acceptance:
- `dashboard._Plans` no longer calls `reports.account_overview`, and a test
  asserts the plan tile still prices the same span it did before.
- `server_records` carries a covering index for GROUP_COLS, created both by the
  schema script and by a numbered migration Step one above the current head, and
  `tests/test_migrations.py` (or its equivalent) covers the upgrade path from a
  database that predates it.
- Repeat visits to a `/{dimension}/{key}` page are served from cache and the
  cache is bounded; a push or a date rollover invalidates it, proven by a test
  the way `cached_build`'s invalidation is.
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.
- Measured on sea afterwards: cold detail page well under 2s, warm one under
  0.2s.

_Plans reads two account names without scanning 815k rows
description:
`dashboard._Plans.__init__` (src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py:546) calls
`reports.account_overview(conn)` and reads only `account_uuid` and `label` off
each row. That query runs the full `_dedup_clause` scan over server_records and
sums cost per account; on sea's 815061-row database it takes 2.23s of the
4.30s a detail page spends in `dashboard.build`. Every other field it returns —
cost, records, tier, declared — is discarded here.

`SELECT DISTINCT account_uuid FROM server_records` answers in 0.07s, and the
newest-label-per-uuid correlated subquery `account_overview` already uses can
ride along on it. Measured on the production copy: 0.82s for both together,
0.07s for the distinct alone.

`account_overview` keeps its /settings/accounts caller, which wants the totals
and must keep the dedup. Do not weaken it — add the cheap read beside it.

Why _Plans needs the names at all: the timeline is keyed by uuid, a folded
record carries the display name, and `_Plans` is where the two meet.
acceptance:
- `dashboard._Plans` does not call `reports.account_overview`.
- The plan tile and the per-month plan columns price the same spans they did
  before, covered by a test in tests/test_dashboard.py.
- `reports.account_overview` is unchanged and still deduped.
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.

Covering index for GROUP_COLS so load_grouped stops building a temp b-tree
description:
`reports.load_grouped` (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:276) takes 2.06s on
sea's 815061-row server_records. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN:

    SCAN a USING INDEX idx_srec_file
    LIST SUBQUERY 1
    SCAN server_records USING COVERING INDEX idx_srec_account_dk
    USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY

The temp b-tree is the cost. An index whose leading columns are the seven
`reports.GROUP_COLS` in order, carrying the aggregated columns as well, lets
SQLite walk the groups in order and covers every SUM:

    CREATE INDEX idx_srec_group ON server_records(
      machine_id, account_uuid, account_label, project, model, day, oslo_date,
      ts, cost, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_create, cache_read, dk, id)

`dk` and `id` are in it so the dedup clause's `a.dk IS NULL OR a.dk = '' OR
a.id IN (...)` is answered off the same index and the plan stays covering.

Measured on a `.backup` copy of the production database: query 2.04s before,
1.02s after; the plan becomes `SCAN a USING COVERING INDEX idx_srec_group`;
the index takes 3.1s to build and grows the file from 599 MB to 773 MB.

Per AGENTS.md a schema change reaches an existing database only through
`migrations.py`: a numbered `Step` appended to `server/db.py`'s
`MIGRATION_CHAIN`, one above the current head. A new index is carried by the
`CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS` script too, and `Step(N, "name")` with no callable
is what re-runs it. Do not renumber or edit a shipped entry.

Note the +174 MB. If that is unwelcome on this host, the alternative is
dropping the trailing token columns from the index and accepting a partial
cover — measure before choosing.
acceptance:
- The index is in server/db.py's CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS script and in a numbered
  Step one above the current MIGRATION_CHAIN head.
- A test upgrades a database created before the step and asserts the index
  exists afterwards.
- EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for _GROUPED_SQL no longer contains USE TEMP B-TREE.
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.

Cache /{dimension}/{key} builds, bounded, against content_stamp
description:
`pages.detail` (src/ccreport/server/pages.py:454) calls `dashboard.build`
directly, so a detail page is rebuilt on every request. The dashboard at / goes
through `dashboard.cached_build`, which is why it answers in 0.135s while
/model/claude-opus-5?days=0 takes 4.6s over the wire against sea.

AGENTS.md states the current rule outright: the catch-all "is never cached:
`cached_build` holds the whole-server view per range, which is the page a
browser opens over and over". A detail page is opened over and over too — that
line needs updating with whatever this issue lands.

Invalidation is `cached_build`'s: `db.content_stamp(conn)` plus the render's
local date, so a push or a midnight rebuilds. `content_stamp` reads
ingest_files, account_aliases, machines.label_updated_at, project_aliases,
rate_limit_samples, extra_usage_samples and account_tiers, which is thousands of
rows, not hundreds of thousands — cheap enough to check per request.

The difference from `cached_build` is the key space. `cached_build` holds one
entry per (database, range toggle), which is `len(RANGES)` per server. A detail
cache is keyed on (database, days, dimension, key) and has one key per model,
project, machine, account, day, week and month this server holds — hundreds and
growing daily, each entry a whole Dashboard with its four chart series. It
therefore needs a bound; an LRU is the obvious shape, and the size should be
chosen against what one entry weighs rather than picked round.

Keep `_CACHE_LOCK`'s existing bargain: two threads missing on the same key both
build, which costs a duplicate query and does not serialize every other key
behind one build.

Depends on nothing, but the win compounds with ccreport-432w and ccreport-rpmz:
those cut the cold build, this removes the repeat.
acceptance:
- A repeated GET of the same /{dimension}/{key} URL builds once.
- The cache is bounded and evicts; a test drives it past the bound and asserts
  the oldest entry is gone and the newest is served.
- A moved content_stamp and a changed local date each invalidate, tested the
  way cached_build's invalidation is in tests/test_dashboard.py.
- The AGENTS.md bullet saying the catch-all is never cached is rewritten to
  match.
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.

Covering index for GROUP_COLS so load_grouped stops building a temp b-tree
description:
`reports.load_grouped` (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:276) takes 2.06s on
sea's 815061-row server_records. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN:

    SCAN a USING INDEX idx_srec_file
    LIST SUBQUERY 1
    SCAN server_records USING COVERING INDEX idx_srec_account_dk
    USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY

The temp b-tree is the cost. An index whose leading columns are the seven
`reports.GROUP_COLS` in order, carrying the aggregated columns as well, lets
SQLite walk the groups in order and covers every SUM:

    CREATE INDEX idx_srec_group ON server_records(
      machine_id, account_uuid, account_label, project, model, day, oslo_date,
      ts, cost, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_create, cache_read, dk, id)

`dk` and `id` are in it so the dedup clause's `a.dk IS NULL OR a.dk = '' OR
a.id IN (...)` is answered off the same index and the plan stays covering.

Measured on a `.backup` copy of the production database: query 2.04s before,
1.02s after; the plan becomes `SCAN a USING COVERING INDEX idx_srec_group`;
the index takes 3.1s to build and grows the file from 599 MB to 773 MB.

Per AGENTS.md a schema change reaches an existing database only through
`migrations.py`: a numbered `Step` appended to `server/db.py`'s
`MIGRATION_CHAIN`, one above the current head. A new index is carried by the
`CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS` script too, and `Step(N, "name")` with no callable
is what re-runs it. Do not renumber or edit a shipped entry.

Note the +174 MB. If that is unwelcome on this host, the alternative is
dropping the trailing token columns from the index and accepting a partial
cover — measure before choosing.
acceptance:
- The index is in server/db.py's CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS script and in a numbered
  Step one above the current MIGRATION_CHAIN head.
- A test upgrades a database created before the step and asserts the index
  exists afterwards.
- EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for _GROUPED_SQL no longer contains USE TEMP B-TREE.
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.

Cache /{dimension}/{key} builds, bounded, against content_stamp
description:
`pages.detail` (src/ccreport/server/pages.py:454) calls `dashboard.build`
directly, so a detail page is rebuilt on every request. The dashboard at / goes
through `dashboard.cached_build`, which is why it answers in 0.135s while
/model/claude-opus-5?days=0 takes 4.6s over the wire against sea.

AGENTS.md states the current rule outright: the catch-all "is never cached:
`cached_build` holds the whole-server view per range, which is the page a
browser opens over and over". A detail page is opened over and over too — that
line needs updating with whatever this issue lands.

Invalidation is `cached_build`'s: `db.content_stamp(conn)` plus the render's
local date, so a push or a midnight rebuilds. `content_stamp` reads
ingest_files, account_aliases, machines.label_updated_at, project_aliases,
rate_limit_samples, extra_usage_samples and account_tiers, which is thousands of
rows, not hundreds of thousands — cheap enough to check per request.

The difference from `cached_build` is the key space. `cached_build` holds one
entry per (database, range toggle), which is `len(RANGES)` per server. A detail
cache is keyed on (database, days, dimension, key) and has one key per model,
project, machine, account, day, week and month this server holds — hundreds and
growing daily, each entry a whole Dashboard with its four chart series. It
therefore needs a bound; an LRU is the obvious shape, and the size should be
chosen against what one entry weighs rather than picked round.

Keep `_CACHE_LOCK`'s existing bargain: two threads missing on the same key both
build, which costs a duplicate query and does not serialize every other key
behind one build.

Depends on nothing, but the win compounds with ccreport-432w and ccreport-rpmz:
those cut the cold build, this removes the repeat.
acceptance:
- A repeated GET of the same /{dimension}/{key} URL builds once.
- The cache is bounded and evicts; a test drives it past the bound and asserts
  the oldest entry is gone and the newest is served.
- A moved content_stamp and a changed local date each invalidate, tested the
  way cached_build's invalidation is in tests/test_dashboard.py.
- The AGENTS.md bullet saying the catch-all is never cached is rewritten to
  match.
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.

Pull the declared plan timeline from the server
description:
## Why

The timeline now exists in four places — one file per machine plus the server's
`account_tiers` — and a plan change means editing every copy. They drift
silently: nothing compares them, and a machine left behind reports a stretch
under the wrong plan with no sign anything is wrong.

Making the server the one source removes three of the four copies. It is
already where the timeline has to be typed for the dashboard, and it is the
copy that reaches records no client can still re-push.

## Scope

1. Carry the declared timeline back on the ingest response, beside the cost
   rows `server/pull.py` already returns, rather than through `/v1/report`.
   That endpoint sits inside the network allowlist and answers nothing when a
   laptop is away from home, which is exactly when a machine is most likely to
   be running on a stale copy.
2. Bump `protocol.PROTOCOL_VERSION` to 2: a new section on the ingest response
   is the bump rule's first case.
3. Scope what comes back to `read_latest_account()`, as the remote cost tables
   already are, so a login switch cannot write another account's plan history
   into this machine's log.
4. Write the entries through `cache_db.backfill_account_events`, which is
   already keyed on ts and idempotent. A pull replaces the backfilled rows for
   the accounts the server declared and leaves captures alone.

## Notes

- `ccreport tiers <file>` stays. It is how a timeline is first written, how a
  machine that pushes to no server declares one, and what a person edits when
  the server is wrong.
- Decide and document which side wins when both have declared something for one
  account. Server-wins is the point of the change; it also means a local
  `ccreport tiers` run is undone by the next pull, and the command should say so.
- No new endpoint and no new round trip: `push.run_once` already pulls by
  default.

## Acceptance criteria

- An ingest response carries the asking machine's accounts' timelines.
- A pull writes them as backfilled rows and leaves captures untouched.
- A second pull with nothing changed writes nothing new.
- Another account's entries never reach a machine signed in elsewhere.
- A client one version behind still pushes; one ahead is refused, as now.
- pytest coverage for the response section, the write, and the account scoping.

Detail pages take 4.3s: _Plans scans the corpus for two account names, and nothing caches them
description:
Every /{dimension}/{key} page on the merged server takes ~4.6s over the wire
against the production database on sea (815061 rows in server_records, 599 MB).
The dashboard at / answers in 0.135s, because `dashboard.cached_build` holds it
against `db.content_stamp`; `pages.detail` calls `dashboard.build` directly and
so pays full price on every visit.

Reproduced:

    /                                 0.135s
    /model/claude-opus-5?days=0       4.568s
    /project/opentd2                  4.602s
    /account/personal?days=0          4.586s

cProfile of `dashboard.build(conn, 0, scope=Scope("model", "claude-opus-5"))`
inside the running container: 4.30s total, of which 3.79s is
`sqlite3.Connection.execute`. Two calls account for all of it.

1. 2.23s in `dashboard._Plans.__init__` (src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py:546),
   which calls `reports.account_overview(conn)`
   (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:351). That query runs the full
   `_dedup_clause` scan over all 815k rows and sums cost per account, and
   `_Plans` reads only `account_uuid` and `label` off the result — the spend,
   the record count, the tier and the declared count are all discarded. The two
   fields it wants cost 0.07s:
   `SELECT DISTINCT account_uuid FROM server_records`, with the existing
   newest-label subquery per uuid.

2. 2.06s in `reports.load_grouped` (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:276).
   EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows `SCAN a USING INDEX idx_srec_file` plus
   `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY`. Adding a covering index over the seven
   GROUP_COLS plus ts, cost, the four token columns, dk and id removes the temp
   b-tree: the query drops from 2.04s to 1.02s and the plan becomes
   `SCAN a USING COVERING INDEX`. The index costs 3.1s to build and +174 MB on
   a 599 MB database.

Filter pushdown is not the lever here. With the index in place the
model-filtered grouped query is 0.955s against 1.02s unfiltered, because
`_dedup_clause` deliberately drops the date bounds and its subquery scans the
whole table either way. Pushing a scope filter into SQL would also change which
copy of a synced call survives the dedup, which `_dedup_clause`'s docstring
calls out as intentional — so leave the Python-side scope filter alone.

Three fixes, in the order they pay:

1. `_Plans.__init__` stops calling `account_overview` and reads the (uuid,
   label) pairs it needs directly. `account_overview` keeps its own callers on
   /settings/accounts, which want the totals.
2. A new numbered `Step` on `server/db.py`'s MIGRATION_CHAIN creating the
   covering index, plus the `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` in the schema script
   so a fresh database gets it too.
3. `pages.detail` goes through a cached build the way `index` does. Unlike
   `cached_build`'s one entry per range toggle, a detail cache is keyed on
   (database, days, dimension, key) and is unbounded in principle — one key per
   model, project, machine, account, day, week and month this server holds — so
   it needs an eviction bound. Same invalidation as `cached_build`:
   `db.content_stamp` plus the render's local date.
acceptance:
- `dashboard._Plans` no longer calls `reports.account_overview`, and a test
  asserts the plan tile still prices the same span it did before.
- `server_records` carries a covering index for GROUP_COLS, created both by the
  schema script and by a numbered migration Step one above the current head, and
  `tests/test_migrations.py` (or its equivalent) covers the upgrade path from a
  database that predates it.
- Repeat visits to a `/{dimension}/{key}` page are served from cache and the
  cache is bounded; a push or a date rollover invalidates it, proven by a test
  the way `cached_build`'s invalidation is.
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.
- Measured on sea afterwards: cold detail page well under 2s, warm one under
  0.2s.

build, which costs a duplicate query and does not serialize every other key
behind one build.

those cut the cold build, this removes the repeat.

  way cached_build's invalidation is in tests/test_dashboard.py.

  match.

title: Cache /{dimension}/{key} builds, bounded, against content_stamp
Detail pages take 4.3s: _Plans scans the corpus for two account names, and nothing caches them
description:
Every /{dimension}/{key} page on the merged server takes ~4.6s over the wire
against the production database on sea (815061 rows in server_records, 599 MB).
The dashboard at / answers in 0.135s, because `dashboard.cached_build` holds it
against `db.content_stamp`; `pages.detail` calls `dashboard.build` directly and
so pays full price on every visit.

Reproduced:

    /                                 0.135s
    /model/claude-opus-5?days=0       4.568s
    /project/opentd2                  4.602s
    /account/personal?days=0          4.586s

cProfile of `dashboard.build(conn, 0, scope=Scope("model", "claude-opus-5"))`
inside the running container: 4.30s total, of which 3.79s is
`sqlite3.Connection.execute`. Two calls account for all of it.

1. 2.23s in `dashboard._Plans.__init__` (src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py:546),
   which calls `reports.account_overview(conn)`
   (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:351). That query runs the full
   `_dedup_clause` scan over all 815k rows and sums cost per account, and
   `_Plans` reads only `account_uuid` and `label` off the result — the spend,
   the record count, the tier and the declared count are all discarded. The two
   fields it wants cost 0.07s:
   `SELECT DISTINCT account_uuid FROM server_records`, with the existing
   newest-label subquery per uuid.

2. 2.06s in `reports.load_grouped` (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:276).
   EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows `SCAN a USING INDEX idx_srec_file` plus
   `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY`. Adding a covering index over the seven
   GROUP_COLS plus ts, cost, the four token columns, dk and id removes the temp
   b-tree: the query drops from 2.04s to 1.02s and the plan becomes
   `SCAN a USING COVERING INDEX`. The index costs 3.1s to build and +174 MB on
   a 599 MB database.

Filter pushdown is not the lever here. With the index in place the
model-filtered grouped query is 0.955s against 1.02s unfiltered, because
`_dedup_clause` deliberately drops the date bounds and its subquery scans the
whole table either way. Pushing a scope filter into SQL would also change which
copy of a synced call survives the dedup, which `_dedup_clause`'s docstring
calls out as intentional — so leave the Python-side scope filter alone.

Three fixes, in the order they pay:

1. `_Plans.__init__` stops calling `account_overview` and reads the (uuid,
   label) pairs it needs directly. `account_overview` keeps its own callers on
   /settings/accounts, which want the totals.
2. A new numbered `Step` on `server/db.py`'s MIGRATION_CHAIN creating the
   covering index, plus the `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` in the schema script
   so a fresh database gets it too.
3. `pages.detail` goes through a cached build the way `index` does. Unlike
   `cached_build`'s one entry per range toggle, a detail cache is keyed on
   (database, days, dimension, key) and is unbounded in principle — one key per
   model, project, machine, account, day, week and month this server holds — so
   it needs an eviction bound. Same invalidation as `cached_build`:
   `db.content_stamp` plus the render's local date.
acceptance:
- `dashboard._Plans` no longer calls `reports.account_overview`, and a test
  asserts the plan tile still prices the same span it did before.
- `server_records` carries a covering index for GROUP_COLS, created both by the
  schema script and by a numbered migration Step one above the current head, and
  `tests/test_migrations.py` (or its equivalent) covers the upgrade path from a
  database that predates it.
- Repeat visits to a `/{dimension}/{key}` page are served from cache and the
  cache is bounded; a push or a date rollover invalidates it, proven by a test
  the way `cached_build`'s invalidation is.
- `just lint-all` and `just test` pass.
- Measured on sea afterwards: cold detail page well under 2s, warm one under
  0.2s.
closed_reason: All three children landed. The sea wall-clock criterion was not measured: no access to that host from this session

title: Detail pages take 4.3s: _Plans scans the corpus for two account names, and nothing caches them
Pull the declared plan timeline from the server
description:
## Why

The timeline now exists in four places — one file per machine plus the server's
`account_tiers` — and a plan change means editing every copy. They drift
silently: nothing compares them, and a machine left behind reports a stretch
under the wrong plan with no sign anything is wrong.

Making the server the one source removes three of the four copies. It is
already where the timeline has to be typed for the dashboard, and it is the
copy that reaches records no client can still re-push.

## Scope

1. Carry the declared timeline back on the ingest response, beside the cost
   rows `server/pull.py` already returns, rather than through `/v1/report`.
   That endpoint sits inside the network allowlist and answers nothing when a
   laptop is away from home, which is exactly when a machine is most likely to
   be running on a stale copy.
2. Bump `protocol.PROTOCOL_VERSION` to 2: a new section on the ingest response
   is the bump rule's first case.
3. Scope what comes back to `read_latest_account()`, as the remote cost tables
   already are, so a login switch cannot write another account's plan history
   into this machine's log.
4. Write the entries through `cache_db.backfill_account_events`, which is
   already keyed on ts and idempotent. A pull replaces the backfilled rows for
   the accounts the server declared and leaves captures alone.

## Notes

- `ccreport tiers <file>` stays. It is how a timeline is first written, how a
  machine that pushes to no server declares one, and what a person edits when
  the server is wrong.
- Decide and document which side wins when both have declared something for one
  account. Server-wins is the point of the change; it also means a local
  `ccreport tiers` run is undone by the next pull, and the command should say so.
- No new endpoint and no new round trip: `push.run_once` already pulls by
  default.

## Acceptance criteria

- An ingest response carries the asking machine's accounts' timelines.
- A pull writes them as backfilled rows and leaves captures untouched.
- A second pull with nothing changed writes nothing new.
- Another account's entries never reach a machine signed in elsewhere.
- A client one version behind still pushes; one ahead is refused, as now.
- pytest coverage for the response section, the write, and the account scoping.
closed_reason: pull.tiers on the ingest response, scoped to the asking account; push.store_tiers writes via cache_db.replace_backfilled_account; PROTOCOL_VERSION 2

Materialize the dedup winner as a column instead of re-deriving it per query
description:
431,439 of 815,841 rows in server_records (53%) are duplicates, and every single read re-computes which ones.

reports._dedup_clause (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:236) emits:

    (a.dk IS NULL OR a.dk = '' OR a.id IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM server_records GROUP BY account_uuid, dk))

EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows that inner query as a LIST SUBQUERY scanning idx_srec_account_dk and materializing 384,063 rows, plus a bloom filter, on every request. It runs in load(), load_grouped(), account_overview() and project_overview() — so /, every detail page, /settings/accounts and /settings/projects each pay it.

Measured on a VACUUM INTO copy of the live database:

  grouped WITH dedup subquery       1.69s
  grouped WITHOUT dedup             0.41s
  grouped WHERE dup=0 (flag+index)  0.20s
  account_overview WITH subquery    2.16s -> WHERE dup=0  0.23s
  project_overview WITH subquery    0.98s -> WHERE dup=0  0.22s

The backfill of the flag over the whole table took 4.2s; building the covering index took 2.9s.

Shape that measured: a `dup INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column on server_records, set to 1 for every row that is not MIN(id) within its (account_uuid, dk), plus idx_srec_group rebuilt with dup as its leading column.

What has to be settled before writing it:

- Ingest has to maintain the flag. server/ingest.py is the only writer; a newly arrived row either wins its (account_uuid, dk) or loses to an existing id. Deleting a machine (ON DELETE CASCADE) can promote a loser to winner, so the delete path in db.py has to re-run the flag for the affected keys.
- AGENTS.md documents the dedup trade in prose ('the lowest id per (account, dedup key) wins'). That rule must not change; only where it is computed.
- The dedup subquery deliberately drops the date bounds but keeps every other filter, because which copy survives depends on the set being deduped: ask for one machine alone and that machine's copy wins. A single global flag changes that answer for machine-filtered and project-filtered reads. Decide whether that is acceptable (it is what the dashboard already shows for the unfiltered case) or whether the flag is only used on the unfiltered path and the subquery stays for filtered ones.
- Schema change goes through migrations.py: a numbered Step appended to MIGRATION_CHAIN in src/ccreport/server/db.py, one above 9. A column added to an existing table is skipped by CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, so the step needs the ALTER plus the backfill.
acceptance: dashboard.build(conn, 0) under 0.5s. account_overview and project_overview each under 0.3s. tests/ covers the ingest path promoting and demoting a winner, and the machine-delete path re-flagging. Golden report output unchanged.

Index the newest-account-label lookup account_overview sorts a whole account for
description:
reports.account_overview (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:351) carries this correlated scalar subquery to find the newest label an account pushed:

    (SELECT r.account_label FROM server_records r
      WHERE r.account_uuid = a.account_uuid AND r.account_label IS NOT NULL
   ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)

EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN:

    CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY 1
      SEARCH r USING INDEX idx_srec_account_dk (account_uuid=?)
      USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY

idx_srec_account_dk is (account_uuid, dk) and does not carry ts or account_label, so each of the two accounts has ~400k rows read and sorted to produce one string.

Measured on the live database:

  account_overview whole query                      2.13s
  same query with the label subquery removed        1.41s
  the label subquery alone, over both accounts      0.79s
  SELECT DISTINCT account_uuid                      0.08s

Adding CREATE INDEX idx_srec_acct_ts ON server_records(account_uuid, ts DESC, account_label) turned the plan into 'SEARCH r USING COVERING INDEX idx_srec_acct_ts (account_uuid=?)' with no temp b-tree, and took account_overview from 1.59s to 0.86s on an ANALYZEd copy.

reports.account_names (reports.py:392) runs the same subquery over SELECT DISTINCT account_uuid and costs 0.86s on its own; it is called from dashboard's view constructor on every cold build, so the same index pays there too.

Weigh the write cost: the table already carries four indexes totalling 388 MB against 347 MB of data. A fifth adds to every ingest. Check whether idx_srec_ts (15 MB, on ts alone) still has a reader once this lands, and whether idx_srec_account_dk can be widened instead of a new index added.

Schema change goes through migrations.py: a numbered Step appended to MIGRATION_CHAIN in src/ccreport/server/db.py. An index is covered by the CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS script, but still needs Step(N, "name") with no callable to move the version that re-runs it.
acceptance: account_overview under 1.0s before ccreport-52h5's dedup work and under 0.3s after. account_names under 0.2s. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for both shows no USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY.

Cache /limits and the two /settings pages, which rebuild from scratch every load
description:
Four routes in src/ccreport/server/pages.py have no cache at all, where index() and detail() both go through dashboard.cached_build / cached_detail against db.content_stamp:

  /limits            pages.py:386  -> limits.build(conn, days)          2.66s
  /limits/{w}/{r}    pages.py:404  -> limits.build_window(...)          2.87s
  /settings/accounts pages.py:162  -> reports.account_overview(conn)    2.37s
  /settings/projects pages.py:263  -> reports.project_overview(conn)    1.10s

limit_windows' docstring says 'Not cached. A window list is a page someone clicked into, and its records are loaded over the window spans rather than over the whole range.' That reasoning holds for the span but not for the repeat: the same reader reloads it, and content_stamp only moves when a push lands. Push cadence measured on the live server: 4 distinct minutes carried a push in the last 6 hours, so a stamp-keyed cache would hit almost always.

Separately, limits is expensive for a reason the cache does not remove. cProfile of limits.build(conn, 30), 3.78s total:

  0.836s  sqlite3 Cursor.fetchall (7 calls)
  0.670s  reports.load          (reports.py:150)
  0.558s  windows.SpendIndex.__init__ (windows.py:345, 2 calls)
  0.404s  reports._as_merged    (77,117 calls)
  0.114s  pricing.model_family  (77,123 calls)

limits._spend_indexes (limits.py:135) calls reports.load over the whole span the windows cover, which on days=30 is 77,117 records built as full UsageRecord objects. Its docstring gives the reason: 'a 5-hour window is priced over hours, and a grouped row has folded the hour away.' That rules out load_grouped as it stands, but not a grouping at a finer grain (per minute, or per (model, hour)) that a SpendIndex could still answer a window from. Worth measuring before adding the cache, since a cache does not help the first reader.

Both /settings pages depend on ccreport-73kp and ccreport-5s96; if those land first, measure again before adding a cache here — 0.23s and 0.22s may not need one.

Note DETAIL_CACHE_MAX is 96 (dashboard.py:621) and the detail key space is one entry per (entity, range toggle) across model, project, machine, account, day, week and month. A new day arrives daily. Check whether real use evicts entries that are then paid for again at 5.36s each.
acceptance: A second load of each of the four routes is under 100ms while content_stamp has not moved. First load of /limits days=30 is under 1.0s.

The server opens SQLite with a 2 MB page cache against a 774 MB database
description:
src/ccreport/server/db.py connect() sets no cache_size and no mmap_size, so the live server runs on SQLite's defaults. Read off the running container:

  journal_mode        wal
  page_size           4096
  page_count          189,014   (774 MB)
  cache_size          -2000     (2 MB)
  mmap_size           0
  wal_autocheckpoint  1000
  synchronous         2

2 MB of page cache against 347 MB of table and 388 MB of index means effectively every query re-reads through the OS. Measured on the live database, three runs each, min taken:

                            grouped   account_overview
  default (2 MB, no mmap)     0.91s        2.13s
  cache_size = -262144        0.94s        1.78s
  that plus mmap_size = 1 GB  0.82s        1.37s

So the two pragmas alone take account_overview down 36%. Cheap, but smaller than ccreport-73kp's win and it stacks with it rather than replacing it.

Two more things found while measuring, both needing a decision rather than an obvious fix:

1. There is no sqlite_stat1 table — ANALYZE has never run. Running it is NOT a free win. On a VACUUM INTO copy, ANALYZE moved account_overview 2.16s -> 1.59s but moved the grouped dashboard query 0.94s -> 1.66s, because the planner switched off the covering scan of idx_srec_group. If ANALYZE is adopted, re-measure every query in this epic, and consider whether ccreport-73kp's dup flag changes the answer.

2. server.db-wal is 204 MB and stays that size. PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(passive) returned (0, 42837, 42837) — busy 0, everything checkpointed — so it is not blocked by a reader; the WAL is simply never truncated. description:

    (a.dk IS NULL OR a.dk = '' OR a.id IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM server_records GROUP BY account_uuid, dk))

  project_overview WITH subquery    0.98s -> WHERE dup=0  0.22s

title: Materialize the dedup winner as a column instead of re-deriving it per query
Cache /limits and the two /settings pages, which rebuild from scratch every load
description:
Four routes in src/ccreport/server/pages.py have no cache at all, where index() and detail() both go through dashboard.cached_build / cached_detail against db.content_stamp:

  /limits            pages.py:386  -> limits.build(conn, days)          2.66s
  /limits/{w}/{r}    pages.py:404  -> limits.build_window(...)          2.87s
  /settings/accounts pages.py:162  -> reports.account_overview(conn)    2.37s
  /settings/projects pages.py:263  -> reports.project_overview(conn)    1.10s

limit_windows' docstring says 'Not cached. A window list is a page someone clicked into, and its records are loaded over the window spans rather than over the whole range.' That reasoning holds for the span but not for the repeat: the same reader reloads it, and content_stamp only moves when a push lands. Push cadence measured on the live server: 4 distinct minutes carried a push in the last 6 hours, so a stamp-keyed cache would hit almost always.

Separately, limits is expensive for a reason the cache does not remove. cProfile of limits.build(conn, 30), 3.78s total:

  0.836s  sqlite3 Cursor.fetchall (7 calls)
  0.670s  reports.load          (reports.py:150)
  0.558s  windows.SpendIndex.__init__ (windows.py:345, 2 calls)
  0.404s  reports._as_merged    (77,117 calls)
  0.114s  pricing.model_family  (77,123 calls)

limits._spend_indexes (limits.py:135) calls reports.load over the whole span the windows cover, which on days=30 is 77,117 records built as full UsageRecord objects. Its docstring gives the reason: 'a 5-hour window is priced over hours, and a grouped row has folded the hour away.' That rules out load_grouped as it stands, but not a grouping at a finer grain (per minute, or per (model, hour)) that a SpendIndex could still answer a window from. Worth measuring before adding the cache, since a cache does not help the first reader.

Both /settings pages depend on ccreport-73kp and ccreport-5s96; if those land first, measure again before adding a cache here — 0.23s and 0.22s may not need one.

Note DETAIL_CACHE_MAX is 96 (dashboard.py:621) and the detail key space is one entry per (entity, range toggle) across model, project, machine, account, day, week and month. A new day arrives daily. Check whether real use evicts entries that are then paid for again at 5.36s each.
acceptance: A second load of each of the four routes is under 100ms while content_stamp has not moved. First load of /limits days=30 is under 1.0s.

title: Materialize the dedup winner as a column instead of re-deriving it per query
Index the newest-account-label lookup account_overview sorts a whole account for
description:
reports.account_overview (src/ccreport/server/reports.py:351) carries this correlated scalar subquery to find the newest label an account pushed:

    (SELECT r.account_label FROM server_records r
      WHERE r.account_uuid = a.account_uuid AND r.account_label IS NOT NULL
   ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)

EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN:

    CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY 1
      SEARCH r USING INDEX idx_srec_account_dk (account_uuid=?)
      USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY

idx_srec_account_dk is (account_uuid, dk) and does not carry ts or account_label, so each of the two accounts has ~400k rows read and sorted to produce one string.

Measured on the live database:

  account_overview whole query                      2.13s
  same query with the label subquery removed        1.41s
  the label subquery alone, over both accounts      0.79s
  SELECT DISTINCT account_uuid                      0.08s

Adding CREATE INDEX idx_srec_acct_ts ON server_records(account_uuid, ts DESC, account_label) turned the plan into 'SEARCH r USING COVERING INDEX idx_srec_acct_ts (account_uuid=?)' with no temp b-tree, and took account_overview from 1.59s to 0.86s on an ANALYZEd copy.

reports.account_names (reports.py:392) runs the same subquery over SELECT DISTINCT account_uuid and costs 0.86s on its own; it is called from dashboard's view constructor on every cold build, so the same index pays there too.

Weigh the write cost: the table already carries four indexes totalling 388 MB against 347 MB of data. A fifth adds to every ingest. Check whether idx_srec_ts (15 MB, on ts alone) still has a reader once this lands, and whether idx_srec_account_dk can be widened instead of a new index added.

Schema change goes through migrations.py: a numbered Step appended to MIGRATION_CHAIN in src/ccreport/server/db.py. An index is covered by the CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS script, but still needs Step(N, "name") with no callable to move the version that re-runs it.
acceptance: account_overview under 1.0s before ccreport-52h5's dedup work and under 0.3s after. account_names under 0.2s. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for both shows no USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY.

title: Dashboard server pages take 1-5s per cold load
A window page costs its first reader 2.25s, and the cache cannot help them
description:
The one page ccreport-52h5 did not fix. Measured live against https://ccreport.lan.rykroken.net on 2026-08-22, immediately after 59e72e1 was deployed to sea:

  /limits/week/1787068800?model=&account=personal   2.25s cold, 0.031s warm

Every other page in that epic is now 30-60ms cold or warm. This one is 2.25s for whoever loads it first after a push, and milliseconds for everyone after. `limits.cached_window` is doing its job; the cost is what it takes to build the view once.

## Where the time goes

`limits._spend_indexes` (src/ccreport/server/limits.py:135) calls `reports.load` over the whole span the listed windows cover and builds a full `UsageRecord` per row. cProfile of `limits.build(conn, 30)` before 59e72e1, 3.78s total:

  0.836s  sqlite3 Cursor.fetchall (7 calls)
  0.670s  reports.load          (reports.py:150)
  0.558s  windows.SpendIndex.__init__ (windows.py:345, 2 calls)
  0.404s  reports._as_merged    (77,117 calls)
  0.114s  pricing.model_family  (77,123 calls)

59e72e1 pushed the dedup into SQL, which took the 30-day load from 289,269 rows to 151,344 and `limits.build(conn, 30)` from 2.64s to 0.87s on a Mac (sea is roughly 2x slower, which is where the 2.25s comes from). The remaining cost is the surviving half still becoming Python objects.

## What has already been tried and rejected

Do not re-propose grouping the records coarsely. It was measured: bucketing by (model, minute) moved a window's spend by **9.7%**, and by five minutes by **37%**. A window's fill span can be minutes long, so one bucket is most of it, and `windows.SpendIndex` prices exactly that span. The rejection is recorded in `_spend_indexes`' docstring.

## Directions that have not been tried

- `_as_merged` builds the full MergedRecord shape — project_display, account_display, a TierTimeline lookup, a datetime. `SpendIndex` reads none of the identity fields. A narrower row type for this one caller may drop most of the 0.404s + 0.114s without touching the grain.
- `_spend_indexes` loads the span every listed window covers, then splits per account. On a 30-day toggle that is one span covering 89 window instances. Loading per window, or per account, may read far less.
- The two `SpendIndex.__init__` calls are 0.558s on their own; read `src/ccreport/windows.py:345` before assuming the cost is all in `load`.

Low priority: the page is one people linger on, and the second load is 31ms.
acceptance: /limits/{window}/{resets_at} answers in under 500ms cold on sea, measured with curl against the live server after a push. The spend, cache-hit and Extra figures on the page are unchanged to the cent from what it draws today.

Detail-page charts start at the range bound, not at the scope's first record
description:
https://ccreport.lan.rykroken.net/model/claude-sonnet-5?days=0 charts four series over the whole all-time range (Feb 2026 onward), but that model has no records before 2026-07-02. Four fifths of every chart is a flat zero line and the shape that matters is squeezed into the right edge.

The tile row already narrows: dashboard._active_span (src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py:301) clips the priced span to what the page's own records cover, for exactly this reason. The chart axis does not - dashboard.build's non-period branch sets axis = _day_axis(start, (end - start).days) from the toggle bounds (src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py:743).

Fix: on a scoped, non-period page, trim the day axis to the first and last day the filtered records carry. Trim on record.day_key(), not on the timestamp - day_key is the pushing machine's calendar day, so a timestamp-derived bound can drop a record off the axis (_day_position returns None). The index page (scope is None) and the three period scopes (day/week/month) keep the full axis: a period page IS its span.
acceptance:
- A scoped non-period detail page's chart_days start at the first day its own records cover and end at the last.
- The index page's axis and series are unchanged.
- day/week/month period pages still chart their whole period, empty days included.
- No record is dropped from a chart by the trim (every day_key in merged is on the axis).
- Test under tests/ covers the trim and the two exemptions.

Detail-page charts start at the range bound, not at the scope's first record
description:
https://ccreport.lan.rykroken.net/model/claude-sonnet-5?days=0 charts four series over the whole all-time range (Feb 2026 onward), but that model has no records before 2026-07-02. Four fifths of every chart is a flat zero line and the shape that matters is squeezed into the right edge.

The tile row already narrows: dashboard._active_span (src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py:301) clips the priced span to what the page's own records cover, for exactly this reason. The chart axis does not - dashboard.build's non-period branch sets axis = _day_axis(start, (end - start).days) from the toggle bounds (src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py:743).

Fix: on a scoped, non-period page, trim the day axis to the first and last day the filtered records carry. Trim on record.day_key(), not on the timestamp - day_key is the pushing machine's calendar day, so a timestamp-derived bound can drop a record off the axis (_day_position returns None). The index page (scope is None) and the three period scopes (day/week/month) keep the full axis: a period page IS its span.
acceptance:
- A scoped non-period detail page's chart_days start at the first day its own records cover and end at the last.
- The index page's axis and series are unchanged.
- day/week/month period pages still chart their whole period, empty days included.
- No record is dropped from a chart by the trim (every day_key in merged is on the axis).
- Test under tests/ covers the trim and the two exemptions.
notes:
Implemented: dashboard._covered_axis (src/ccreport/server/dashboard.py:388) cuts the day axis to the first and last day the scope's records carry, applied in build()'s non-period branch behind 'if scope is not None'. Cut on day_key, so no record falls off the axis.

Verified: just lint-all -> 'All checks passed!' + pyright '0 errors'. just test -> '2329 passed'. Six new tests in tests/test_dashboard.py::TestCoveredAxis cover the open day, the close day, no record dropped, density in the middle, the index page keeping 90 days, and a month page keeping its whole month.
